title: Does MS Dhoni Own a Stake in CSK? Here's What We Know
content:
The news surrounding the reported MS Dhoni CSK stake has sparked widespread discussion online. Fans want to know whether the former captain really asked Chennai Super Kings for a significant stake in the franchise.

However, a recent Cricbuzz report suggests Dhoni made no such demand. A senior CSK official denied the claims, saying, “MS has never asked us about it. We never discussed the matter. We also don’t have any information about him having discussed this with Mr N Srinivasan either.”

But that doesn’t mean Dhoni owns no part of CSK. According to the same report, the former CSK captain already holds more than one lakh shares in Chennai Super Kings Cricket Limited.

Does MS Dhoni Own CSK Shares?

The direct answer is yes. MS Dhoni reportedly owns more than one lakh shares in Chennai Super Kings Cricket Limited.

But how can Dhoni own CSK shares when the company has not gone public?

CSK is an unlisted company. That means its shares are not traded publicly on a stock exchange. However, investors can still acquire shares privately through off-market transactions. According to Cricbuzz, Dhoni acquired his shares when they became available for purchase.

Despite owning more than one lakh shares, Dhoni does not become one of the major owners of CSK. His holding represents only a tiny fraction of CSK’s overall share capital and does not give him significant control over the franchise.

How Much Stake Does MS Dhoni Own in CSK?

The reported number for Dhoni’s holding in the company stands at more than one lakh shares. In isolation, that number might seem enormous. But that is not the case when compared with CSK’s overall shareholding.

According to Cricbuzz, more than 30 crore outstanding shares are held by the public, accounting for close to 40% of the franchise’s total share capital. The Srinivasan family, meanwhile, holds a controlling stake of more than 55%.

This puts the MS Dhoni CSK stake into perspective. His one lakh-plus shares account for only a fraction of the overall equity and do not give him any significant control over the franchise.

Cricbuzz estimates that Dhoni’s holding could currently be worth around ₹2.6-3 crore, although this is an estimated valuation rather than a publicly traded market price.

CSK Deny Reports of Dhoni Seeking a Bigger Stake

This brings us back to the original question: did MS Dhoni really ask for a bigger stake in CSK?

According to the franchise, the answer is no. Earlier reports had claimed that Dhoni wanted to acquire a significant stake in CSK. However, the team management has now denied that any such discussions took place.

The CSK official also said the franchise had no information about Dhoni separately discussing the matter with N Srinivasan.

For now, claims that Dhoni sought a larger stake in CSK remain unsubstantiated.

MS Dhoni’s Influence at CSK

The fact that the management is waiting for Dhoni’s input on the head coach should be enough to show the influence he continues to hold at the franchise.

While there has been plenty of discussion around his future, Cricbuzz reports that CSK are waiting for Dhoni’s return before moving forward with the head-coach selection. The management is also expected to discuss transfers and trades after his return.

While CSK officials maintain that they are yet to identify Stephen Fleming’s successor, sources cited by Cricbuzz suggest the franchise has zeroed in on an overseas candidate who is also believed to be in talks with another team.

Dhoni may not control CSK through his shareholding, but he continues to have considerable influence over its cricketing decisions.

title: CSK First Captain: MS Dhoni’s Debut Season in 2008
content:
MS Dhoni was the first captain of CSK and led the team in the inaugural IPL season in 2008. Chennai Super Kings selected Dhoni as their marquee player at the inaugural IPL auction, where he became one of the league’s most remarkable signings. Under his leadership, CSK enjoyed a brilliant campaign in their first season, reaching the 2008 IPL final. 

CSK First Captain: Quick Facts

Who was the First Captain of CSK?

MS Dhoni was the first captain of CSK, leading the side from its season debut in the 2008 IPL. He was the franchise’s original full-time captain and has created a legacy by winning several titles, and taking the team to Playoffs in record 10 seasons.

How Did MS Dhoni Become CSK Captain in 2008?

MS Dhoni became the Chennai Super Kings captain in 2008 after the franchise signed him for US$1.5 million at the first-ever IPL auction. Unlike teams with designated icon players, CSK entered the auction without a pre-assigned local star and needed someone who could become the face of the franchise.

Dhoni’s journey into the team was not as straightforward as it may now seem. According to VB Chandrasekhar, CSK’s director of cricket operations, N Srinivasan initially preferred Virender Sehwag. Chandrasekhar instead argued for Dhoni, who offered leadership, wicketkeeping and the ability to change a match with the bat.

Srinivasan eventually agreed, and CSK bought Dhoni as the most expensive player at the inaugural auction. Following the auction, he was appointed captain for CSK’s debut IPL season, becoming the first player to lead the franchise.

Dhoni’s First Match as CSK Captain

MS Dhoni’s first match as CSK captain came against Kings XI Punjab on 19 April 2008 in the very first IPL season. In the team’s first-ever match, Dhoni led the side to a memorable victory. Opting to bat first, CSK posted a formidable score of 240/5 in 20 overs, thanks to Mike Hussey’s brilliant 116* off just 54 balls.

Kings XI Punjab responded strongly with the bat and kept themselves in the contest for much of the chase. Yet the CSK bowlers held their nerve during the finishing stages, restricting the opposition to 207/4 and securing a 33-run victory. Hence, Dhoni began his captaincy journey with CSK on a winning note. 

CSK’s IPL 2008 Record Under MS Dhoni 

MS Dhoni led CSK to an impressive first season in the 2008 Indian Premier League. CSK finished third in the league stage, winning 8 of their 14 games and earning 16 points. This brilliant performance secured their place in the knockout stage.

In the semi-final, CSK faced Kings XI Punjab again, where the latter batted first and posted 112 runs. CSK then chased down the target with ease, securing a nine-wicket victory and booking their spot in the inaugural IPL final. 

The final against Rajasthan Royals was a nail-biting contest. CSK batted first and posted 163/5 in 20 overs, setting RR a challenging target of 164. While defending the target, CSK performed well with the ball and maintained pressure on Rajasthan throughout the chase. They fought until the very end, taking the game down to the last delivery. 

Eventually, Rajasthan Royals achieved the target and won by three wickets, with CSK finishing as the runners-up of the 2008 IPL. Despite the loss, CSK’s fighting performance showed their competitiveness under Dhoni’s leadership. 

What Did Dhoni’s First Season Establish at CSK?

Dhoni’s first season as CSK captain showed that he could lead a dressing room filled with experienced international players. At 26, he was younger than several senior names in the squad, including Matthew Hayden, Michael Hussey, Stephen Fleming, Makhaya Ntini and Muttiah Muralitharan.

CSK also received contributions from across the squad during IPL 2008. Suresh Raina led their run-scoring with 421 runs, while Albie Morkel took 17 wickets. The team’s run to the final showed that CSK had found a captain capable of bringing different personalities and levels of experience together.

FAQs

MS Dhoni was the first captain of Chennai Super Kings (CSK) when the franchise made its debut in the very first IPL season in  2008. He led CSK to the final in their inaugural IPL season. 

  1. Why was MS Dhoni appointed as the CSK captain? 

MS Dhoni was appointed as the CSK captain in 2008 after the franchise signed him as their marquee player at the inaugural IPL auction for US$1.5 million. He was appointed captain because of the strong leadership qualities he had displayed during his stint with the Indian team.

CSK made its IPL debut during the inaugural season on April 19, 2008, against Kings XI Punjab. In its very first match, CSK secured a 33-run victory, starting its IPL journey on a winning note.

CSK finished as runners-up in IPL 2008. They reached the final in the inaugural season but lost to Rajasthan Royals by three wickets in a closely fought battle.

title: Prashant Veer’s Masterclass Powers NSK to a Thrilling Win Against KR in the Eliminator of UP T20 League
content:

Noida Super Kings Pull of Last-Ball Heist by 1 Run Over Kashi Rudras

Noida Super Kings edged Kashi Rudras by one run in a dramatic eliminator at Green Park, Kanpur, booking their spot in Qualifier 2. The thrilling victory came down to the final delivery, where Noida’s bowlers held their nerve under immense pressure to seal the win.

Opting to bowl first, Kashi’s bowlers pushed NSK under pressure, but Veer’s blistering knock of 58 runs from 28 balls, including a sensational 27-run final over off Rishabh Rajput, shifted the momentum and gave the side a competitive finish. Meanwhile, the lower order supported his charge as NSK reached 154/6 from 20 overs, setting up a challenging target of 155 for the opposition. The recovery from 82/6 made the CSK all-rounder’s intervention even more important in a tight game. Such intent restored belief and ensured the batting side finished strongly.

Coming in to bat second, KR lost wickets at crucial moments during the chase despite starting off their innings with an aggressive intent. That pressure eventually proved decisive, although Abhishek Goswami’s valuable 45 from 33 deliveries and Shubham Chaubey’s unbeaten 43 off 26 balls kept the contest alive. NSK’s strength lies in Veer’s presence, as he has amassed 227 runs in 11 games so far in the tournament, including three half-centuries, while also making valuable contributions with the ball by picking nine wickets. Experience in the IPL with Chennai Super Kings adds another layer of value, giving the all-rounder exposure to high-pressure contests. Moreover, his ability to deliver at crucial moments has repeatedly strengthened the side through decisive batting bursts and timely breakthroughs.

Under this momentum, Noida Super Kings will hope other team-mates can produce useful contributions and the team can manage pressure effectively. If those elements come together, the Super Kings will have a genuine opportunity to clinch the UP T20 League title this year.

title: Ruturaj Gaikwad Breaks Silence on CSK Planning to Appoint a New Head Coach
content:
Ruturaj Gaikwad has broken his silence on Chennai Super Kings’ plan to appoint a new head coach, with the next IPL edition and mini auction still lying ahead. Chennai’s decision on appointing a new coach has sparked curiosity among the supporters.

Meanwhile, Gaikwad’s comments have added intrigue. As CSK enters a transition stage, every decision could shape the franchise’s next chapter.

The Dawn of a New Era: CSK Begins the Quest for Fleming’s Successor

Stephen Fleming and CSK have mutually agreed to part ways, bringing an end to a remarkable 18-year coach-franchise partnership. The decision has left the cricketing world, particularly Chennai supporters, wondering who will guide the team next. Speculation has already spread, with cricketing legends such as Brendon McCullum, Mike Hussey and few other prominent names being discussed as possible successors.

Finally, Ruturaj Gaikwad told reporters that CSK will have a head coach, with no urgency needed to make the final decision, with plenty of time still remaining before the next IPL season and the mini-auction also yet to come. Selecting the right candidate, however, will require careful planning because the franchise must build a strong roadmap for the coming season. Leadership changes can influence strategy, player growth, and the team’s overall direction, making this an important decision for CSK. It is understood that rebuilding requires patience, clarity, teamwork, and trust from everyone involved throughout the process.

After being chosen as captain, Gaikwad accepted greater responsibility from MS Dhoni and stepped into a demanding role. Although Ruturaj stated that leading CSK was a major challenge, he also said that he had embraced the responsibility and continued to enjoy the experience. Supporters now await the franchise’s next move, while Gaikwad’s confidence suggests that the team is ready to face its transition with patience, preparation, and determination.

Ruturaj Gaikwad Urges Patience from Fans as CSK Navigates a New Transition

Gaikwad has demanded patience from the Chennai Super Kings fans as the franchise enters an important transition. Since the Indian Premier League began in 2008, the men in yellow have built an identity through consistency, strong leadership, and a winning culture. They have established themselves as one of the most successful teams in the tournament history.

Now, the team faces a period of change, and the skipper believes everything will eventually fall into place. Building a new chapter cannot happen overnight, especially when decisions remain before the next season. Fans, therefore, are being asked to trust the process and give the franchise time to settle its plans. The CSK skipper’s appeal reflects the calm approach needed during this phase, while his determination offers reassurance to the supporters. Even though the five-time-champions failed to produce the results as per expectations in their recent IPL campaign, they have repeatedly shown the ability to adapt and compete in this difficult phase. title: CSK News Today: End-of-Month Wrap
content:
Despite the IPL being in its off-season, CSK fans had an eventful August. Several major developments took place across different areas of the franchise.

From the coaching transition and Hardik Pandya trade rumours to fresh reports about MS Dhoni’s future with the franchise, there was plenty happening away from the field. Meanwhile, several CSK players continued to impress for their domestic and international teams.

With plenty to unpack, here’s a roundup of all the major CSK news from August.

CSK’s Head Coach Search Continues

Following Stephen Fleming’s departure, the CSK head coach position remains vacant. The Kiwi coach left in July and has since taken charge of the England Test side.

However, CSK are yet to name his replacement. Almost every week brings a new name into the fray, with the speculation initially starting around Michael Hussey potentially taking up the role.

While there has been little development on that front, pundits have added names such as Brendon McCullum and Eoin Morgan to the conversation, with Ravichandran Ashwin backing the latter.

Fans, on the other hand, continue to see MS Dhoni as the ideal candidate. But while they debate whether Dhoni should replace Fleming, an even bigger question surrounds his future at CSK.

What Is MS Dhoni’s Future With the Franchise?

This question has hounded CSK fans for months. After Dhoni didn’t feature in a single game during IPL 2026, everyone wants to know what his future with the franchise looks like.

Recent reports have claimed that Dhoni explored acquiring a significant stake in CSK. Some reports suggested that he wanted 25% equity, while the franchise was willing to offer a considerably smaller share, with figures of 3% and later 5.5% being reported.

However, neither Dhoni nor CSK have confirmed that such negotiations took place.

Meanwhile, RevSportz has reported that CSK want Dhoni to remain involved with the franchise and that he could potentially take up a mentoring role next season.

For now, his exact role remains unclear. But whether as a player, mentor or something bigger, speculation surrounding Dhoni’s long-term relationship with CSK is unlikely to disappear anytime soon.

Hardik Pandya Trade Rumours Continue

Apart from MS Dhoni’s future, another story that kept CSK fans occupied throughout August was the possibility of Hardik Pandya joining the franchise.

The Indian all-rounder has repeatedly been linked with CSK amid uncertainty surrounding his future at Mumbai Indians. However, acquiring Pandya could come at a significant cost if MI eventually decide to entertain a trade.

Shivam Dube and Ayush Mhatre are two names that have featured in hypothetical trade packages, with former CSK batter Subramaniam Badrinath suggesting that Mumbai should demand the duo in return for Pandya.

However, there is no confirmation that MI have formally demanded either player or that serious negotiations with CSK have begun.

For now, Hardik to CSK remains one of the biggest trade rumours rather than an imminent deal.

CSK Players Stay Busy Around the World

While most of the major CSK news came from developments off the field, several players also made their presence felt with bat and ball in August.

Dewald Brevis was the biggest standout. The South African smashed consecutive scores of 75 in the T20I tri-series in Namibia. After scoring 75 off 50 balls against the hosts, he followed it with an unbeaten 75 off just 32 deliveries against Zimbabwe, smashing seven fours and six sixes.

Back home, Anshul Kamboj showed that he can contribute with the bat as well. Playing for North Zone in the Duleep Trophy, the pacer smashed 60 off just 52 balls from No. 9, including five sixes. Ruturaj Gaikwad also returned to domestic action as West Zone captain and scored 66 in the tournament.

Meanwhile, Noor Ahmad enjoyed another successful stint in The Hundred. The Afghan spinner returned figures of 3/33 in the final, helping his side finish the tournament with the title.

With several CSK players finding form away from the IPL, Chennai will hope they carry the same momentum into the next season.

A Crucial Few Months Ahead for CSK

August perfectly summed up the transition CSK currently find themselves in. While questions remain over the new head coach, MS Dhoni’s future and possible trades, their players continue to deliver around the world. With retentions and the IPL 2027 mini-auction approaching, the next few months could shape Chennai’s new era.

title: MS Dhoni's Bond with CSK under Strain
content:
Chennai Super Kings face fresh uncertainty as reports suggest that management has rejected MS Dhoni’s proposal to buy a stake in the franchise.

Behind the disagreement, negotiations over ownership have reportedly created tension, raising questions about whether the strong partnership between the franchise and its iconic player can remain unchanged or not.

Dhoni’s Negotiations with CSK Didn’t Go Well for the Franchise Legend

Initially, MS Dhoni reportedly sought a 25 percent stake in Chennai Super Kings, hoping to invest his own money and become a meaningful stakeholder in the franchise. However, the owners allegedly declined the proposal and offered only 3 percentage, creating a wide gap between both sides. Subsequently, the former CSK skipper is said to have reduced his demand to 18 percentage after further discussions, showing readiness to compromise during the negotiations.

Nevertheless, the management reportedly increased its offer to just 5.5 percent, which still failed to match the cricketer’s expectations. Importantly, the former captain was not asking for a free share; instead, he reportedly wanted to purchase a stake and invest in the team he has represented for nearly two decades. Therefore, the disagreement was not simply about receiving ownership, but about the size and value of his proposed investment.

Ultimately, negotiations appear to have ended without an agreement that satisfied both parties. Although neither side’s position has been independently confirmed in the information provided, the reported difference between the offers highlights how difficult the discussions became. Consequently, the failed bargaining has fuelled speculation about the future of Dhoni’s association with the franchise and whether a revised proposal could bring both parties back to the negotiating table.

Could Dhoni’s Partnership with CSK come to an End?

Meanwhile, the unsuccessful negotiations over Dhoni acquiring a stake have reportedly placed his relationship with CSK under strain. Speculation has therefore grown that the two sides could eventually end the partnership. Recently, the ex-Indian skipper did not play in IPL 2026, where CSK finished eighth in the points table, due to injury. Despite failing to qualify to the play-offs, the side discovered effective combinations and built a winning run before recurring injuries disrupted momentum, adding another important layer to the former captain’s chances of parting ways with the team.

Historically, Dhoni has been the key figure to Chennai Super Kings’ success, guiding the side to five IPL glories and also remaining the team’s leading run-scorer with 4,699 runs. Should the stake dispute remain unresolved and the partnership end, many fans and teammates could be disappointed. Undoubtedly, his leadership, accomplishments, and the lasting respect he earned within the franchise have made any possibility of separation an emotional prospect for the Chennai Super Kings community.

title: CSK Coaching Staff 2027
content:
For the first time in nearly two decades, CSK are searching for a new head coach. Stephen Fleming’s departure has left a massive void at the top of Chennai’s coaching structure.

However, the uncertainty may not end with Fleming. Reports suggest batting coach Michael Hussey could also pursue opportunities elsewhere, potentially leaving CSK with another important position to fill.

With that in mind, let’s take a look at the current CSK coaching staff and understand the roles they play.

CSK Coaching Staff List

CSK Face Major Changes After Stephen Fleming’s Exit

Fleming’s association with CSK began as a player in 2008 before he took over as head coach in 2009. He went on to oversee the franchise’s most successful era, winning five IPL titles and two Champions League T20 trophies.

He managed the side for over 18 years, across 3 teams, and won them 7 major trophies. His departure followed a difficult period for CSK, with the franchise failing to add another title after IPL 2023.

Fleming’s successor could bring members of his own staff, but retaining experienced coaches already familiar with CSK would also provide much-needed continuity during the transition.

But what roles do the other CSK coaches play?

Eric Simons and Sriram Provide Continuity

Let’s understand why even without Fleming, the coaching staff is important. Firstly they provide a sense of continuity to the team’s coaching philosophy.

Starting with Eric Simon who is the bowling consultant for pacers mostly, we have a man who has studied the Indian conditions for years, and worked with some of the best in business. From Bravo to Mark Wood, and Pathirana, he has seen the rise of young bowlers as well as guided the older generation in Ashish Nehra.

Sridharan Sriram on the other hand might be a recent edition. But has the world of knowledge, especially when it comes to spin bowling. Before assuming the CSK role, he was with the Bangladesh’s national team. And on this team, he has worked closely with the likes of Noor and Hosein. The results of that association speak for themselves.

Rajiv Kumar and James Foster Complete the Coaching Core

Rajiv Kumar provides another layer of continuity within the CSK coaching staff. As assistant batting coach, he works alongside the batting unit and already understands the methods and expectations built during Fleming’s tenure. That familiarity could prove valuable when a new head coach arrives with different ideas.

James Foster, meanwhile, handles the fielding department. The former England wicketkeeper brings extensive coaching experience from franchise cricket and adds another specialist voice to an already experienced backroom team.

The Team Behind the CSK Coaches

The support structure goes much deeper than the coaches seen in the dugout. Taifun Simsek oversees physiotherapy, while Gregory King handles strength and conditioning. Dr Madhu Thottappillil serves as team doctor, with David Reid working as the team’s psychologist.

Russell Radhakrishnan and Sanjay Natarajan also handle team management and logistics respectively, completing a support system that operates behind the scenes throughout the IPL season.

Will CSK Completely Rebuild Their Coaching Staff?

That now becomes the bigger question. Fleming is gone, while Hussey’s future remains uncertain. But CSK do not necessarily need to dismantle everything they built under their former head coach.

Keeping experienced figures like Simons, Sriram, Rajiv and Foster would provide continuity while allowing Fleming’s successor to introduce his own ideas. For a franchise entering its biggest coaching transition in years, that balance could prove crucial.

title: Noor Ahmad and Leus du Plooy Shine as MSG Clinch The Hundred Title
content:
Super Kings stars Noor Ahmad and Leus du Plooy stole the spotlight as MSG beat Trent Rockets in a nail-biting The Hundred final, sealing a memorable five-wicket win at Lord’s.

The young bowler’s clever spin and the JSK batter’s composed finishing powered their side to a thrilling victory, sealing the Super Giants’ first Hundred crown in a stylish fashion. Their standout performances showcased exceptional skill, fighting spirit, and big-match temperament, playing a decisive role in a landmark victory and underlining their ability to deliver when the stakes were highest.

Manchester Super Giants Beat Trent Rockets in a Thrilling Chase

Trent Rockets, batting first, posted a competitive total of 158/8 from their alloted 100 balls, with Aneurin Donald top-scoring for his team with a blistering 38 off 19 deliveries. Noor Ahmad produced the standout bowling performance for MSG, claiming an impressive 3 for 33 from his 20 balls, with his wickets including the dangerous trio of Ben Duckett, Finn Allen and Tim David. The CSK spinner’s magical spell helped his team restrict the opponents from posting a mammoth total.

Coming to bat second, Manchester started their chase aggressively, with Tim Seifert taking charge of the the attack and smashing an outstanding 72 off 38 deliveries to build a strong foundation. However, after Seifert’s dismissal, the chasing side briefly struggled to maintain the same momentum as TRE fought back with crucial breakthroughs. With wickets continuing to fall and the pressure mounting, Leus du Plooy showed remarkable composure in the closing stages. His valuable unbeaten knock of 27 from 18 deliveries, followed by a winning six from Liam Dawson, helped Manchester Super Giants reach the target with 5 wickets in hand and two balls to spare.

Ultimately, the result reflected a disciplined chase from the winning side, who absorbed pressure, recovered from setbacks, and maintained control when the finish became tense. Although the Rockets’ bowlers created openings, MSG held the nerves and found enough runs to complete the pursuit before the final delivery was required.

Manchester Super Giants Clinch Their First Hundred Championship

Manchester secured their maiden Hundred title under captain Jos Buttler, completing a campaign with a five-wicket triumph over TRE at Lord’s. Ahmad played a crucial role with the ball, using his variations to remove three dangerous batters and disrupt the opposition’s momentum at key moments, while Leus showed composure when the chase entered its decisive phase, ensuring the champions finished the job after the settled Tim was dismissed.

Throughout the tournament, the champions received contributions across departments, with their batting unit, pacers, and spin bowlers stepping up in different situations. Together, those performances created the consistency needed to reach the final and clinch the title in a stylish fashion. Importantly, the achievement marked not only the team’s maiden Hundred championship but also the first title for the Super Giants family in a franchise league, adding another milestone to their history.

From the head coach search to Dhoni and Hardik, here’s everything that made headlines in CSK news this week.

CSK Head Coach Search Continues

Ever since Stephen Fleming stepped down in July, CSK have been searching for a new head coach. For former players and pundits, this has also become an opportunity to suggest names who could replace the Kiwi.

The latest additions to that conversation are former England captain Eoin Morgan and current England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum.

Ravichandran Ashwin, who has remained vocal about developments surrounding CSK, recently touted Morgan as a potential candidate. He claimed that the World Cup-winning captain’s name was “doing the rounds strongly” for the vacant position.

However, there has been no confirmation from CSK that Morgan is an official candidate.

What appears more likely is that Chennai could once again turn towards an overseas coach. CSK CEO Kasi Viswanathan has indicated that the franchise is likely to appoint an overseas expert, with the management expected to finalise its decision after considering the available candidates.

McCullum’s name has also featured in recent reports, making the CSK head coach search one of the biggest stories to follow ahead of IPL 2027.

MS Dhoni Spotted in Chennai

After missing the entire IPL 2026 season, MS Dhoni was spotted in Chennai last week. Naturally, his return raised questions about what had brought him back to the city.

Dhoni has not played for CSK since being ruled out of last season due to injury, leading to plenty of speculation over whether he will return for another IPL campaign.

However, his appearance at CSK’s fitness camp suggests he remains involved with the franchise. The camp was reportedly organised to assess players before Chennai make their retention and release decisions ahead of IPL 2027.

While Dhoni’s fitness assessment has not been made public, his presence will inevitably raise hopes of another IPL comeback.

His visit also comes at an interesting time, with CSK currently searching for Stephen Fleming’s replacement. CEO Kasi Viswanathan has indicated that Dhoni will be involved in the process of selecting the franchise’s next head coach.

Michael Hussey’s CSK Future Remains Uncertain

Another name to keep an eye on is Michael Hussey. The CSK batting coach was initially seen as one of the most natural candidates to replace Stephen Fleming, given his long association with the franchise.

However, his own future at Chennai has now become a talking point. Fleming reportedly wants Hussey to join his England Test coaching setup, which could potentially take another familiar face away from CSK. Hussey has also publicly praised Fleming following his England appointment, although there is no confirmation that he plans to leave Chennai.

For now, his future remains uncertain. But with CSK searching for a new head coach and Fleming reportedly interested in taking Hussey with him, the coming weeks could bring further changes to Chennai’s coaching staff.

A Crucial Few Weeks Await CSK

From finding Fleming’s successor to deciding Dhoni’s future and dealing with trade rumours, CSK have several major decisions ahead. What happens over the next few weeks could shape not only their IPL 2027 squad, but also the beginning of a completely new era in Chennai.

title: CSK News Today: Weekly Update
content:
Dale Steyn Opens Door to CSK Head Coach Role Ahead of IPL 2027

As CSK’s search for a new head coach intensifies, another candidate has opened the door to the job. And it is none other than legendary South African pacer Dale Steyn.

In a recent interaction on X, Steyn was asked whether he would be interested in becoming the next CSK head coach. Steyn replied with: Yes Possibly.

His response was short, but it was enough to become one of the biggest pieces of CSK news surrounding the head coach search.

There is no indication yet that Chennai Super Kings have approached Steyn for the position. However, with the franchise searching for Stephen Fleming’s replacement, the former South African pacer’s interest adds another intriguing name to the conversation.

Dale Steyn’s IPL Coaching Experience

Steyn would not be entering unfamiliar territory if CSK decided to consider him for a coaching role.

The former RCB and SRH pacer served as Sunrisers Hyderabad’s pace-bowling coach after retiring from professional cricket. His stint gave him first-hand experience of working with an IPL dressing room and developing young fast bowlers.

One of the biggest names he worked with was Umran Malik, who emerged as one of India’s fastest bowlers and regularly crossed the 150 kmph mark during his breakthrough period.

Beyond the IPL, Steyn has continued to build his coaching experience through franchise cricket. However, taking charge of an entire IPL team would represent a significant step up from working primarily with fast bowlers.

Dale Steyn Has Always Wanted to Join CSK

If CSK ever make an offer, Steyn’s previous comments suggest he would certainly have something to think about.

The latest CSK news surrounding Steyn becomes even more interesting given his long-standing admiration for MS Dhoni. In a previous interview, Steyn revealed that there was a part of him that hoped Chennai would sign him during his playing career.

He was even willing to accept a reduced role simply to experience the franchise from within. Steyn has also spoken about his fascination with Dhoni’s captaincy and his desire to learn from one of the IPL’s most successful leaders.

That admiration becomes particularly interesting now, with Steyn himself looking to grow as a coach.

Would Dale Steyn Be a Good Fit for CSK?

Steyn certainly has qualities that could benefit Chennai. He understands the IPL, has worked with young fast bowlers and could bring fresh ideas to a CSK side entering a new era.

His biggest strength, however, could also expose his biggest weakness. Most of Steyn’s coaching experience has centred around fast bowling rather than managing an entire franchise.

Replacing Fleming requires someone capable of handling tactics, player management, auctions and overall squad planning. Steyn has yet to prove himself in such a role.

For now, Steyn remains an intriguing name in the latest CSK news surrounding Fleming’s replacement, rather than an obvious front-runner for the job

title: CSK Retained Players 2027: Who Could Chennai Super Kings Keep?
content:
Chennai Super Kings could face some difficult calls before submitting their IPL 2027 retention list. With CSK once again involved in some high-profile trade rumours, it becomes even more important to understand which players they might retain and who could eventually be allowed to leave.

While there are some obvious CSK retentions, several names might not make the final cut because of factors such as squad balance, form and auction purse.

With the mini-auction approaching, let’s take a look at the players CSK are most likely to retain.

CSK’s Indian Core

If there is one area CSK would not want to disturb, it is their Indian core. Sanju Samson, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Ayush Mhatre, Shivam Dube and Anshul Kamboj all have strong cases to stay.

Barring Gaikwad and Dube, each of these players enjoyed an impressive season. Samson finished as CSK’s leading run-scorer, while Kamboj led their bowling attack with 21 wickets. Mhatre also made an immediate impact, scoring 201 runs at a strike rate of 177.88 before injury cut his campaign short.

But these players offer more than numbers. Samson and Gaikwad give CSK two established Indian top-order batters and leadership options. Mhatre represents the future, while Kamboj provides something every IPL team values: a reliable Indian pacer.

More was expected from Gaikwad and Dube last season. However, both have done enough in the past to retain their places. Dube, in particular, continues to offer a specific middle-order role as a powerful spin-hitter that CSK would find difficult to replace with another Indian batter.

Brevis, Overton and Noor Lead Overseas Retentions

Jamie Overton should have one of the strongest cases among CSK’s overseas players.

The England all-rounder took 14 wickets while also scoring 136 runs at a strike rate of 158.14. His ability to bowl important overs and provide late-order power gives CSK valuable balance without requiring two separate overseas players for those roles.

Noor Ahmad should also remain part of Chennai’s plans. His 2026 campaign did not quite match his 24-wicket season in 2025, but a young wrist-spinner who already understands the conditions at Chepauk remains a valuable long-term asset.

Then comes Dewald Brevis. The South African had a quiet IPL 2026, scoring 151 runs at a strike rate of 127.97. But at just 23, releasing him after one poor campaign would mean giving up on a potential long-term middle-order option just when CSK are trying to build their next core.

What Happens to MS Dhoni?

This has to be the biggest question surrounding the CSK retained players 2027 announcement. For almost two decades, CSK have been synonymous with MS Dhoni. But IPL 2026 felt different.

Dhoni did not feature in a single match after suffering a calf injury before the tournament. Although there were hopes of a comeback, fitness concerns kept him on the sidelines throughout the campaign.

Hence, the question is looming large: has MS Dhoni finally moved on?

It is hardly about whether CSK want to retain him. The bigger question is whether Dhoni wants to play another IPL season. The answer should become clearer once Chennai announce their final retention list.

What Could the Retentions Mean for CSK’s Auction?

Keeping this core would mean CSK do not need another complete rebuild at the IPL 2027 mini-auction. Instead, the franchise could focus on releasing expensive or peripheral players, recovering auction purse and filling specific gaps in the squad.

With Chennai also featuring heavily in trade rumours, their final retention list could provide the first real indication of just how aggressive they plan to be before IPL 2027.

title: Eoin Morgan as CSK Coach: Why He Makes Sense
content:
Eoin Morgan Makes Sense as CSK’s Next Head Coach, even if the move would come with one major risk. The former England captain brings extensive T20 experience, an IPL final on his résumé and a proven record of leading teams through major changes.

Morgan has also developed a reputation for aggressive, data-driven white-ball cricket, which could offer CSK a fresh approach. The obvious concern is his lack of professional coaching experience.

Let’s explore his acumen in detail to understand how fit is Morgan as next CSK Head Coach.

Proven Leadership in High-pressure Cricket

Morgan’s leadership record is perhaps the strongest argument for why he could fit into CSK’s setup.

Morgan’s numbers underline his ability to lead at the highest level, but his biggest strength may lie in what he did with England. He led them to the 2016 T20 World Cup final before overseeing their transformation into a white-ball powerhouse, culminating in their maiden ODI World Cup triumph in 2019. Morgan knows what it takes to take a team through a transition and turn it into a genuine world-beating side. And if there is one thing CSK needs right now, it is exactly that. If anyone understands how to navigate a transition, it is Morgan.

Extensive T20 and Franchise Experience

Morgan’s T20 experience is another major advantage. He has played 374 T20 matches and scored 7,780 runs, featuring across leagues including the IPL, Vitality Blast, PSL, BBL and CPL. In the IPL alone, he has 83 appearances and 1,405 runs, giving him first-hand experience of the league’s unique pressures and demands.

He also led KKR in 24 matches, winning 11, after taking over from Dinesh Karthik midway through the 2020 season. More importantly, he guided KKR to the IPL 2021 final, showing that he can make an immediate impact when entrusted with leadership. Having a coach who has actually experienced the IPL dressing room, pressure and intensity from the inside could be invaluable.

That experience also strengthens the case for Morgan as CSK coach, particularly because he already understands the IPL environment from inside the dressing room.

Modern Tactical Approach

Morgan was ahead of his time when it came to white-ball cricket. He transformed England from a traditionally conservative side into an aggressive, fearless team, introducing clear roles and repeatable patterns that remain part of their white-ball blueprint today. After the disastrous 2015 World Cup exit, Morgan rebuilt the side around aggressive batting, a deep lineup and multiple all-rounders. 

He backed Ben Stokes after the disappointment of 2016 and gave Jason Roy and Jonny Bairstow clear roles to attack from the top. Rather than relying on instinct, Morgan established patterns and formulas that allowed England to play with freedom while knowing exactly what was expected of them. He was essentially building the modern template for England’s white-ball cricket nearly a decade ago. His aggressive white-ball philosophy could also shape what Morgan as CSK coach might bring to the franchise.

Experience Managing Elite Players

A good leader needs more than tactical knowledge; they need to understand people. Morgan demonstrated that during England’s 2019 World Cup-winning campaign, managing players from different backgrounds, personalities and roles while keeping the group aligned towards one goal. His experience extends far beyond international cricket too. Having played 374 T20 matches across major leagues and countries, his passport has barely had time to rest. 

From the IPL to the Vitality Blast, PSL, BBL and CPL, Morgan has shared dressing rooms with elite players across cricketing cultures and environments. That breadth of experience gives him an instinct for managing high-level players, while his own achievements ensure that he commands respect when he walks into a dressing room.

The Biggest Concern: Limited Coaching Experience

For all Morgan’s credentials, there is one glaring question mark: he has never formally coached a professional team. That makes replacing Stephen Fleming, who has been CSK’s head coach since 2009, an enormous challenge. There is also the question of how Morgan would operate alongside MS Dhoni, should Dhoni continue to have a significant say in the team’s affairs. Would Morgan be comfortable working within that dynamic while still establishing his own authority? 

His only formal coaching credential is an ECB-accredited Level Two coaching qualification, which he earned through a PCA/ECB course in 2015. Morgan has the leadership résumé, but whether that can translate into coaching remains an unanswered question.

Final Verdict

So, is Eoin Morgan the right fit for CSK? Why not? His lack of coaching experience makes the appointment a gamble, but the pool of candidates who combine elite leadership, extensive T20 experience and a proven record of rebuilding a team is not exactly overflowing. 

While, whether Eoin Morgan ultimately becomes CSK’s next coach remains uncertain, other experienced options should certainly be explored. But Morgan has arguably the most compelling overall profile. He may not be the safest option, but given what CSK needs right now, he could well be the best one.

title: CSK IPL 2027 Trade Rumours — Every Update So Far
content:
As the retention deadline gets closer, CSK trade news and rumours are beginning to blow like wild winds.

Ever since Chennai Super Kings pulled off the blockbuster Sanju Samson trade involving Ravindra Jadeja and Sam Curran, there has been a feeling that the franchise could remain aggressive in the trade market.

As a result, big names like Hardik Pandya, Ashutosh Sharma and Washington Sundar continue to be linked with the five-time champions. But is there really any truth behind the latest CSK trade rumours? Let’s take a closer look.

CSK Might Land Hardik Pandya

The biggest name currently dominating the conversation is Hardik Pandya.

Reports surrounding Pandya’s future at Mumbai Indians have sparked speculation over another potential blockbuster trade. CSK are among the franchises being linked with the Indian all-rounder, although no agreement between Chennai and Mumbai has been confirmed.

Pandya himself is no stranger to major IPL trades. Mumbai brought him back from Gujarat Titans ahead of IPL 2024 before immediately handing him the captaincy.

Now, uncertainty surrounding his future has once again put him at the centre of the trade market. Recent reports suggest multiple franchises are monitoring the situation, with CSK and Kolkata Knight Riders among the teams linked with him.

However, Mumbai Indians are yet to make a final decision on whether they are even willing to trade Pandya. That makes any potential move to Chennai far from straightforward.

Could Ayush Mhatre and Shivam Dube Be Involved?

This is where the story becomes particularly interesting for CSK fans.

Former Chennai Super Kings batter Subramaniam Badrinath suggested that Mumbai Indians should demand Ayush Mhatre and Shivam Dube if CSK seriously want Pandya. That would be an enormous price.

Dube has established himself as an important part of Chennai’s middle order, while Mhatre represents one of the franchise’s brightest long-term prospects. Giving up both players for one all-rounder, even one of Pandya’s quality, would therefore represent a major gamble.

However, it is important to separate suggestion from actual negotiation. There is currently no confirmation that Mumbai Indians have formally demanded Mhatre and Dube from CSK.

Will CSK Actually Trade for Hardik Pandya?

That remains the biggest question.

From a cricketing perspective, Pandya would solve several problems. He provides power in the middle order, gives CSK another Indian pace-bowling option and brings significant leadership experience.

But acquiring him could come at a huge cost.

Recent reports also suggest CSK’s immediate priority is finalising its new head coach following Stephen Fleming’s departure. That decision could influence how aggressively the franchise approaches the trade market.

For now, Hardik remains the biggest name associated with CSK trade news, but a deal is far from certain. Until Mumbai decide whether they are willing to let him leave, everything surrounding a move to Chennai should be treated as speculation rather than an imminent trade.

Other CSK Trade Rumours That Never Materialised

Hardik Pandya is hardly the first big name to be linked with Chennai Super Kings. Over the past few months, players such as Washington Sundar and Ashutosh Sharma have also featured in CSK trade rumours, with fans discussing how both could fit into the franchise’s plans.

However, those links never developed into anything concrete. There has been no confirmed trade agreement involving either player, highlighting how quickly speculation can grow around CSK during the IPL trade window.

The Sanju Samson deal only added fuel to that trend. After CSK showed their willingness to make a blockbuster move, almost every unsettled Indian player became a potential target. For now, Hardik remains the most prominent name in the conversation, but even that potential trade is still far from confirmed.

title: CSK News Today: Latest Chennai Super Kings Updates
content:
It has been another eventful week for Chennai Super Kings. The franchise continues to deal with the fallout of Stephen Fleming’s departure, while the search for the man who will replace one of the most successful coaches in IPL history gathers momentum.

From Michael Hussey’s uncertain future to the growing debate around MS Dhoni’s role in CSK’s next chapter, here are the biggest Chennai Super Kings news stories from the past week.

CSK’s Search for Stephen Fleming’s Replacement Continues

Finding Fleming’s replacement remains the biggest challenge facing CSK.

The former New Zealand captain ended his long association with Chennai last month before moving towards a new challenge with England’s Test team. His departure leaves CSK searching for a new head coach after an era defined by stability and five IPL titles.

That makes the next appointment particularly important. CSK are not simply replacing a coach. They must find someone capable of taking the franchise into a new era without completely dismantling the culture Fleming helped create.

Michael Hussey’s Future Takes Another Twist

Michael Hussey remains one of the most interesting names surrounding CSK’s coaching situation.

The Australian has spent years inside the franchise as both a player and batting coach. That familiarity makes him a logical option if Chennai decide to promote from within.

However, a fresh development has complicated matters.

Fleming reportedly wants Hussey to join his England Test setup as batting coach. Hussey has already worked with England as a consultant during their victorious 2022 T20 World Cup campaign, while his long relationship with Fleming makes a reunion understandable.

For CSK, that creates an intriguing situation. One of their most natural internal options could potentially follow Fleming out of Chennai.

Could MS Dhoni Play a Bigger Role at CSK?

And then there is MS Dhoni.

His playing future remains uncertain after he failed to feature in IPL 2026 because of injury. However, his influence within CSK has hardly disappeared. Fleming highlighted Dhoni’s importance in mentoring younger players during the season, while bowling coach Eric Simons said the decision over his playing future ultimately rests with Dhoni himself.

That naturally raises another question: could Dhoni eventually take on a formal role within the CSK setup?

There is no confirmation that Dhoni wants to become a head coach, and speculation should remain just that. Yet few people understand CSK’s philosophy better than the man who helped build it alongside Fleming.

Ajinkya Rahane Highlights the CSK Effect

Another reminder of CSK’s long-established culture came from Ajinkya Rahane this week.

Rahane reflected on how his time with Chennai transformed his approach to T20 batting. The franchise gave him greater freedom to play aggressively rather than restricting him to the anchor role that had defined much of his IPL career.

His comments are particularly relevant now. Fleming may be gone, but the environment he helped create remains one of CSK’s greatest assets.

A Defining Period for Chennai Super Kings

The biggest Chennai Super Kings news this week ultimately revolves around one theme: what comes next?

Fleming has left. Hussey’s future has another layer of uncertainty. Dhoni’s next move remains unknown.

For a franchise built on stability, CSK suddenly face several major decisions. How they handle them could determine whether Fleming’s departure marks the end of their golden era or simply the beginning of another one.

title: CSK set to Appoint an Overseas Legend as their New Head Coach
content:
Following the recent exit of CSK’s former head coach, Stephen Fleming, the franchise is preparing for a potential coaching change, with an overseas legend emerging as one of the top candidates for the role. The move could signal a fresh tactical direction for the franchise.

However, CSK CEO Kasi Vishwanathan has clarified that no final confirmation has been made yet, with several candidates currently under discussion before the management finalizes its decision.

Possible Contenders for the CSK Head Coach Role

Brendon Mccullum

Brendon McCullum stands out as one candidate, who could lead with an aggressive mindset and tactical ideas. His approach could encourage Chennai Super Kings to refresh their methods while retaining the discipline that has defined the franchise. Moreover, McCullum’s international coaching experience with the England cricket team would help him manage a squad containing different personalities and styles. Brendon’s experience with CSK as a former player gives him an added benefit of possessing an in-depth knowledge about the franchise culture.

Mike Hussey

Mike Hussey is another compelling option because of his deep connection with CSK and his understanding of the franchise’s environment. Since the Australian legend has been a part of the squad both as a player and coaching staff in the previous years, he knows the demands of the team and the local pitch conditions very well. Calm leadership, batting knowledge, and familiarity with Chennai could provide continuity during the transition phase.

Albie Morkel

Albie Morkel also deserves a serious attention because he combines all-round cricketing experience with a history at CSK. Morkel’s connection with sister franchise Joburg Super Kings could further boost his credentials. He was previously part of JSK’s coaching setup, giving him familiarity with the Super Kings group and its working methods. With the former South-African all-rounder now appointed as the head coach of JSK ahead of the upcoming SA20 season, his growing coaching experience within the Super Kings ecosystem could strengthen his chances if Chennai is looking for someone who already understands the franchise’s expectations.

Why Chennai Super Kings Eye Foreign Options?

Strategically, CSK’s interest in overseas options makes sense because modern T20 cricket increasingly depends on ideas gathered from different leagues, countries, and playing conditions. Fresh international perspectives can challenge familiar routines, sharpen strategic planning, and help a franchise adapt faster to evolving trends. Equally important, a foreign coach may offer experience from environments where innovative T20 methods have developed rapidly.

CSK and Overseas Stars: A Strong Connection in IPL History

Historically, CSK have shared a strong connection with foreign stars, giving the franchise a pool of coaching figures. Legends and popular names such as Brendon McCullum, Mike Hussey, Albie Morkel, and many other foreign players have contributed to the Super Kings’ success story across different eras of IPL. Consequently, the management could aim any former overseas player of Chennai Super Kings for the head coach role, considering their past contributions to the team and knowledge of the dressing room culture. Finally, an appointment would strengthen the link between CSK’s past successes and future plans for the franchise’s next era while adding a global dimension to the team’s coaching philosophy.

title: Sarfaraz Khan Picked in the Indian Test Squad for the Upcoming Sri-Lankan Tour
content:
Sarfaraz Khan has been named in the Indian Test squad for the two-match series against Sri-Lanka, with the right-hander returning to the side nearly two years after his last appearance, replacing the injured Sai Sudharsan.

The right-hander’s return comes after a consistent run of performances at domestic level, where he once again showcased his hunger for scoring runs. This recall gives him another chance to revive his international career on an important overseas assignment for India again.

Sarfaraz’s Consistent Domestic Performances Earn him a Place in the Indian Test Side Nearly After Two Long Years

After a long wait, Sarfaraz has earned another chance to represent India in Test cricket, having last appeared in November 2024 against New Zealand. Having played only six matches, he has accumulated 371 runs in 11 innings. Despite producing an overall average run, he has delivered some impactful knocks, with one of his most memorable efforts coming against New Zealand with a magnificent 150, an innings that helped the team avoid a major collapse. That knock remains a reminder of the batting quality he can bring when given responsibility.

Recent domestic performances have strengthened the CSK batter’s case for another opportunity at the highest level. During the latest Ranji Trophy campaign for Mumbai, he amassed 429 runs in seven games, including a top score of 229. Months ago, he also impressed in the Mumbai T20 League for Akash Tigers, producing the joint-fastest half-century of the tournament. Consistent contributions across formats have kept his name firmly in contention and ultimately helped him earn a recall to the national side.

Khan’s consistent performances have provided a timely platform for rebuilding confidence after a lengthy absence of nearly two years from the Indian set-up. The sustained run of form has made his selection a timely and deserved opportunity at this stage. A crucial opportunity stands in his way as he looks to regain his place and establish himself as a dependable option in India’s Test set-up.

Sarfaraz Faces a Challenging Assignment Ahead of the Sri Lanka Tour

More importantly, Khan now faces a tough challenge that could define his next chapter with the Indian team. Until now, his international experience has come entirely in home conditions, making the Sri Lankan tour his first overseas assignment. Such a change will test his technique, temperament and ability to adapt, particularly because Sri-Lankan pitches favor the bowlers and demand patience from the batters.

Success on this tour could significantly improve the Chennai Super Kings star’s prospects in the Indian Test setup. Performing consistently away from home would demonstrate that his batting can withstand different conditions and strengthen the selectors’ confidence in him. A productive series could therefore open the door for more opportunities and establish him as a regular option in India’s Test middle-order. For Sarfaraz, this recall is not merely a return to the squad; it is a chance to prove his run-scoring ability across conditions, further highlighting his talent.

title: MS Dhoni's New CSK Role for IPL 2027 — What We Know
content:
Stephen Fleming’s departure has left Chennai Super Kings with more questions than answers. After a dismal campaign, sections of the fanbase and several pundits called for changes to the coaching setup. Now, the biggest change has arrived.

But that leads to a much bigger question: who leads CSK into the future?

Replacing Fleming will be no easy task. He spent 18 years building one of the most successful teams in IPL history and became synonymous with the franchise. Several names could emerge as possible successors, but few can match his understanding of the CSK system.

Unless, of course, the franchise turns to someone who helped build that system alongside him.

Someone who hasn’t even officially retired from the IPL yet.

Yes, we are talking about MS Dhoni.

Why MS Dhoni Makes Sense as CSK Head Coach

Much of what CSK have achieved in their nearly two-decade-long history stems from the partnership between MS Dhoni and Stephen Fleming.

Fleming shaped the team from the dugout. Dhoni led it on the field. Together, they built one of the most successful franchises in cricket.

That is why Dhoni taking over as head coach feels like a natural progression. He understands how CSK operate because he helped establish many of the principles on which the franchise still stands today.

More importantly, Dhoni knows how to turn those principles into results. He has already led players through pressure situations, defined roles and extracted performances from unlikely match-winners.

If Dhoni takes over, it would feel less like a transition and more like an evolution.

Dhoni Has Already Been a Coach on the Field

Everyone knows the master tactician that MS Dhoni is. He has long been regarded as one of the sharpest cricketing minds of his generation.

As captain, Dhoni built his reputation on reading batters and reacting before they could take control. From identifying weaknesses to setting unconventional fields and knowing exactly when to turn to a particular bowler, he often changed games through decisions alone.

His reading of conditions was equally impressive. The 2014 Lord’s Test remains a famous example, with India successfully turning to the short ball against England on the final day.

Then comes his relationship with players. Numerous bowlers have spoken highly of playing under Dhoni, particularly spinners who benefited from his guidance behind the stumps.

In many ways, Dhoni has already been coaching from the field for years.

Does Dhoni Want the Job?

In many ways, MS Dhoni looks like the ideal candidate to become CSK’s next head coach. But there is one question nobody can answer yet: does he even want the job?

Dhoni has largely stayed away from formal coaching roles since retiring from international cricket in 2020. His most notable non-playing role came when he joined India as a mentor for the 2021 T20 World Cup. Since then, he has not taken up a permanent coaching position.

That makes his appointment difficult to predict. An IPL head coach must remain involved beyond matchdays, contributing to recruitment, auctions, player development and season-long preparation.

Dhoni may have the cricketing brain for the job. The bigger question is whether he wants the responsibility that comes with it.

Could Dhoni Replace Stephen Fleming?

Replacing Stephen Fleming requires more than finding an experienced coach. CSK need someone who understands the culture he helped build.

Michael Hussey may offer continuity, while other candidates could bring greater coaching experience, but nobody knows CSK quite like MS Dhoni.

He helped shape the franchise alongside Fleming and understands what makes the system work. That makes him perhaps the most natural successor available.

Ultimately, everything comes down to one question: does Dhoni want the responsibility? If the answer is yes, CSK may already have Fleming’s successor sitting in their dressing room.

title: Cricket Australia Set to Allow Mitchell Marsh and Matthew Short to Participate in SA20 only After Completing BBL Assignment
content:
Cricket Australia’s decision sends a clear message, stating national duty comes before any other commitments.

Mitchell Marsh and Matthew Short will receive no-objection clearance for the SA20 only after completing their full Big Bash League assignment, ensuring Australia’s home tournament remains their first priority and preventing an early departure for South Africa.

CA Prioritizes National Duty of the Players

Attention around Australia’s white-ball stars has intensified after CA confirmed that Marsh and Short will complete their BBL commitments for their respective teams, Perth Scorchers and Adelaide Strikers, before flying to South-Africa. This decision underlines CA’s view that national and domestic responsibilities should not be overshadowed by foreign franchise leagues.

Meanwhile, Marsh is set to feature for Sunrisers Eastern Cape in SA20 2027, while the CSK all-rounder is going to represent Pretoria Capitals. The South African tournament begins on January 17, 2027, whereas the BBL is set to conclude on 26th of the same month, creating a clear overlap. Consequently, the Australian duo will only be released after completing their domestic assignment, rather than leaving midway for any other overseas tournaments.

Franchise cricket now dominates the sport industry like never before, with major tournaments competing aggressively for world-class cricketers, television audiences, sponsorships and commercial attention. Ultimately, Cricket Australia’s decision to keep its players committed to the Big Bash League before allowing them to participate in the SA20 underlines the importance of finding a sustainable balance. Protecting national priorities will remain essential as the franchise era continues to rise in popularity in the sport industry.

Franchise Cricket Brings New Challenges for Players and Administrators

Managing several tournaments has become one of cricket’s toughest modern balancing acts. Elite players are constantly moving between countries, franchises and demanding schedules, leaving little room for rest, preparation and personal time between tournaments throughout the packed calendar each year. Growing overlap between the competitions can also force difficult choices when national duties cross paths with foreign contracts.

While the franchise leagues offer valuable opportunities and popularize the game, their expanding footprint creates pressure on players and administrators alike. Administrators now face the increasingly crowded calendar confronting world-class cricketers. These leagues span multiple countries and months, making availability, workload and travel increasingly difficult to manage. Popular T20 talents like Mitchell Marsh and Matthew Short must balance national responsibilities with several lucrative leagues, requiring proper planning, while the authorities face the challenge of protecting domestic competitions without ignoring the commercial power of global franchise cricket.

title: Who Will Be CSK's Next Head Coach? Top Candidates Analysed
content:
Chennai Super Kings is entering one of the biggest transitions in its history. This time, the spotlight is not just on the playing squad but also on the search for a new head coach following Stephen Fleming’s departure last month.

Fleming spent 18 years as CSK coach, at the helm of the franchise, guiding CSK to seven major trophies, including five IPL titles and two Champions League T20 crowns.

More importantly, he helped build the culture that turned Chennai into one of the most consistent and respected teams in franchise cricket, with clearly defined roles, unwavering backing of players, and a reputation for long-term stability.

Replacing a coach of that stature was never going to be straightforward. Yet, with Fleming stepping away, the focus has now shifted to who can carry forward the Super Kings’ legacy.

Who could replace Stephen Fleming?

Several names have already emerged as potential candidates, each bringing a different coaching philosophy and level of experience. Here are the leading contenders to become Chennai Super Kings’ next head coach.

  • Michael Hussey:

Michael Hussey arguably stands out as the most natural candidate to replace Stephen Fleming, and the reason is simple: continuity.

Hussey has been part of the CSK setup for years, first as a player and later as batting coach. He tasted success during his playing days and later contributed to multiple title-winning campaigns as part of the coaching staff.

More importantly, Hussey understands how CSK operate. Having worked closely with Fleming for years, he knows the team’s preparation, player management and emphasis on clearly defined roles.

Instead of bringing in an outsider who would need time to understand the CSK culture, promoting Hussey could ensure a smooth transition into the post-Fleming era.

  • Rahul Dravid

    If CSK want a complete reset after Fleming’s departure, a new CSK coach in Rahul Dravid could emerge as an intriguing option.

    Unlike Hussey, Dravid brings significant experience in leading teams and has already delivered in one of cricket’s highest-pressure jobs with the Indian national side.

    However, his biggest strength lies in developing young Indian players. His work with India’s Under-19 and developmental setups helped nurture several players who later graduated to the senior level.

    That could make Dravid an ideal fit if CSK want to build around young Indian talent. Few candidates can match his understanding of domestic cricket and Indian conditions.

    The obvious drawback is his lack of connection with CSK, meaning both sides would need time to adapt to each other’s methods.

    • MS Dhoni

    But what if CSK decide against appointing an overseas coach altogether? What if they replace Fleming with someone who has been an integral part of that 18-year journey?

    Yes, MS Dhoni could be a strong candidate for the job. Not just because fans would love to see him win another trophy as a coach, but because the appointment makes sense.

    Dhoni helped build the culture Fleming leaves behind and remains an influential figure within the franchise. His tactical understanding and ability to get the best out of players only strengthen his case. Ravichandran Ashwin has also publicly backed Dhoni as CSK coach to succeed Fleming.

    The only question is whether Dhoni actually wants to coach. If he does, CSK may not need to look any further.

    Who Is the Best Fit as CSK coach?

    Replacing Stephen Fleming after 18 years will never be an easy decision for Chennai Super Kings. Michael Hussey offers continuity and already understands the system from within, while Rahul Dravid could bring fresh ideas and help build the next generation of Indian talent. MS Dhoni, meanwhile, represents perhaps the most fascinating option, given his influence on the culture Fleming helped create.

    Ultimately, CSK must decide whether they want continuity, a complete reset, or to hand the responsibility to one of their greatest-ever leaders. Whoever takes charge as CSK coach will inherit not just a successful team, but the responsibility of shaping next era.
