title: Who is Prashant Veer?
content:
Prashant Veer is an uncapped Indian cricketer from Uttar Pradesh who plays as a left-handed batter and slow left-arm orthodox bowling all-rounder. He came into national spotlight after Chennai Super Kings bought him for ₹14.20 crore at the IPL 2026 auction, making him the most expensive uncapped player in IPL history. Veer is known for controlling the middle overs with the ball and providing quick lower-order runs in T20 cricket.

Prashant Veer Player profile

Who is Prashant Veer?

Prashant Veer enters the IPL 2026 cycle as one of the most discussed uncapped Indian cricketers in recent times, and for reasons that go far beyond a headline auction price.

A left-handed batter and slow left-arm orthodox spinner from Uttar Pradesh, Veer represents a very specific T20 profile that franchises chase relentlessly: a spin-bowling all-rounder who can influence games in short, decisive phases.

We are not looking at a finished product or a domestic bully inflated by one good tournament. We are looking at a player whose recent domestic trajectory, role clarity, and skill set align uncannily well with what the Chennai Super Kings have always valued.

CSK paid 14.2 crore for Prashant Veer

At the IPL 2026 auction in Abu Dhabi, Prashanth Veer’s name turned into one of the defining moments of the event. Picked by us for ₹14.20 crore from a base price of ₹30 lakh, Veer became the joint most expensive uncapped Indian player in IPL auction history.

That number naturally grabbed attention, but it did not come out of nowhere. Rajasthan Royals and Sunrisers Hyderabad pushed aggressively, clearly identifying the same upside. This was not speculation-driven bidding. This was franchises responding to a sustained domestic body of work.

For CSK, the call was simple. When a rare Indian spin-bowling all-rounder becomes available at the right age, with role clarity and recent form backing him, you act decisively. We did exactly that.

Why CSK Went All-In on Prashant Veer?

CSK’s auction philosophy has never been about star power. We build squads around roles, balance, and longevity. Prashant Veer ticks boxes that are increasingly difficult to fill in Indian cricket.

As a bowler, he offers control through the middle overs, a phase where T20 games are often won or lost quietly. As a batter, he adds left-handed depth in the lower middle order and plays with clear intent rather than inflated responsibility.

His T20 numbers already show that his value is bowling-first, with batting as a genuine upside rather than the core. That is exactly the kind of profile CSK backs, develops, and turns into long-term contributors.

Prashant Veer Domestic Stats

Prashant Veer’s rise is firmly rooted in his 2024–25 domestic T20 season. The UP T20 League was his breakout platform. Batting in the middle order, he scored roughly 300–330 runs at a strike rate above 150, repeatedly delivering impactful contributions rather than chasing big personal scores

With the ball, he operated largely through the middle overs, maintaining tight lines and picking up a steady stream of wickets. His ability to bowl economically while still attacking made him one of the most reliable all-rounders in the tournament.

In the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, his batting contributions were more cameo-based, but his bowling consistency stood out. Across national events, he kept his economy rate under 7, a strong indicator of composure and tactical discipline. Selectorial reports repeatedly highlighted his pattern of quick 20–30 run finishes combined with timely breakthroughs.

Batting statistics

Veer’s batting record underlines his role as an impact player rather than a volume run-scorer.

The red-ball numbers clearly show that he is not yet a first-class batter, and CSK are not pretending otherwise. In T20s, however, a strike rate of 167.16 highlights his ability to finish innings and change momentum rapidly. These are cameo numbers, and that is precisely the role he plays.

Bowling statistics

Veer’s bowling is where his primary value lies, and the numbers support that assessment strongly.

In T20 cricket, an economy of 6.45 combined with a strike rate of 15.5 points to a bowler who doesn’t just contain but actively breaks partnerships. That balance of control and wicket-taking is rare, especially among uncapped Indian spinners.

Is Prashant Veer a Good Replacement for Ravindra Jadeja?

Prashant Veer is not a like-for-like replacement for Ravindra Jadeja, but he does fit a similar functional role in T20 cricket. Like Jadeja, Veer is a bowling-first left-arm spin all-rounder whose main value comes from controlling the middle overs and breaking partnerships rather than chasing wickets recklessly.

With the bat, Veer is used as a situational contributor, capable of quick 20–30 run cameos instead of long innings. The “Jadeja-like” label refers to impact style, not experience or stature. Veer operates in short, decisive phases — a tight spell, a timely wicket, or late-order acceleration — making him a developmental option for CSK rather than a direct replacement.

What Role Will Prashant Veer Play at CSK?

Prashanth Veer comes to CSK with a price tag that demands scrutiny, but also with a profile that fits our philosophy almost perfectly. We did not buy him for instant superstardom. We invested in a controllable, high-impact Indian all-rounder with the tools to grow inside our system.

For us, this is not a gamble. It is a calculated long-term call. And if his domestic rise is anything to go by, Prashanth Veer is only getting started.

Prashant Veer is an uncapped Indian cricketer from Uttar Pradesh who plays as a left-handed batter and slow left-arm orthodox bowling all-rounder. He gained national attention after being signed by Chennai Super Kings at the IPL 2026 auction for ₹14.20 crore, the highest price for an uncapped player in IPL history.

CSK bought Prashant Veer for his rare T20 skill set as a bowling-first spin all-rounder. His ability to control the middle overs, take wickets at a low economy rate, and add quick lower-order runs fits CSK’s long-term squad-building philosophy focused on role clarity and balance.

What are Prashant Veer’s bowling stats?

In T20 cricket, Prashant Veer has taken 12 wickets in 9 matches at an average of 16.66 and an economy rate of 6.45. His strike rate of 15.5 highlights his effectiveness as a wicket-taking spinner rather than a purely defensive option.

Is Prashant Veer an all-rounder?

Yes, Prashant Veer is a spin-bowling all-rounder. While his primary value lies in his slow left-arm bowling, he also contributes as a lower-order left-handed batter, known for short, high-impact innings rather than long batting performances.

title: Prashant Veer and Kartik Sharma Become Highest Paid Uncapped Players in IPL
content:
Chennai Super Kings have created history. They have signed Prashant Veer and Kartik Sharma for the price of 14.2 crores each, making them the joint highest paid uncapped players in the IPL history.

The five times champions headed into the auction with a different approach. Having released 9 players, everyone knew that big changes were coming, but none could have expected them to do something like this, and buy two young players for 28.4 crore rupees.

Prashant Veer and Kartik Sharma become highest paid uncapped players

Prashant Veer and Kartik Sharma emerged as the biggest talking points of the IPL auction 2025 after Chennai Super Kings spent ₹14.2 crore each to secure the two uncapped youngsters, making them the most expensive buys of the auction.

The identical price tags also pushed both players to the top of the all-time list of highest-paid uncapped players in IPL history, underlining the premium franchises are now willing to pay for young Indian talent.

Their deals comfortably surpassed the previous benchmark held by Avesh Khan, who had become the costliest uncapped player after earning a ₹10 crore contract in an earlier auction. The record-breaking bids for Veer and Sharma marked a clear shift in auction dynamics, with teams prioritising long-term potential alongside immediate impact.

Veer and Sharma’s performance in Domestic cricket

Both the player’s eye-watering price tags at the IPL 2026 auction were backed by strong recent domestic performances that made franchises overlook CSK’s usual preference for seasoned players.

Prashant Veer, a 20-year-old left-arm orthodox spin-bowling all-rounder, impressed in the UP T20 League and Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, where he scored 112 runs in nine T20 innings at a strike rate above 167 and picked up 12 wickets at an economy of around 6.45 — numbers that highlighted his dual-skill potential in the shortest format.

Kartik Sharma, a 19-year-old right-handed wicketkeeper-batter from Rajasthan, brought power to the middle order, amassing 334 runs in 12 T20 games at a strike rate of about 164 with 28 sixes, and also notching a century on his Ranji Trophy debut.

Their ability to influence matches with bat and ball made them extremely attractive to bidders, prompting CSK to break its traditional mould of backing experience by investing heavily in these uncapped talents.

What does the future holds for CSK?

With the acquisition of these two players, CSK will be hoping to fill the void left by Ravindra Jadeja among other players. Veer will be a great replacement for the Indian stalwart, while Kartik can really be an investment for the future, considering he is a good keeper-batter.

title: CSK Auction Buys 2025
content:
The CSK mini auction 2025 buy strategy turned out to be one of the most efficient and decisive among all franchises, with Chennai Super Kings walking away confident and well-balanced at the end of the event. Known for clarity in planning and calm execution, CSK once again showed why they remain one of the smartest teams at the auction table.

The franchise managed to address key gaps, strengthen both Indian and overseas depth, and secure players that fit seamlessly into their long-term blueprint. As discussions around CSK auction buy 2025 continue, the consensus is clear: Chennai got exactly what they needed, without overreaching or compromising their core philosophy.

CSK Purse and Auction Strategy

Chennai Super Kings entered the auction with a remaining purse of ₹43.3 crore and nine slots to fill, including four overseas and five Indian positions. It was a healthy purse by auction standards and gave CSK the flexibility to bid aggressively where required while still maintaining control.

Rather than chasing marquee names blindly, the franchise focused on role-specific signings, ensuring squad balance across departments. By the time the final hammer fell, CSK would be satisfied with both the quality of players acquired and the value secured, reinforcing confidence in their overall auction execution and future competitiveness.

CSK Buys in 2025

Here are the players bought by CSK in the Mini Auction of 2025.

Akeal Hosein 2.0 Cr

Akeal Hosein was CSK’s first buy at the 2025 mini auction, a move rooted in control and clarity. A disciplined left-arm spinner, Hosein bowls flat, hits his lengths relentlessly, and thrives on denying batters easy scoring options rather than chasing big turn.

He is especially effective against right-hand heavy line-ups and is one of the few spinners comfortable operating in the powerplay. Calm under pressure and tactically sharp, he brings reliability over flash. For CSK, Hosein adds matchup flexibility and spin depth, fitting naturally into Chepauk conditions.

Notably, he now becomes a rare link across the Super Kings ecosystem, having represented all three Super Kings franchises, underlining trust in his skillset and adaptability.

Prashant Veer

Prashant Veer is not just the highest paid uncapped player in IPL history but a clear future investment. A left-arm spinner who bats left-handed, he is the closest profile CSK have signed to reflect the balance Ravindra Jadeja provided for years. With Jadeja no longer in the setup, Veer’s arrival carries both cricketing and symbolic value. His bowling is built on control, accuracy, and smart use of slower surfaces rather than mystery.

With the bat, he adds depth and composure, rotating strike and finishing innings when required. Veer is not being asked to replace Jadeja overnight but to grow into a role defined by balance and accountability. He strengthens CSK’s spin attack, deepens the batting, and offers a long-term Indian all-rounder to build around.

Batting statistics

Bowling statistics

Kartik Sharma

Kartik Sharma, the joint highest paid uncapped player in the IPL, reflects clarity in long-term planning. A young Indian wicketkeeper-batter with maturity beyond his years, he is built for responsibility and high-impact roles. His batting is grounded in awareness and timing, but what truly sets him apart is his ability to change gears instantly. When required, he can turn into a clean striker, shifting momentum in a few strokes without resorting to blind hitting.

Behind the stumps, Kartik is sharp, vocal, and technically sound. His game awareness stands out. He stays calm during pressure situations and maximises advantage when his side is on top. He reads the match well, not just the delivery. Kartik is not viewed as a backup option but as a frontline player in waiting. With MS Dhoni nearing the final phase of his career, Kartik is well-placed to learn closely and transition smoothly into a larger role at Chepauk.

Batting statistics

Kartik Sharma’s numbers across formats underline why franchises viewed him as a serious investment rather than a speculative pick.

Aman Khan

Aman Khan is a pace-bowling all-rounder who adds versatility to our squad. He can contribute with the ball, bat down the order, and float up when required. Aman’s strength lies in adaptability rather than specialization. He understands team needs and is comfortable playing supporting roles.

For us, Aman Khan adds flexibility. He allows us to balance combinations, manage workloads, and adjust based on conditions. As a tail-end floater, he can provide quick runs or steady partnerships. These are the kind of players CSK have historically trusted to fill gaps without noise. Aman strengthens our depth and tactical options. 

Batting Statistics

Bowling Statistics

Matthew Short

Matthew Short is a Watson-like all-rounder in profile and intent. A leader, a captain for Adelaide Strikers in the BBL, and a proven top-order batter, Short is built to impact games from ball one. He is aggressive but calculated, capable of setting the tone in the powerplay. His off-spin adds further value, especially on slower tracks where he can comfortably give us two overs.

Short’s powerplay intent allows us to start fast without reckless risk, something CSK have lacked consistently. If he settles early, he can single-handedly tilt games before spinners even enter the contest. 

For us, Matthew Short is an opening option who brings intent without chaos. He gives us flexibility at the top and bowling depth through part-time spin. His leadership experience also adds maturity to the group. Used correctly, Short can dictate games early and give us balance through the Impact Player rule. This is a tactical weapon, not just a squad filler. 

Batting Statistics

Sarfaraz Khan

Sarfaraz Khan is, quite simply, a domestic giant. A run machine. A batter whose numbers in Indian domestic cricket demand respect. His technique against spin, use of crease, and ability to bat long innings have earned him the reputation of a “domestic Don Bradman.” The question has never been talent; it has been opportunity and fit. Sarfaraz gives us elite spin-playing security in the middle overs, especially on worn Chepauk surfaces.

If called upon, he can bat long and stabilise innings when others struggle for timing.

For us, Sarfaraz is middle-order insurance. He gives CSK a technically strong backup who can step in when conditions demand stability. On slow tracks, his ability to dominate spin becomes invaluable. In our environment, with defined roles and trust, Sarfaraz has a real chance to translate domestic dominance into franchise success. This is a smart depth move with upside.

Batting Statistics

Matt Henry

Matt Henry is an experienced international seamer whose strength lies in new-ball control, discipline, and intelligent use of swing and seam rather than raw pace. He builds pressure through accuracy and patience, understanding phases better than most.

Henry is also a familiar face, having been part of the CSK setup nearly a decade ago, and returns as a far more complete bowler shaped by experience. For CSK, he provides genuine powerplay insurance, an area that hurt the team last season. On surfaces offering even slight movement, Henry can deliver early breakthroughs while controlling run flow. He may not play every game, but in suitable conditions, he becomes a vital tactical option.

Bowling Statistics

Rahul Chahar

Rahul Chahar is a classic CSK-style signing: experienced, composed, and role-defined. A leg-spinner who relies on flight, control, and subtle variation, he focuses on building pressure rather than chasing wickets. Chahar thrives when batters are forced to manufacture shots, making him well-suited to slower surfaces like Chepauk.

His experience across franchises has sharpened his game awareness, especially against aggressive players. He stays calm even after being hit, trusting his plans under pressure. For CSK, Chahar strengthens the middle-overs choke.

Alongside left-arm spin options, he adds variation and attacking intent. His presence improves balance immediately, allowing CSK to control games through spin, a formula the franchise has long trusted.

Bowling Statistics

Zak Foulkes

Zak Foulkes is a young seam-bowling all-rounder with a strong work ethic and coachable mindset. He bowls with discipline and can contribute useful lower-order runs. While still developing, his fundamentals are solid.

For us, Foulkes is a future investment. We will develop him quietly, without pressure, and integrate him when ready. He strengthens our long-term overseas depth and aligns with our philosophy of building players, not burning them. Foulkes adds long-term pace-all-rounder depth to our overseas pool without immediate pressure.

In the CSK system, he has the space to grow steadily into a reliable option across conditions.

Zak Foulkes Bowling Statistics

CSK Released Players Before the Auction

Ahead of the auction, CSK made several tough but necessary calls, releasing players who failed to deliver consistent impact or no longer fit the team’s evolving structure. Among Indian batters, Deepak Hooda and Rahul Tripathi were let go after underwhelming 2025 campaigns. Hooda managed just 31 runs in seven matches, while Tripathi’s aggressive reputation failed to translate into results, with only 55 runs across five innings.

Vijay Shankar, despite a comparatively better average, did not provide the all-round balance CSK expected. His lack of bowling contribution made his release a logical move. On the overseas front, Sam Curran’s exit stood out. Despite scoring 114 runs, his overall impact with both bat and ball did not justify his price tag, and releasing him significantly boosted CSK’s auction purse.

Another notable departure was Devon Conway, previously a reliable opener. While his numbers were steady, CSK sought a more explosive overseas option to complement Ruturaj Gaikwad. Young players like Vansh Bedi, Andre Siddarth, Shaik Rasheed, and Kamlesh Nagarkoti were also released as CSK shifted focus from long-term projects to ready-made performers.

The most emotional and surprising decision was releasing Matheesha Pathirana. Once viewed as the future of CSK’s death bowling, injuries and a rising economy rate in 2025 forced a rethink. Alongside him, Rachin Ravindra was also released after showing promise but lacking consistency across seasons.

These exits set the stage perfectly for CSK players in auction 2025, allowing the franchise to reset its squad, free up funds, and approach the auction with clarity and purpose.

title: MS Dhoni IPL Salary (2008–2026): Complete Year-Wise Salary & Earnings Breakdown
content:
What is MS Dhoni IPL Salary?

MS Dhoni’s IPL salary is ₹4 crore for the IPL 2026 season after being retained by Chennai Super Kings under the uncapped Indian player rule. From 2008 to 2026, Dhoni has earned approximately ₹180 crore in IPL salaries, making him one of the highest-paid players in tournament history.

Explore the complete breakdown of MS Dhoni’s IPL Salary from the 2008 launch season to IPL 2026. We track how Dhoni’s pay evolved with us at Chennai Super Kings, during his RPSG stint, and across eras.

MS Dhoni’s name is inseparable from us and the Chennai Super Kings squad. From the very first IPL season, he has been the leader who defined our identity, our calm under pressure, and our sustained success in a league built on constant churn.

When fans discuss MS Dhoni’s IPL Salary, they are really tracking the evolution of the IPL itself, from explosive auctions to structured retention cycles. Over the years, his pay has not followed a straight line. It has risen, dropped, and reset in accordance with league rules, franchise strategy, and Dhoni’s own willingness to put the team first. More than the figures, his salary history reflects how value in the IPL is measured, not just in runs or trophies, but in long-term impact.

MS Dhoni IPL Salary in 2026

MS Dhoni’s IPL salary is ₹4 crore per season as of IPL 2026, earned through his retention by Chennai Super Kings under the uncapped Indian player provision.

An IPL salary refers to the amount a player is paid for a single season, either through the auction or via franchise retention under league rules. It is an annual contract value, not a lifetime agreement, and it resets whenever new auction cycles or special retention regulations are introduced.

When discussing MS Dhoni’s IPL salary, the focus is on how his yearly pay has been structured across different phases of the tournament. IPL contracts are fixed before the season begins and are paid regardless of the number of matches played.

Dhoni’s current ₹4 crore salary reflects role definition rather than market competition. Having retired from international cricket more than five years ago, he qualifies as an uncapped Indian player under IPL rules. Chennai Super Kings retained him under this provision, prioritising leadership continuity, experience, and franchise stability over auction-driven valuation.

MS Dhoni IPL Salary Year-Wise (2008–2026) 

Below is a clear, season-wise breakdown of Dhoni’s IPL earnings, showing how his salary shifted with retentions, mega auctions, and special rules. The numbers reflect the league’s changing dynamics as much as Dhoni’s evolving role with us.

Why Did MS Dhoni’s IPL Salary Change Over the Years?

Dhoni’s salary trajectory was never random. His 2008 highest salary stemmed from a single factor: trust. We backed him as captain, leader, and the core of the Chennai Super Kings squad, and the results followed. Titles, playoffs, and consistency justified every jump in the Chennai Super Kings Dhoni salary during retention cycles.

The plateau phase occurred in 2016 and 2017, not because his value dipped, but because CSK was suspended and Dhoni moved to the Rising Pune Supergiants. His pay stayed steady in a temporary setup where long-term planning did not exist.

The real shift came in the later years. Post-2021, Dhoni consciously stepped back from the spotlight. His role evolved from full-time match-winner to on-field guide and mentor. Salary reductions happened because CSK retained him as an uncapped player.

MS Dhoni Total IPL Earnings

From 2008 through 2026, Dhoni’s cumulative IPL salary stands at approximately ₹180 crore. This includes his confirmed ₹4 crore retention for the 2026 season under the uncapped Indian player rule. That figure firmly places MS Dhoni’s total IPL earnings among the highest in IPL history, achieved without chasing auctions late in his career.

What’s critical to understand is scale. IPL wages were never Dhoni’s primary income stream. His match salary is only one component of his overall cricketing economy. Endorsements, brand equity, and long-term associations have comfortably exceeded his playing contracts. Still, when we talk about value to us, MS Dhoni’s Total Earnings undersell the real return. Leadership continuity, dressing-room authority, and franchise stability cannot be priced; they can only be experienced.

MS Dhoni IPL Salary 2026: Latest Update

MS Dhoni will play the IPL 2026 season for us at Chennai Super Kings, officially marking his 19th IPL campaign. Retained at ₹4 crore under the uncapped Indian player provision, this decision was never about market value. It was about continuity, loyalty, and control. Despite ongoing knee management, Dhoni chose to stay on, reinforcing his bond with the franchise he built. Five IPL titles later, his legacy with us is already sealed, and if this is the final chapter, it will end in a CSK jersey.

Fan expectations are clear. Last season unravelled after Ruturaj Gaikwad’s injury left leadership unstable, and Dhoni stepped in as captain during a turbulent phase that ended with a wooden spoon. CSK fans are now demanding a reset. The hope is familiar. Comebacks like 2018, 2021, and 2023 have conditioned us to believe that when written off, we respond louder.

MS Dhoni IPL Salary vs Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma

This comparison puts Dhoni’s earnings in perspective against those of other modern IPL giants. While Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli stayed near the top of the pay scale in later years, Dhoni’s curve tells a different story. His numbers dip by choice, not relevance, reflecting role evolution rather than bargaining power.

What stands out is intent. While peers maximised salary ceilings, Chennai Super Kings Dhoni salary trends downward by design. We adjusted for squad balance. Dhoni adjusted for legacy. Different paths, same stature.

Key Highlights of MS Dhoni IPL Salary

  • MS Dhoni has earned approximately ₹180 crore in IPL salary.
  • His highest IPL salary was ₹15 crore per season.
  • Dhoni has represented only Chennai Super Kings and Rising Pune Supergiant in the IPL.
  • He was retained by CSK for ₹4 crore ahead of IPL 2025 and IPL 2026.
  • His IPL salary reflects both auction value and franchise retention strategy.
  • Dhoni remains one of the highest-paid cricketers in IPL history.

Conclusion

The MS Dhoni IPL Salary journey perfectly reflects the evolution of both the player and the Indian Premier League. From becoming the most expensive player in the inaugural IPL auction to accepting a reduced salary as an uncapped player, Dhoni has consistently prioritized the success of Chennai Super Kings over personal earnings.

Between 2008 and 2026, his estimated total IPL earnings of ₹180 crore place him among the highest-paid players in league history. More importantly, his contribution to CSK extends far beyond salary figures. Five IPL titles, unmatched leadership, and nearly two decades of loyalty have made MS Dhoni the face of Chennai Super Kings and one of the greatest icons in IPL history.

FAQs

What is MS Dhoni’s IPL salary?

MS Dhoni’s IPL Salary refers to his per-season earnings from the IPL through auctions or CSK retentions. It has ranged from ₹6 crore in 2008 to a current ₹4 crore retention with us at Chennai Super Kings.

How much has Dhoni earned from the IPL?

Across 2008 to 2026, MS Dhoni’s total IPL earnings are estimated at around ₹180 crore. This figure covers only playing contracts and excludes endorsements and brand income.

What was Dhoni’s salary at his peak?

Dhoni’s peak IPL salary came between 2018 and 2021, when Chennai Super Kings’ Dhoni’s salary stood at ₹15 crore per season. This phase coincided with CSK’s title-winning resurgence.

What is MS Dhoni’s IPL salary in 2026?

MS Dhoni’s IPL salary for the 2026 season is ₹4 crore. Chennai Super Kings retained him under the IPL’s uncapped Indian player rule, recognizing his leadership, experience, and long-standing contribution to the franchise.

How does Dhoni’s salary compare to that of other CSK players?

Even at ₹4 crore, Dhoni remains central to the Chennai Super Kings squad, earning less than marquee players. His value to us extends beyond numbers, influencing leadership, stability, and culture.

How much has MS Dhoni earned from the IPL?

From 2008 to 2026, MS Dhoni has earned an estimated ₹180 crore in IPL salaries. This figure includes his contracts with Chennai Super Kings and Rising Pune Supergiant but excludes endorsement income and sponsorship deals.

title: Why CSK Let Ravindra Jadeja Go: Inside the CSK Jadeja Trade Before IPL 2026
content:
CSK released Ravindra Jadeja ahead of IPL 2026 as part of a long-term team transition. The move, described as one of the franchise’s toughest decisions, focused on future squad balance and succession planning. Jadeja was consulted and was open to a fresh challenge, leading to the high-profile trade with Rajasthan Royals.

Background: Jadeja’s Long Association with CSK

For over a decade, conversations about the Ravindra Jadeja trade were unthinkable. The deal feels surreal because Jadeja hasn’t been just another player since he walked into Chennai in 2012; he became part of the team’s spine.

We’ve seen him drag games out of chaos, steal wins from losing positions, and script moments that live permanently in CSK folklore, especially that cold-blooded finish in the 2023 final. His presence shaped our identity, our temperament, and the way we believed in tight run-chases. For many of us, Jadeja wasn’t a chapter in CSK’s story; he was a whole era. And that’s exactly why this transition hits harder than any other Ravindra Jadeja CSK news we’ve witnessed.

What Happened: The Jadeja Trade Details

The moment the Jadeja to Rajasthan Royals trade became official, the entire landscape of the league shifted. CSK parted ways with two major assets, Ravindra Jadeja and Sam Curran, while securing Sanju Samson in what is now being recognised as one of the most consequential moves ahead of the IPL 2026 cycle. Samson’s arrival fits perfectly into the broader Sanju Samson trade to CSK narrative, but the numbers underline how serious this transition truly is.

Jadeja’s switch reportedly closed at ₹14 crore, a noticeable dip from his earlier retention tag of ₹18 crore. The deal was confirmed by the BCCI just before the retention window, turning whispers into headline Ravindra Jadeja CSK news and setting the tone for sweeping IPL 2025 CSK team changes.

What CSK Says: Reasoning Behind the Decision

When the CSK CEO Kasi Viswanathan’s statement finally dropped, it reflected exactly what we suspected: this wasn’t a performance-driven exit; it was a reality-driven restructure. He called it “one of the toughest decisions we’ve ever taken,” and coming from the man who has overseen every major CSK cycle, that line carried weight.

The franchise made it clear that age, role overlap, and the upcoming mini-auction forced them to reevaluate their Indian core. With almost no top-order Indian batters available in the market, securing Sanju Samson became a priority that outweighed holding on to experienced all-rounders.

CSK framed the move around team composition, long-term planning, and a responsible transition, rather than any dissatisfaction with Jadeja himself.

Jadeja’s Perspective & Consent to Trade

From CSK’s side, the Ravindra Jadeja CSK news came with an important clarification: this wasn’t a forced exit. Jadeja reportedly acknowledged that he was “at the fag end of his career” in white-ball cricket and was open to exploring a new environment. The franchise made it clear that the Ravindra Jadeja trade progressed only after direct conversations with him, ensuring every step carried his approval.

This mutual agreement matters. It shows CSK’s commitment to treating a long-serving player with dignity, and it reflects Jadeja’s own awareness of his career stage. Instead of clinging to comfort zones, both sides chose a transparent, respectful path; one that prioritised honesty over sentiment.

Bigger Picture: CSK’s Strategy Ahead of IPL 2026

The bigger picture behind the CSK Jadeja trade becomes clearer when we revisit the wreckage of the 2025 season. We didn’t just slip; we collapsed. Finishing as wooden spooners was the loudest alarm the franchise had heard in years. Our batting misfired repeatedly, the auction picks didn’t land, the retained core looked undercooked, and matches slipped out of our hands because we simply couldn’t keep pace with the league’s scoring standards.

Heading into the IPL 2026 cycle, CSK had no choice but to confront reality. Indian top-order batters were scarce in the mini-auction, which meant waiting wasn’t a luxury. That’s why the management acted early, moving aggressively for Sanju Samson while the window was still open. His arrival gives us power, leadership, and much-needed dynamism at the top; something we haven’t consistently enjoyed since 2021.

This trade signals a clear shift: CSK is preparing for the next generation, not surviving on past glory. We’re moving from a squad built on experience to one built on future-proof roles: younger cores, flexible skill sets, and a stronger batting foundation. Therefore it will be interesting to see what Ravindra Jadeja replacements we can find in the upcoming auction.

Reactions & Implications: For CSK, Jadeja, and IPL Fans

The reactions to the Ravindra Jadeja trade were always going to be explosive. CSK fans have spent over a decade watching him define tight chases, manipulate middle overs, and carry the team’s temperament on his shoulders. So the heartbreak is real, and CSK themselves acknowledged that many supporters would find this decision tough to accept; a sentiment echoed across platforms like Hindustan Times. But tough doesn’t mean wrong.

For Jadeja, this is a full-circle moment. Returning to Rajasthan Royals gives him breathing space and possibly a leadership role, as myKhel and other outlets have noted. A fresh environment could unlock the final productive chapter of his white-ball career.

For CSK, though, the implications run deeper. We gain a reinforced batting core with Samson, but we lose irreplaceable all-round depth. Team balance now demands sharper resource allocation, especially in the lower-order and spin departments.

And for the league, this move signals a new era. IPL teams are no longer bound by legacy loyalty; they’re prioritising aggressive reshuffles, succession planning, and long-term architecture over sentiment. The CSK Jadeja trade isn’t just a storyline; it’s a message to every franchise about where modern IPL strategy is heading.

Future without Jadeja

In the end, the CSK Jadeja trade wasn’t a knee-jerk reaction but a calculated transition shaped by respect, necessity, and future design. CSK weighed Jadeja’s legacy, the squad’s structural gaps, and the demands of a ruthlessly competitive league before finalising the move.

And while the fanbase will understandably grieve the end of an era, the franchise’s approach reflects what modern IPL cricket now demands: evolution over emotion, and long-term stability over short-term comfort.

Whether this bold step turns into a masterstroke or a misread will only become clear from the 2026 season onwards. What we do know is that the Ravindra Jadeja trade has opened two new chapters: one for CSK’s rebuild, and one for Jadeja’s reinvention at Rajasthan.

title: CSK 2008 Squad: Full List, Key Players & Season Highlights
content:
The 2008 CSK squad was an OG lineup featuring a mix of Indian and international stars, all deserving of the label ‘superstar’. Led by the charismatic Thala MS Dhoni, the Chennai Super Kings 2008 squad set the tone for the team’s long-term success. Here’s the complete list of players, roles, and season highlights.

When the first season of IPL took place in 2008, many people found it hard to understand what T20 cricket was was really all about and how to strategise. And then there was one man, sitting in the CSK dressing room, who had it all figured out – MS Dhoni.

Dhoni was the captain of the inaugural champions of the ICC T20 World Cup. The first of its kind. Hence, when others were scrambling for ideas, Thala had it all figured out. And what aided him the most was the Chennai Super Kings 2008 Squad.

With this squad, they didn’t just participate in the tournament. Rather, they put up a strong challenge for the title itself, going all the way to the final. Only to come up a bit short of the finishing line. But that was just the beginning of the legacy.

So, without further ado, let’s take a look at the very first Chennai Super Kings squad from the year 2008.

Full CSK 2008 Squad List

The CSK team in the inaugural season of the IPL had a perfect blend of everything you could ask for. Yes, there was a good mix of Indian and foreign players, with the right balance of experience and youth.

Indian Players in the CSK 2008 Squad

  • MS Dhoni (Captain & Wicketkeeper)
  • Suresh Raina
  • Parthiv Patel
  • Joginder Sharma
  • S Badrinath
  • Lakshmipathy Balaji
  • Manpreet Gony
  • Vidyut Sivaramakrishnan
  • Palani Amarnath
  • Abhinav Mukund

Overseas Players in the 2008 CSK Squad

  • Matthew Hayden
  • Michael Hussey
  • Stephen Fleming
  • Albie Morkel
  • Jacob Oram
  • Makhaya Ntini
  • Muttiah Muralitharan
  • Chamara Kapugedera

CSK’s Performance in the IPL 2008

The debut campaign of the Chennai Super Kings in 2008 witnessed them gain the respect of cricket fanatics. And other teams knew that if they were to win the league in the coming seasons, CSK was the team to beat.

Chennai Super Kings finished their first season third on the league standings, with eight wins from 14 games. Their key players like Suresh Raina and MS Dhoni emerged as the highest run scorers for the side, with 421 and 414 runs to their name, respectively.

Manpreet Gony and Albie Morkel were the highest wicket takers for CSK with 17 wickets each to their name. Showcasing that the team had already broken the code of how to use Indian and foreign players in tandem. Together, they were the joint fourth-highest wicket taker for the season.

In the same season, pacer Lakshmipathy Balaji etched his name in history — he claimed the first hat-trick of the tournament and the first five-wicket haul (5/24), significantly boosting CSK’s attack.

Morkel was certainly a revelation for the team, as he also emerged as the highest run-scoring international player for the side as well. Morkel had 241 runs from just 10 innings, at an average of 34 and a strike rate of 148.

Thanks to this balanced performance and strategic depth, CSK beat Kings XI Punjab in the semifinal to reach the maiden final. In the final, they posted 163/5, but lost by three wickets to Rajasthan Royals — a last-ball finish denied CSK the title. Despite the loss, the 2008 CSK squad left a strong mark on the inaugural season.

How the 2008 CSK Squad Was Assembled?

In the inaugural 2008 season of the Indian Premier League (IPL), the 2008 CSK squad was built through a mix of auction buys and smart strategy under the new “icon-player” rule.

Auction and Icon Player Rules

When the first auction was held, five players were designated as “icon players” — stars such as Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid, Sourav Ganguly, Yuvraj Singh and Virender Sehwag — and assigned to their home-city franchises directly. Icon players did not go under the hammer; instead, they were paid about 15 % more than the top-paid auction player in the team.

Because CSK did not have an icon player, the franchise enjoyed more financial freedom under the $5 million salary cap. This allowed them to bid aggressively for top talent.

CSK Franchise Strategy

Using this freedom, CSK spent big to secure then-rising star MS Dhoni at the auction, reportedly paying US $1.5 million (about ₹9.5 crore).

The move was not just about raw talent — Dhoni’s proven T20 credentials and leadership added strategic value. Alongside Dhoni, CSK also snapped up experienced foreign names like Matthew Hayden, Muttiah Muralitharan, Michael Hussey and Stephen Fleming, along with Indian players such as Suresh Raina, Parthiv Patel and Lakshmipathy Balaji.

This blend of strategic bidding, absence of icon surcharge, and balanced squad construction helped the 2008 CSK squad become competitive right from the start.

Who was the captain of the CSK 2008 squad?

MS Dhoni captained the CSK 2008 squad, leading the team in their first IPL season and guiding them to the final.

Who were the overseas players in the Chennai Super Kings 2008 squad?

The overseas group included Matthew Hayden, Michael Hussey, Stephen Fleming, Jacob Oram, Albie Morkel, Makhaya Ntini, Muttiah Muralitharan and Chamara Kapugedera.

How many matches did CSK win in IPL 2008?

CSK won 8 out of 14 league-stage games, finishing third before advancing to the semifinal and then the final.

Suresh Raina was CSK’s top run-scorer, while MS Dhoni added crucial middle-order runs. Lakshmipathy Balaji led standout bowling performances with a hat-trick and the tournament’s first five-wicket haul. Michael Hussey also made early impact with a match-winning century.

title: Matthew de Villiers in JSK: A New Addition for SA20 2025
content:
Joburg Super Kings have added Matthew de Villiers to their squad for the upcoming SA20 season. He joins the team as a replacement for Brandon King, who was picked in the auction but has now been withdrawn. The reason for King’s replacement has not been disclosed yet.

De Villiers arrives as one of the most in-form batters in South African domestic cricket and brings strong recent numbers across formats. His call-up marks a big moment in his young career and gives JSK a player who has been rising fast through the system.

Why JSK Picked Matthew de Villiers?

De Villiers has been one of the standout performers of the CSA T20 Challenge. He scored 394 runs in 8 innings, averaging 65.66 at a strike rate of 141.21. He also hit five fifties and finished as the top run scorer in the tournament.

No batter matched his consistency or ability to hold an innings together. His highest score of 96 not out showed the kind of temperament that wins games. JSK needed a player who could arrive in form, and de Villiers checked every box.

A Background Built on Early Promise

Before turning professional, de Villiers built his game through years of heavy scoring in school and club cricket. He captained Wynberg Boys’ 1st XI, scored more than 1,500 runs in a UK league season, and followed it with big returns in the Netherlands and again in England.

In first-class cricket for the Warriors, he has 618 runs with a double century to his name. Everything about his journey points to a batter who knows how to adapt and grow.

Why Matthew de Villiers Fits Joburg Super Kings?

JSK’s batting needed stability in the middle order. They have hitters who can clear boundaries, but they lacked someone who can farm strike, rotate well, and steady the innings without slowing the scoring rate. De Villiers brings exactly that.

His T20 numbers show he scores quickly while still batting deep. His 50 fours and five sixes in just nine T20 games reflect smart, controlled batting rather than blind aggression. For a team that often loses momentum between overs 7 and 14, he offers balance. He can rebuild after early wickets, guide a chase, or launch late. De Villiers arrives as a dependable anchor who can hold JSK’s innings together when the game becomes chaotic.

title: Dewald Brevis' Maiden ODI Fifty Powers South Africa’s Chase to Win
content:
Dewald Brevis played a crucial role in South Africa’s chase in Raipur, stitching together a breathtaking fifty that shifted the match in their direction. His maiden fifty in ODIs came at a time when India were trying to pull things back, but Brevis walked in and turned the game on its head with clean, confident hitting that kept the momentum with the visitors.

Brevis has already built a name for himself as a natural striker of the ball in limited overs cricket, and this knock only strengthened that reputation. This was one of his most impactful ODI fifties, adding to his growing list of half centuries in the format. His ability to hit sixes at will, especially in high-pressure moments, makes him one of South Africa’s most dangerous middle-order players. That quality was on full display in this innings.

Brevis smashes maiden Fifty in ODIs

Brevis’ approach was simple. He took a few balls to settle and then went after the bowlers without hesitation. Kuldeep Yadav, who had earlier slowed things down for India, could not hold Brevis back. Brevis used his feet well, stepped out, and launched him straight down the ground for a pair of massive sixes. It was the kind of hitting that immediately forced India to rethink their field placements.

Harshit Rana, who had been mixing his lengths well, faced similar treatment. Anything even slightly short sat up perfectly for Brevis, and he pulled it cleanly into the stands. By the time his innings ended, he had struck 5 towering sixes and kept the required run rate firmly within reach. His 54 from just 34 balls was the exact injection of pace South Africa needed during the second half of the chase.

Brevis set stage for the win

The partnership he built during that period helped stabilise the innings after a couple of wickets and gave South Africa the belief and scoring rate they needed. Once Brevis had done his job, Matthew Breetzke carried the chase forward with a steady hand.

In the final overs, the remaining batters finished what Brevis and Markram had set up. Calm, risk-free batting from the lower order ensured South Africa crossed the line with four wickets in hand.

Brevis’ half-century may have been short in length, but it carried tremendous value. His clean striking, his confidence against both spin and pace, and his natural ability to find the boundary made him the spark that brought South Africa back into the contest and eventually to victory.

Gaikwad’s Century

Earlier the Indian nnings was anchored by Ruturaj Gaikwad’s maiden ODI century, supported by Virat Kohli at the other end. After a shaky start at 62/2, Gaikwad and Kohli stitched a commanding 195-run third-wicket stand. Their efforts powered India to a competitive 358/5 in 50 overs, setting a challenging target for South Africa.

title: Ruturaj Gaikwad Scores Maiden ODI Century in Raipur
content:
Ruturaj Gaikwad struck his maiden ODI hundred in Raipur on Wednesday, becoming the first batter to score a century at the venue. His 195-run stand with Virat Kohli powered India to 358, but South Africa chased the target to win by four wickets.

CSK captain Ruturaj Gaikwad announced his return to international cricket in style, scoring his maiden hundred at Raipur on Wednesday. Filling in for Shreyas Iyer, Gaikwad batted at number four in the second ODI against South Africa and showcased his composure with a massive 195-run partnership with Kohli for the third wicket, helping India post a total of 358 runs.

Gaikwad’s hundred in tough times

When Gaikwad reached the crease, India were reeling at 62 for two after the wicket of Yashasvi Jaiswal. The pitch was nothing like the one seen at Ranchi. There was no true bounce, which made batting difficult.

In such a situation, Gaikwad was dealt a snorter first up by Marco Jansen, a ball that would have dismissed many batters. However, Gaikwad survived a scare as the ball brushed his glove and flew over the keeper to the boundary.

Gaikwad was tentative from there onwards, playing one ball at a time, but his approach remained positive as he continued to put away the loose deliveries. It took him 52 balls to reach his first fifty, a grinding knock built on strike rotation.

Those first fifty runs involved several singles and doubles, as both Kohli and Gaikwad communicated well and kept the scoreboard moving. It was a steady phase of rebuilding, and the pair handled it smartly. Only after crossing the fifty-run mark did Gaikwad truly begin to open up.

In the 20-odd balls that followed, he played some of the most fluent cricket associated with him. While the first fifty took 52 balls, the next came in just 25. His acceleration included nine fours and a massive six against Keshav Maharaj. That shift in tempo eased the pressure on Kohli too, allowing him to settle into his natural rhythm.

The 195-Run Kohli–Gaikwad Stand

The partnership between Kohli and Gaikwad was the backbone of India’s innings. Their 195-run stand transformed a precarious start into a position of strength, giving India a platform for a competitive score. Kohli’s century at the other end ensured the pressure never shifted back to the South African bowlers.

Gaikwad crates history in Raipur

Gaikwad’s century also carried historic weight — he became the first batter ever to score an ODI century at the Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Stadium. His knock set the tone for India’s strong first-innings total.

Despite the twin centuries and India’s imposing 358 for 5, the result did not go their way. Aiden Markram’s well-paced 110, supported by Dewald Brevis and Matthew Breetzke, guided South Africa to a four-wicket win. The visitors chased down 359 with composure, levelling the series 1-1 and leaving India to reflect on a lost opportunity despite a standout Gaikwad ODI Century.

title: CSK Openers for IPL 2026: Who Should Open for Chennai Super Kings?
content:
The most likely CSK openers for IPL 2026 are Ayush Mhatre and Sanju Samson, with Ruturaj Gaikwad moving permanently to his preferred No. 3 role. Sanju’s arrival almost solidifies this setup. It gives CSK an aggressive yet experienced powerplay batter alongside a fearless young enforcer, instantly addressing the instability that has plagued their opening combinations over the last two seasons and anchoring the franchise’s wider structural reset for 2026.

Who Can Open for CSK in IPL 2026?

The debate around CSK openers for IPL 2026 is no longer speculative—it is structural. Ruturaj Gaikwad has committed to batting at No. 3, Ayush Mhatre has exploded onto the scene as a 17-year-old phenomenon, and MS Dhoni is entering what is likely his final competitive stretch. Together, these transitions force Chennai Super Kings to rethink their approach from the very first over.

CSK openers troubles in Powerplay

With the auction done, the focus shifts purely to execution. Chennai Super Kings must address their dipping powerplay run rate from 2025 and devise a clear top-order strategy that maximises intent early without exposing the middle order too soon.

Aayush Mhatre: The Confirmed First Opener

Ayush Mhatre isn’t just a promising teenager; he is CSK’s most uncompromisable asset among CSK openers. His 2025 breakout—240 runs in seven matches at a strike rate touching 190—instantly cemented him as a long-term starter.

What sets Ayush apart is his unfiltered powerplay intent. There is no hesitation and no anchoring—only clean, repeatable hitting against both pace and spin. That reliability gives CSK the aggressive foundation they have lacked since Devon Conway’s exit. Simply by being fearless, Ayush stabilises the structure and allows the rest of the CSK batting order to fall into place naturally.

Who Should Partner with Ayush Mhatre? CSK Openers 2026 Breakdown

With Ruturaj Gaikwad settling at No. 3 and Ayush Mhatre locked in as the first name among CSK openers, the real question becomes unavoidable: who walks out with Ayush? The answer will decide not just the top order, but CSK’s entire XI.

Sanju Samson

Sanju Samson is not just an option anymore; he is the reality. CSK did not trade for a stopgap. They brought in a 31-year-old, long-term T20 asset who has already proven himself as an opener for India and in the IPL. With over 4,700 IPL runs at a strike rate of around 140, pushing Sanju to open alongside Ayush would immediately supercharge the powerplay.

More importantly, Sanju’s move almost solidifies the opening structure. It creates clarity, unlocks an all-Indian top order, and frees CSK to use overseas slots for bowling and finishing depth—an area that hurt them badly in 2025.

Overseas CSK Opener (Devon Conway Replacement)

The alternate path is a return to tradition. Across CSK’s title-winning eras, one pattern stands tall: when an overseas opener controlled the powerplay, CSK looked like champions. Names like Matthew Hayden, Mike Hussey, Faf du Plessis, and Devon Conway defined this template.

If CSK revert to that model in 2026, an overseas opener alongside Ayush—Matthew Short is the only viable option in the squad, as he is the sole foreign batter with consistent experience opening the innings.

This keeps Sanju Samson in the middle order and deepens the batting around Dhoni. The trade-off is clear, though: burning an overseas slot at the top reduces flexibility and forces players like Shivam Dube to bowl regularly.

In-Squad Alternative: Urvil Patel

On paper, Urvil Patel offers flexibility. In reality, he is insurance. He is not in the same bracket as Sanju Samson. His value lies in being a domestic plug-in option if injuries strike, without forcing CSK to reshuffle their settled top three.

Statistical & Analytical Comparison of CSK Openers

A clearer look at the available data helps frame the CSK openers debate for IPL 2026. Ayush Mhatre has already displayed elite powerplay tempo in a limited window. Sanju Samson brings proven aggression across IPL and international cricket, while Ruturaj Gaikwad offers long-term stability, now best suited to No. 3. Even Urvil Patel, in a very small sample, has shown the ability to strike cleanly in the powerplay.

Rather than projecting outcomes, the snapshot below outlines what each option already brings in the first six overs.

Powerplay Performance Snapshot

Note: Data reflects limited sample sizes and role-based usage, not future projections.

This comparison underlines why Ayush Mhatre sets the tempo, Sanju Samson raises the ceiling, and Ruturaj Gaikwad anchors the structure, making the opening combination a question of balance rather than raw numbers.

Best Opening Pair for CSK in IPL 2026

Sanju Samson and Ayush Mhatre are the best CSK openers for IPL 2026.

This combination offers the most balance, clarity, and long-term value for Chennai Super Kings. It fixes the powerplay problem, stabilises the batting order, and strengthens every department without forcing compromises elsewhere.

Why This Pair Works Best

  • All-Indian top four
    Sanju, Ayush, Ruturaj Gaikwad, and Shivam Dube give CSK control and continuity at the top.
  • Ruturaj’s natural role at No. 3
    He anchors where he is most effective, without being rushed in the powerplay.
  • Explosive yet controlled powerplay
    Sanju’s clean ball-striking pairs perfectly with Ayush’s fearless tempo from ball one.
  • Overseas depth where it matters
    Free overseas slots allow CSK to load the lower order and bowling with impact players like Dewald Brevis, Nathan Ellis, Noor Ahmad, or Akeal Hosein.
  • Long-term stability
    This pairing future-proofs the top order while easing pressure on an ageing MS Dhoni.

Who Should Open for CSK in IPL 2026?

Choosing Sanju Samson to open alongside Ayush Mhatre finally gives CSK clarity at the top. No more reactive powerplays. No more catch-up cricket. With intent on both sides and structure behind them, CSK start innings on the front foot again.

The verdict is clear: Sanju Samson and Ayush Mhatre should open for CSK in IPL 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who will open for CSK in IPL 2026?

Sanju Samson and Ayush Mhatre are the strongest predicted opening pair, offering the perfect mix of aggression and stability.

Is Ayush Mhatre likely to be part of CSK’s plan?

Absolutely. After his breakout in 2025, Ayush is locked in as a long-term opener and central to CSK’s future structure.

Will CSK promote Sanju Samson as an opener?

Highly likely, as it maximises CSK’s powerplay impact and frees overseas slots for bowlers and all-rounders.

For CSK, Mhatre’s rise adds reliability and explosiveness at the top of the order — something the franchise values deeply. For India’s U-19 team, his current form and confidence are exactly what a young captain needs heading into a major tournament.

The timing of his form could not be better. Mhatre was recently appointed the captain of India’s U-19 side for the upcoming Asia Cup, and since then, his batting has only gone upward. What looked like raw promise last season in the IPL has now evolved into consistent match-winning impact.

title: Faf du Plessis IPL – Veteran Opener Withdraws from 2026 Auction
content:
Former CSK opener and the captain of Joburg Super Kings and Texas Super Kings, Faf du Plessis, has announced his decision to withdraw his name from the IPL Auction pool. This decision comes just weeks before the IPL auction, which is set to take place on December 15.

To announce his decision to step away from the IPL, Faf du Plessis took to social media, saying he will not play in the IPL for the first time in 14 years.

The statement further read: It’s a big decision, and one that comes with a lot of gratitude when I look back. This league has been a massive part of my journey. I’ve been lucky to play with world-class teammates, for amazing franchises, and in front of fans whose passion is like nothing else.

Faf du Plessis in IPL

Faf made his IPL debut in 2012, playing for Chennai Super Kings. In his very first season, he caught everyone’s attention by scoring 398 runs at an average of 33 and a strike rate in excess of 130. And rest, as they say, is history.

In total, he featured in 92 games for the Chennai Super Kings, scoring 2721 runs at an average of 37. He was also part of their cup wins in 2018 and 2021, playing an integral role in the title glory.

Following this, he played for RCB for 2 years and had a brief stint with Delhi Capitals in 2025. But after poor team performance, he was axed from the squad, which might have led him to opt out of the auction.

Let’s face it, the age of talent in IPL is getting younger by the day, and Faf is not. The player is already 41 years old and plays in several leagues around the world. Hence, it’s only normal for him to know what his body is capable of and want to play in a less demanding league: PSL.

What does Faf’s absence from IPL mean for Super Kings’ fans?

Faf du Plessis’ absence from IPL will have no impact on his commitment towards the other teams. The player will continue to feature in his home league, SA20, wherewhere he will take up the role of captain of Joburg Super Kings.

Also, IPL absence comes as a blessing in disguise for us. Since PSL is shorter and soon followed by MLC, we will have a sharp yet rested captain for the showdown in America with Texas.

title: Ayush Mhatre Scores Maiden T20 Century in SMAT
content:
CSK opener Ayush Mhatre smashed his maiden T20 century in the ongoing Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy match against Vidarbha on Friday. This innings came just hours after he was appointed as the captain of the Indian U-19 side for the upcoming Asia Cup Under-19 tournament.

Mhatre scores maiden T20 hundred

Mhatre grabbed everyone’s attention with his fierce approach in last year’s IPL, but with this knock, he has proved that last season wasn’t a one-off. This century comes after a dry run in white-ball cricket, especially during the Australia tour, where he clearly struggled. Now, it finally looks like he has broken through that phase.

Mhatre opened the innings with Ajinkya Rahane, who played a crucial role in their previous win against Railways. However, Rahane fell early, and a couple of wickets followed, putting the responsibility squarely on the CSK opener to take charge.

CSK’s youngster plays vital knock in big run chase

What followed next was absolute carnage. The 18-year-old smashed 8 fours and 8 sixes in his 53-ball 110*, ensuring Mumbai chased the target comfortably. Alongside his CSK teammate Shivam Dube, he guided the team to victory with 7 wickets in hand and 13 balls remaining.

Mhatre also stitched together two crucial partnerships. The first came with Surya Kumar Yadav, adding 88 runs in 59 balls for the third wicket. Then, he joined hands with Dube, who scored 39 runs in an 85-run stand that pushed them towards an emphatic finish.

In the first innings, Vidarbha’s openers Taide and Mokhade both scored in the 60s, giving their team a strong start. But Shivam Dube struck at the right moments, breaking the backbone of their middle order and denying them what once looked like a 200+ total. Vidarbha eventually managed 192/9 in 20 overs.

With this win, Mumbai sit second in the Group A table, tied on points with Andhra Pradesh and behind only on NRR. The defending champions will undoubtedly be targeting back-to-back titles.

Mhatre: The Youngest Centurion Across Formats

This SMAT hundred adds to an even bigger milestone in his young career. Earlier this year, Ayush Mhatre became the Youngest Centurion in men’s domestic cricket across all formats, breaking a 19-year-old record previously held by Rohit Sharma. His blistering List A century announced him as one of India’s brightest upcoming batters — and today’s T20 hundred reinforces that rise.

title: Ayush Mhatre named Under-19 Captain for Asia Cup
content:
Ayush Mhatre has officially been appointed as the captain for India ahead of the upcoming ACC U19 Asia Cup in Dubai, marking a significant milestone in his fast-rising career. After an impressive year across formats and conditions, the young batter has now been handed the responsibility of leading a promising U19 squad in one of the biggest youth tournaments on the calendar.

Ayush Mhatre Under 19 performance as captain

Mhatre’s selection as captain comes on the back of strong performances and remarkable maturity shown on tours to England and Australia. In England, he produced one of the most eye-catching knocks of the season—a blistering 126 off 80 balls in the Youth Test at Chelmsford, one of the fastest centuries in Youth Test history.

In the same match, he also added 80 runs in the first innings, finishing with 206 runs in the match. He went on to score twin hundreds in the Youth Test series, silencing critics and showing his ability to perform under pressure overseas.

His consistency earned him the captaincy for the subsequent India U19 tour of Australia, further cementing his status as one of the most trusted young leaders in India’s system.

Mhatre Domestic stats

Domestically, he has excelled for Mumbai as well, scoring 504 First-Class runs in nine matches, including two centuries, and delivering a record-breaking List A knock as the youngest to score 150+ in a men’s domestic 50-over match.

With the bat, he has shown range—from long-format temperament to explosive T20 hitting. In IPL 2025, he smashed 240 runs in seven matches at a strike rate of 189, including a top score of 94, proving his ability to dominate at the highest junior level.

U19 Asia Cup: Tournament Details

The ACC U19 Asia Cup 2025 will be held in Dubai from December 12 to December 21. India will open their campaign against a qualifier before facing rivals Pakistan on December 14.

The tournament will feature two groups: India, Pakistan, and two qualifiers in Group A, while Group B consists of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and one qualifying team.

With Ayush Mhatre leading from the front, India will look to combine talent, depth, and discipline as they aim to lift the Asia Cup once again.

title: Urvil Patel Century in SMAT: CSK Opener Smashes 31-Ball Ton
content:
CSK’s Urvil Patel has had a great start to the new season of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. The CSK opener and Gujarat’s captain smashed the third fastest century by an Indian in the history of T20 cricket.

Urvil Patel, who opened the batting for Gujarat against Services, scored a magnificent inning of 119 runs from just 37 balls, to help his side record an easy win in a Group C fixture.

Urvil Patel smash third fastest century

However, in doing so, he smashed a century in just 31 balls, the third-fastest in T20S. In his entire inning, Urvil smashed 12 fours and 10 sixes, as his side cruised past Services with 45 balls to spare.

What’s really interesting is the fact that Urvil Patel also holds the record for the fastest century by an Indian in T20S. This record, the player smashed in last year’s Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, against Tripura. Many claim it was an eye-opener knock for teams who overlooked his potential just days before in the IPL Mega Auction.

He also holds the record for the third fastest century in List A cricket, with a scintillating knock of 100 runs in 41 balls against Arunachal Pradesh in the Vijay Hazare Trophy.

Urvil Patel CSK stats

Urvil Patel became one of the most significant mid-season stories for Chennai Super Kings after joining the franchise as an injury replacement for Vansh Bedi, who was ruled out with an ankle ligament tear. Patel arrived with strong domestic form behind him, including a magnificent knock in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, and carried that confidence straight into the IPL.

Across his three appearances for CSK, he scored 68 runs at a strike rate above 200, showcasing rare aggression at the top. His 31 on debut at No. 3 set the tone, while a rapid 37 off 19 balls later in the season reinforced his ability to influence games in short bursts. Despite limited opportunities, his impact was immediate, giving CSK a dynamic middle-order option when they needed it most.

His performances convinced the franchise to retain him ahead of the upcoming auction, a sign of the long-term value they see in his profile. With Sanju Samson now strengthening CSK’s batting core, Patel’s explosiveness and wicket-keeping utility offer tactical flexibility.

In other games, Sanju Samson of CSK, who will join the team next season, also smashed a fifty. Samson was part of a great victory Kerala pulled off against Orissa in their season opener as well.

While chasing the total of 176, Samson opened the inning with Rohan Kunnumal and scored 51 runs in 41 balls with the help of 3 fours and 1 six as well.

title: Indian Replacement for Jadeja at CSK in IPL 2026
content:
Whenever we talk about a Jadeja Replacement, the first place we should be looking at is India’s domestic circuit. Overseas all-rounders might offer experience, but Indian options give us flexibility in the XI and allow us to play a stronger overseas core elsewhere.

And with the IPL 2026 Auction shaping up to be one of the most important in CSK’s recent history, we don’t have the luxury of gambling on foreigners when reliable Indian spin-bowling all-rounders are available.

The truth is simple: if we want to rebuild the balance Jadeja gave us, we need a player who can bowl consistently, bat in the lower middle order, and handle pressure in slow, turning conditions. That narrows the list, but it doesn’t empty it. There are three Indian names who can realistically step into the CSK system and strengthen our CSK all-rounders and CSK spinners group going forward.

Indian Players who can act as Jadeja Replacement

India’s talent pool is deep, and while none are proven at Jadeja’s level yet, several impactful match-winners have the potential to step into his role. Replacing Ravindra Jadeja’s greatness will take time, so fans must stay patient. Below is a list of Indian players who could replace Jadeja in future auctions.

Tanush Kotian — The Most Complete Domestic Option

Tanush Kotian is one of the most underrated players in Indian domestic cricket. He has been part of IPL squads before but barely got game time, which has wrongly convinced many that he isn’t IPL material. That’s nonsense. Kotian is 27, experienced, and offers exactly the kind of versatility CSK values.

His first-class numbers are outstanding:

  • 43 matches
  • 129 wickets
  • 2120 runs

That is elite for an Indian spin-bowling all-rounder. He’s not a tailender who occasionally swings; he is a proper lower-order contributor who understands long-format batting and can grind if needed.

In T20 cricket, his value becomes even clearer:

  • 33 wickets in 33 T20S
  • Economy under 7

This alone puts him ahead of most domestic spin options. His off-spin is tight, disciplined, and suited for conditions like Chepauk. And unlike many bowlers, he doesn’t hide—he bowls attacking lines and forces batters into mistakes.

Kotian, as a Jadeja replacement, works because he isn’t flashy. He offers control, balance, and the ability to slot in at No. 7 or 8. If CSK wants a domestic, long-term, low-risk option, Kotian is the smartest pick of the three.

Tanay Thyagarajan — The Most Explosive Spin Hitter on the List

Hyderabad’s Tanay Thyagarajan is 30 years old and, arguably, the most explosive lower-order batter among the Indian spin options. He is a left-arm spinner who can hit big, and that alone makes him valuable in the modern IPL.

Let’s break down his domestic numbers:

  • 34 first-class matches
  • 155 wickets
  • 852 runs

Those are serious stats. Tanay is not a part-timer or a bits-and-pieces cricketer; he is a full-fledged bowling all-rounder with a high ceiling. But where he truly stands out is in T20 impact. His strike rate is around 140, which is rare for Indian spinners who typically bat at No. 8 or 9.

CSK have always valued players who can contribute in both dimensions, even if they aren’t superstars. Tanay ticks exactly that box. His left-arm angle gives us variety, something we currently lack after Jadeja’s exit. He bowls with dip, uses the crease well, and has shown that he can handle pressure overs for Hyderabad.

If we want a Jadeja role-cover rather than a Jadeja clone, Tanay fits. He gives us a bowler first, then a hitter who can finish games late if needed. And with Samson now part of the setup, we need lower-order firepower. Tanay brings that.

Karn Sharma — The Proven IPL Performer Who Can Step In Instantly

People unfairly label Karn Sharma as just a specialist spinner. That’s lazy analysis. He has played across franchises, delivered in high-pressure situations, and even produced one of the most dramatic finishes in IPL 2024 when he smashed three sixes off Mitchell Starc, needing 24 in the final over.

His overall T20 record is far better than what fans assume:

  • 184 matches
  • 161 wickets
  • 1544 runs at a strike rate close to 130

That is the definition of a reliable bowling all-rounder.

Karn understands CSK’s culture too; he has already played three seasons for us. He knows Chepauk, knows the tempo, and knows exactly what the franchise demands from its spinners. He isn’t a long-term project, but he is a plug-and-play option who can step in on day one and cover Jadeja’s bowling overs without hesitation. CSK need bowlers who can bat, not batters who can bowl. Karn fits the requirement perfectly. He’s experienced, battle-tested, and offers immediate value.

Can CSK find Jadeja Replacement?

Finding a Jadeja Replacement from the Indian pool isn’t easy, but it isn’t impossible either. Tanush Kotian gives us control and consistency, Tanay Thyagarajan gives us variety and hitting power, and Karn Sharma gives us experience and immediate impact. If CSK want to maintain balance without reshuffling the entire XI, one of these three Indian all-rounders needs to walk into the squad at the IPL 2026 Auction.

title: Sanju Samson to lead Kerala in SMAT 2025-26
content:
Sanju Samson has been appointed captain of the Kerala senior men’s team for the upcoming Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy 2025–26, set to begin on November 26 in Lucknow. The move comes at a time when Samson is already in the spotlight after his high-profile trade to Chennai Super Kings and his strong run in India’s white-ball setup. His recent form and experience make him the natural choice to lead a fresh Kerala unit aiming for a stronger campaign.

Samson’s Role and Tournament Outlook

As Kerala’s leader, Samson will anchor the top order, control the pace of their innings, and handle match situations with the calm that has become his trademark. He offers Kerala stability with the bat and sharp tactical reading in the field. With a young squad around him, his presence brings maturity and direction—qualities Kerala have long needed in crunch moments of the tournament.

Samson has played 91 games in this format, for his side and scored a massive 2217 runs at a strike rate of 128. He has 15 fifties in this tournament, with 91 being his highest score. Hence, all eyes will be on him for inspiration and providing his team the perfect start.

Samson Recent performance in T20s

Samson enters SMAT on the back of a strong run in domestic and international cricket. He recently hammered three consecutive fifties in the Kerala Cricket League, showcasing sharp touch heading into a busy season.

Over the past year, he has delivered impactful knocks for India in T20Is, strengthening his case as a dependable top-order option. His clean ball-striking, quick acceleration, and safe wicket-keeping add significant value to both Kerala and India’s T20 plans.

He played a very crucial role in India’s recently concluded Asia Cup campaign, in which they trounced Pakistan in the final to lift the title. Samson played a vital role, to ensure his team went over the line. And will be considering this opportunity as the stepping stone to strengthen his bid for the upcoming T20I World Cup next year.

Leadership Wave Across Domestic Cricket

Kerala isn’t alone in turning to new leadership. Ruturaj Gaikwad has been appointed captain of Maharashtra, while Urvil Patel takes charge of Gujarat. This reflects a broader shift across domestic cricket: teams are banking on players with strong IPL exposure and leadership potential as they gear up for the new season.
