Latest JSK Squad Updates

JSK is entering a new phase for the 2027 SA20, with Albie Morkel replacing Stephen Fleming as head coach and several key players released after the fourth season. The franchise also has the league’s largest auction purse, signalling a major recruitment push before the new season. 

Joburg Super Kings have made one of the clearest changes among the SA20 teams by parting ways with long-time head coach Stephen Fleming and appointing former South African all-rounder Albie Morkel. The change comes as JSK prepares for a new era ahead of its fifth SA20 campaign. 

Several significant moves have reshaped the JSK squad. Faf du Plessis, who captained the side in Season 4, was released at the end of the campaign and is now available at the auction. Wiaan Mulder, the costliest buy in the last season, was also released ahead of the 2027 SA20 auction. In contrast, Jason Holder was pre-signed, adding an experienced overseas all-rounder to JSK’s squad for 2027. 

Therefore, JSK’s recruitment strategy is centred on rebuilding rather than simply carrying the previous squad forward. The franchise enters the Season 5 Player Auction with the largest purse, giving Morkel and the team management considerable room to revamp the squad. With the auction scheduled for 7 October 2026, 156 players have been shortlisted out of 789 applications. 

The overseas market is also expected to be important. As the auction shortlist includes experienced international players, JSK has a great opportunity to address gaps with proven T20 options.

For now, treat the confirmed squad as the list of players announced before the auction. The departures leave gaps in captaincy, top-order batting and fast bowling, giving JSK opportunities to address these areas through the auction.

Jason Holder is the only confirmed new buy for the Joburg Super Kings ahead of SA20 2027, joining as a pre-signing rather than an auction purchase. The West Indies lad brings valuable all-round experience and strengthens the squad’s balance. JSK pre-signed Akeal Hosein and James Vince after they were part of the squad last season. JSK still has six auction slots with R20.6 million available in hand, while the wildcard signing will be made separately. JSK can use the auction to address the gaps created by the released players, particularly in captaincy, top-order batting and fast bowling.

title: Joburg Super Kings Full Squad for SA20 Season 4 (2025-26)
content:
The Joburg Super Kings full squad for the SA20 Season 4 (2025-26) has finally been revealed, and fans are buzzing with excitement. With a smart mix of retained stars, pre-auction signings, and some eye-catching buys at the 2025 auction, the Johannesburg-based franchise is once again ready to chase glory in South Africa’s premier T20 league. Much like their sister franchise, Chennai Super Kings, JSK has focused on experience, balance, and local talent while sprinkling in overseas flair.

For those eagerly searching for the JSK full squad, or wanting to know the JSK team players list 2025, this blog takes you through every detail: from retentions and pre-auction signings to their latest auction picks. Let’s break down the Joburg Super Kings squad SA20 in detail and see how they stack up for Season 4.

Joburg Super Kings squad SA20

JSK Auction Picks for 2025

The Joburg Super Kings' full squad 2025 got a major boost at the auction table. The team spent big on domestic all-rounders and bowlers while picking experienced internationals at bargain prices. Here’s the JSK team players list 2025 from the auction, broken down by categories:

JSK Batters

Joburg Super Kings’ batting line-up blends power, experience, and youth. From Rossouw’s proven firepower to King’s aggression and Moonsamy’s stability, alongside rising talents like Forrester and Stolk, this unit promises depth and versatility for the season ahead.

Rilee Rossouw (R500,000):

The left handed batter is a great addition to the JSK squad. A destructive batter, Rossouw brings power and experience. His ability to dominate spin in the middle overs makes him invaluable.

JSK have lacked quality batters at the top in the past, and that reflects the over-reliance on the captain, Faf Du Plessis, all along. Rossouw will add the vintage touch of destruction and experience at the top.

Brandon King (R200,000):

The West Indies opener is known for his aggressive stroke play. At a base price, he’s a steal who can provide blistering starts. His keeping prowess is an added advantage, and it would allow Donovan to play as a spin bowling all-rounder.

Rivaldo Moonsamy (R400,000):

A promising domestic batter, Moonsamy adds depth to the batting unit and is seen as a future star for South African cricket. Averages nearly 40 in first class and has a T20 strike rate of 120, which only means he will provide stability in the middle.

Dian Forrester (R200,000):

Just when everyone thought that JSK Squad was once again going to be about experience players only, they went for Dian Forrester. He is a young South African talent who impressed in the domestic circuit. Forrester will look to learn from senior pros while grabbing opportunities.

Run machine in first-class cricket, has a T20 strike rate of nearly 130, the 25-year-old adds versatility and some leisure in team selection. 

Steve Stolk (R200,000):

Another emerging domestic batter who adds depth and future potential to JSK’s line-up. Under-19 star with SA, has proved his powers in the YODIs but is yet to make a mark in the T20 circuit. Watch out for this bloke!

Neil Timmers (R200,000)

A young fast bowler who adds backup options to the pace unit. A development signing with long-term prospects.

Janco Smit (R200,000): Known for his all-round ability but mainly seen as a batting resource, Smit could develop into a valuable squad member. Right arm pace and a destructive batter, JSK have invested judiciously on promising talents.

JSK Bowlers

Joburg Super Kings’ bowling attack is a mix of fiery pace and crafty spin. With Burger leading the charge and veterans like Tahir adding guile, this group offers balance, depth, and wicket-taking options.

Nandre Burger (R6.3 million)

The second-highest signing is a valuable addition to the JSK Squad for the upcoming season. Burger is a left-arm pacer who has grown into one of South Africa’s brightest bowling stars. His pace, bounce, and accuracy make him a strike bowler for JSK. Familiarity with JSK gives him an added advantage.

Imran Tahir (R600,000)

Teams change, but the philosophy of backing experience over youth remains the same across all super kings franchise. Another example of the same comes in the form of the presence of Imran Tahir in the JSK team for the SA20 2025-26.

The veteran leg-spinner returns to JSK. Though nearing the end of his career, Tahir’s experience and ability to pick wickets in crunch moments remain priceless.

Imran Tahir has played 435 Twenty20 matches and taken 554 wickets. He is currently fourth on the all-time list for most wickets in T20 cricket. 

Reece Topley (R600,000)

The tall English left-arm seamer brings variation and experience. His ability to swing the new ball and bowl in power plays strengthens JSK’s pace attack.

Prenalen Subrayen (R1 million)

A solid domestic off-spinner who provides depth and control. Subrayen’s inclusion balances the spin department alongside Hosein and Tahir.

JSK All-Rounders

All-rounders bring balance and flexibility to Joburg Super Kings. With Mulder’s marquee presence and Ranjane’s utility value, JSK have options that can influence games in both batting and bowling departments.

Wiaan Mulder (R9 million)

The most expensive signing for JSK and the third most expensive player overall in the SA20 2025 auction.

The recent triple centurion in test, Wiaan Mulder’s dual ability as a pace-bowling all-rounder makes him the marquee player of the season. He is expected to play a pivotal role with both bat and ball.

Shubham Ranjane (R200,000)

The USA all-rounder provides squad depth. His handy middle-order batting and crucial bowling in the middle could be useful in rotations.

Star Pick(s)

The Joburg Super Kings squad SA20 had two standout signings:

  1. Wiaan Mulder (R9 million) – A marquee South African all-rounder. His price tag reflects JSK’s confidence in his ability to win matches single-handedly. Mulder strengthens both batting and bowling, and his all-round balance will be key.
  2. Nandre Burger (R6.3 million) – One of the fastest-rising left-arm pacers in South Africa. Burger’s consistency in the domestic circuit has made him a household name, and now, with a hefty auction price, expectations will be sky-high.

Together, these two picks symbolise JSK’s strategy: invest heavily in South African core players who can deliver across conditions.

JSK Retentions and Pre-Auction Signings for SA20 2026

Joburg Super Kings head into the new season with a blend of seasoned icons and explosive match-winners in their retention kitty. From Faf du Plessis’ leadership to Donovan Ferreira’s firepower, this squad is built for impact.

Faf du Plessis

The first name on the JSK team's player list 2026 is going to be that of the captain, mentor, and inspiration for JSK. Faf du Plessis brings leadership, calmness, and unmatched T20 experience.

At 40, his fitness and batting consistency remain top-tier, making him the backbone of the batting order. Not only has he been carrying the batting of the Super Kings, but he has also been the face of the Super Kings since the inception of multiple leagues. 

Donovan Ferreira

Ferreira the hard-hitting wicketkeeper-batter continues to be an exciting middle-order option for JSK. Known for explosive finishing, Ferreira also provides flexibility as a secondary wicketkeeper.

As if that was not enough, in the recent seasons, he has also played the role of a handy spinner, who picks crucial wickets in powerplays. Integrated into the JSK and TSK teams, Donovan is slowly becoming a close member of the Super Kings’ family. 

James Vince

One of the first retained players, James Vince is going to be a vital cog of JSK batting line up in SA20 season 4. The English opener adds class and reliability at the top. Vince’s experience in BBL, PSL, and international cricket makes him a crucial anchor against the new ball.

Akeal Hosein

The Windies spinner has become a household name in the Super Kings Franchises. Having broken into the scene in the previous MLC season, Hosein is a player JSK cannot have enough of.

The crafty West Indies spinner is retained for his wicket-taking ability and ability to control runs in the middle overs. His batting ability also makes him a handy lower-order option, further adding to the depth of Joburg Super Kings squad SA20.

Richard Gleeson

Another one of the retentions is The English pacer is known for his raw pace and variations at the death. His selection highlights JSK’s faith in his match-winning abilities. He has had past success with Sunrisers Eastern Cape and will be adding a world of difference. 

How the JSK Squad Shapes Up

Looking at the Joburg Super Kings' full squad 2025, it is evident that the franchise has struck a balance:

Batting Strength: With Faf, Vince, Rossouw, and King at the top, JSK has both solidity and explosiveness.

All-Round Depth: Mulder, Ferreira, and Subrayen provide flexibility and balance across departments.

Bowling Arsenal: Burger, Topley, Gleeson, Tahir, and Hosein make up a versatile attack with pace, spin, and left-arm options.

The JSK team's player list for 2025 appears more rounded than in previous seasons, with fewer gaps in the middle-order and bowling combinations.

Joburg Super Kings in SA20

Since the launch of SA20, the Joburg Super Kings have been one of the most followed franchises thanks to their CSK connection. Owned by India Cements, JSK came into the tournament with a philosophy of consistency and balance.

  • Season 1 (2022/23): Finished 2nd in the league stage, qualifying for playoffs.
  • Season 2 (2023/24): Secured 4th place and a playoff berth again, though fell short of the trophy.
  • Season 3 (2024/25): A season of mixed fortunes, where injuries and inconsistent batting hampered their campaign.

Despite these hurdles, the Joburg Super Kings squad SA20 has always been competitive. With Faf du Plessis continuing as captain, the team has retained a solid leadership core and added impactful names through the 2025 auction.

Final Word

The Joburg Super Kings full squad for SA20 Season 4 (2025-26) is arguably one of the most balanced and exciting line-ups the franchise has assembled. With retained leaders like Faf du Plessis, explosive new additions like Mulder and Burger, and experienced campaigners such as Rossouw and Tahir, JSK fans have plenty to look forward to.

As the Joburg Super Kings squad SA20 takes the field in Season 4, the big question remains: can they finally break the jinx and lift their maiden SA20 trophy? With the squad depth and balance they now have, 2025 might just be the year Joburg Super Kings roar the loudest.

title: JSK Buy Nandre Burger at SA20 Auction 2025
content:
Joburg Super Kings have acquired the services of Nandre Burger for the upcoming SA20 season in South Africa. The player was sold to JSK, or rather retained by the franchise, for a total of R 6.3 million.

The moment the name of the player popped up, JSK were quick to put up the padel while competing with Super Giants. In no time, the player’s price reached 2 million.

Nandre Burger sold to JSK

JSK remained steadfast in their resolve to acquire the player’s services. The price kept hiking, but the Super Kings were determined. Even Paarl Royals and Pretoria Capitals jumped into the bidding war, but were unable to keep up.

Things went right down to the wire between DSG and JSK. The final price for the bowler was 6.1 million, for which he was offered to DSG. But since JSK previously owned the player, they were offered an RTM.

It was a huge decision to make. Having already lost Dewald Brevis to a very big bid, JSK were not willing to lose another important player and decided to match the price.

DSG, when asked to quote their final price, raised the bar to 6.3 million, and JSK were up to match it. And that’s how Joburg Super Kings bought Nandre Burger at the SA20 auction.

Nandre Burger SA20 auction was an amazing watch, as teams went back and forth to acquire his services. In the end, it was JK who acquired the player.

Injuries with Burger

What’s really fascinating is that the player was out for the entire last season due to injury. He even missed major international action for the same reason.

But in the recently concluded Major League Cricket, the player showed some great promise upon return. He was the leader of the attack for the Texas Super Kings, and the Super Kings franchise would certainly want to retain the player for JSK as well.

Nandre Burger JSK Stats

Nandre Burger’s stint with Joburg Super Kings in the SA20 has been a mixed bag. In 2023, he played 5 matches, picking up just 2 wickets at an expensive average of 76.50, conceding 9 runs per over.

He bounced back in 2024 with a stronger season—11 wickets in 11 matches, including a best of 3/26, while keeping his economy under 8. His bowling was far more consistent, showing control and penetration.

By 2025, though, he didn’t feature in the wickets column, going wicketless across appearances. Burger’s journey with JSK highlights flashes of promise but also inconsistency that he’ll look to iron out.

title: MS Dhoni The Chase: Captain Cool Shares Screen With R Madhavan
content:
MS Dhoni to feature in a Bollywood movie or series?

Well, we know that our Captain Cool has all the qualities of being a great actor on the big screen. Dhoni has showcased his artistic abilities in various advertisements; however, this time, he might actually be featuring in a movie/series project.

R Madhavan took the internet by storm on Sunday when he launched a teaser for one of his upcoming projects. While people had no idea what it was going to be about, they were surprised to see MS Dhoni alongside him.

What do we know about MS Dhoni and The Chase?

The project, according to the post by the 3 Idiots actor, is called “The Chase” and will be directed by the renowned filmmaker Vasan Bala. Although there is not much known about the project, the teaser suggests an action-packed story, for which Bala is famously known.

In this teaser, MS Dhoni is seen wearing body armour that reads ‘Task Force’ and brandishing his gun, even firing shots at enemies, while driving a car and performing stunts.

Along with him in the teaser is his partner, R Madhavan. Both characters are introduced with their names, and while MS Dhoni is called cool, he is someone who thinks with his mind. R Madhavan is introduced as a romantic, who thinks from his heart.

The caption of the post reads, “One mission. Two fighters. Buckle up – a wild, explosive chase begins. The Chase teaser is out now. Directed by Vasan Bala. Coming soon.”

MS Dhoni as an action hero

Certainly, the part that got fans hyped was the presence of their beloved cricketing figure, MS Dhoni.

Since the player has retired from international cricket and only features in IPL, his fans are always hoping to get a glimpse of him on social media. Hence, when they saw him in the avatar of an action hero, the internet was certain to go into a frenzy.

The character portrayed by Thala in the teaser is one who reacts to the situation, something we rarely see from him. Furthermore, his action-packed sequences left the fans in awe, as nobody could have ever imagined seeing MS Dhoni do something like this on the big screen.

Is “The Chase” a movie project for MS Dhoni?

From the graphics and the introduction of the two characters, it doesn’t really feel like “The Chase” is going to be a movie for MS Dhoni.

Based on the previous works of MS Dhoni, the level of graphics, the presence of Viraj Gehlani, and the absence of any substance that suggests a story, “The Chase” will either be a product or an awareness campaign.

What leads us to reach this conclusion is the fact that the teaser had a very Set-type vibe. It felt distant from the real world, as if the makers wanted the viewers to know that nothing in the video is real.

The presence of cheap graphics and stunt coordination gives away the idea that it is certainly not a serious project, on a movie or series scale.

As if that was not enough, both the characters are introduced by their real names. Again something that very rarely happens in movie/series trailers. Therefore, “The Chase” has to be a campaign for either a product or for some kind of awareness. It just cannot be a movie featuring the captain cool.

When will “The Chase” release?

As of now, there is no information available on when the MS Dhoni-starrer, “The Chase,” will be released. No information regarding this was provided on the video or the captions shared.

Therefore, as MS Dhoni fans, we can only wait and hope for more information to be provided to us soon.

title: Uncover The Whole Truth Behind Irfan Pathan Hookah Controversy
content:
Cricket fans in India are no strangers to old controversies returning to the spotlight. In recent days, a five-year-old interview of former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan has resurfaced, sparking heated discussions on social media.

The subject at the centre of the debate is none other than Mahendra Singh Dhoni, the legendary Indian captain under whom Pathan played his last international matches. While one clip has drawn attention for Pathan’s remarks on hookah and selection, another video highlights the strong friendship he once shared with Dhoni, Robin Uthappa, and Suresh Raina.

Together, the resurfaced statements paint a complex picture of camaraderie, loyalty, and the dynamics of the Indian dressing room. Leading to the creation of what we call today the Irfan Pathan Hookah Controversy. And in this article we will go over the controversy, take a look at the source from where it stems and what the different parties have to say about it.

What is the Hookah Controversy involving Irfan Pathan and MS Dhoni?

The controversy first re-emerged from a 2020 interview that Pathan gave to Sports Tak. At that time, he opened up about his departure from the Indian team in 2012.

Although his last ODI saw him take five wickets, Pathan never featured in the national side again. Many fans have long speculated about the reasons behind his exit, and Pathan’s comments added fuel to the debate.

Watch Video: Irfan Pathan alleges Dhoni of favoritism

In the interview, he hinted that social bonding played a role in how certain players were treated. While he did not take names directly, the insinuation was clear when he referred to Dhoni’s room and hookah sessions.

Pathan said, “I don’t have a habit of setting up hookah in someone’s room or talking about this. Everyone knows. Sometimes, if you don’t speak about it, it’s better. A cricketer’s job is to perform on the field, and that is what I used to focus on.”

The remarks were widely seen as a subtle dig at Dhoni. Many interpreted them as an allegation that players who shared off-field activities with the captain received more chances than those who did not. For a cricketer of Pathan’s caliber, who had played crucial roles in both Tests and limited-overs formats, the suggestion was both surprising and controversial.

What is the context of Hookah Controversy?

The so-called “hookah controversy” between Irfan Pathan and MS Dhoni has often been blown out of proportion. In reality, it traces back to a 2020 SportsTak interview where Pathan reflected on the difficult phase after being dropped from the Indian team in 2008.

Under Dhoni’s captaincy, he admitted seeking clarity on public remarks about his bowling. While Dhoni reassured him, Pathan felt repeatedly pressing for answers would hurt his self-respect. The “hookah” mention wasn’t a swipe at Dhoni or anyone else—it was Pathan’s way of stressing professionalism, making it clear he never leaned on off-field bonding for career progress.

Irfan Pathan was one of India’s brightest young stars in the early 2000s. Known for his ability to swing the ball both ways and contribute valuable runs down the order, he was hailed as the next great all-rounder. He played a pivotal role in several victories, including the famous 2007 T20 World Cup win, where he was named Player of the Match in the final.

However, his international career never reached the heights it once promised. Injuries, loss of form, and intense competition for places saw him fade from the scene. His last appearance for India came in 2012, under Dhoni’s captaincy, leaving many to wonder whether he was sidelined too early. The resurfaced interviews have reopened that debate, with some suggesting that Pathan’s comments are evidence of non-cricketing factors influencing his career trajectory.

Is there enmity between MS Dhoni and Irfan Pathan?

As the hookah comment gained traction again, another video from a 2021 interaction with Zee News also went viral. In this one, Pathan’s tone was very different. He fondly recalled the bond he shared with Dhoni, Uthappa, and Raina during their playing days.

“Robin Uthappa, Suresh Raina and Mahendra Singh Dhoni. Ye teen jo khiladi hote they, na to ye mere bina khana khate they, na to mai inke bina khana khata tha. Itni hamari zabarzast yaari thi jab hum saath mai khelte they,” Pathan said.

Translated into English, this meant that the three players never ate without him, and he never ate without them. According to Pathan, that was how strong their friendship was during their time together in the Indian side.

This clip presented a stark contrast to the earlier one. Rather than hinting at favoritism or politics, Pathan spoke about camaraderie, shared meals, and the brotherhood that often defines life in a cricket team.

Fans React to Contrasting Narratives

The return of these two clips has split opinions among fans. On one side, critics argue that Pathan’s hookah remark shows he was frustrated with how selections were handled and felt that off-field loyalty mattered more than on-field performance. On the other hand, the video about shared meals demonstrates that he also cherished warm memories with Dhoni and his teammates.

Some believe that both statements can be true at the same time. A strong friendship does not rule out differences or frustrations, especially when careers are on the line. Others feel that Pathan may have spoken candidly in frustration in one interview while showing respect and affection in another.

SKD’s take on Hookah Controversy

The resurfacing of Irfan Pathan’s comments has once again highlighted the fragile balance between personal relationships and professional careers in Indian cricket. His words reflect both admiration for his teammates and lingering disappointment about how his own journey ended. For fans, it is another reminder that the stories behind the scenes are often more complex than they appear on the field.

Whether one chooses to focus on the hookah controversy or the heartwarming account of friendship, one thing is certain: Irfan Pathan’s time with Dhoni and company continues to spark debate and fascination, years after his last match in Indian colors.

title: MS Dhoni Likely to Return for IPL 2026: The Srinivasan Factor Behind the Decision
content:
It’s the news every Chennai Super Kings (CSK) fan was hoping to hear, MS Dhoni could return for one final season in the Indian Premier League.

Reports suggest the legendary captain is preparing for IPL 2026, giving his fans another chance to see him in yellow before he walks away from professional cricket. While the thought of Dhoni’s farewell season is reason enough for excitement, the bigger question is; what prompted him to extend his career by another year?

N Srinivasan returns as CSK chairman

The turning point, according to multiple reports, has been the return of N. Srinivasan as chairman of CSK in May 2025. His comeback has brought a sense of stability and familiarity that Dhoni has always valued.

Srinivasan’s influence in Indian cricket is well documented, and his association with Dhoni is one of the most enduring stories of the IPL era. For Dhoni, who has always chosen loyalty over glamour, Srinivasan’s presence might have been the final nudge to lace up his boots for one last season.

The Man Who Brought Dhoni to Chennai in 2008

To truly understand this, we need to revisit the origins of the CSK-Dhoni saga. When the inaugural IPL auction took place in 2008, it was Srinivasan, then at the helm of India Cements, who went all in for the Indian captain.

Dhoni had just led India to victory in the 2007 T20 World Cup, and every franchise wanted him. Yet it was Chennai Super Kings who broke the bank and secured his services.

That single decision didn’t just change CSK’s fortunes; it altered the course of the league itself. With Dhoni as captain, CSK quickly became the most consistent and feared side in IPL history.

Srinivasan’s Faith in Dhoni: The 2011 Test

Their relationship deepened in 2011 during a defining moment in Indian cricket. That year, after India’s disastrous tour of England, calls grew louder for Dhoni to step down as captain. Many in the BCCI selection panel were ready to move on.

But Srinivasan, then the BCCI president, revealed later that he “exercised all my authority” to retain Dhoni as skipper. He admitted to overruling the panel, backing his man when few others were willing to. That act of faith cemented Dhoni’s place in Indian cricket and reinforced the bond between the two.

A Partnership That Defined CSK

From 2008 onward, CSK’s journey has mirrored Dhoni’s. Under his captaincy, the franchise has won five IPL titles and reached the playoffs in most seasons.

Dhoni’s calmness, tactical acumen, and unmatched ability to finish games turned CSK into more than just a team, they became a brand built on consistency and trust. Srinivasan’s unwavering support, whether in IPL boardrooms or BCCI corridors, meant Dhoni never had to look over his shoulder. Their mutual trust has been the backbone of CSK’s rise.

CSK’s redemption after last season

Yet, not every year has been glorious. The 2025 season was a disaster by CSK standards. With Ruturaj Gaikwad injured, Dhoni was forced back into full-time captaincy. The team, however, failed to find momentum and ended up at the bottom of the table for the first time in their history.

For a player who thrives on pride and legacy, that finish must have been hard to digest. And perhaps, it is exactly why IPL 2026 is so tempting. It offers Dhoni one final shot at redemption, a chance to walk away on a winning note.

For CSK, having Dhoni for one more season is about more than cricketing ability. At 44, Dhoni may not be the quickest with the bat or behind the stumps, but his presence still transforms the team.

Youngsters thrive under his guidance, fans rally behind his leadership, and the opposition respects his aura. His bond with Srinivasan only strengthens this narrative, a leader brought to Chennai by one man, and possibly sent off into retirement by the same.

Will MS Dhoni return for IPL 2026?

If Dhoni does indeed return, IPL 2026 won’t just be another edition of the tournament. It will be a farewell tour unlike any the league has seen. Fans will fill stadiums knowing this is the last time their icon walks out in yellow.

Every match will carry the weight of history, every run will feel like a parting gift. And if CSK can go the distance, Dhoni could script the perfect ending: lifting a sixth IPL trophy under the watchful eyes of Srinivasan, the man who believed in him more than anyone else.

For now, the official word is still awaited. Dhoni is currently in the USA, enjoying a good season of the US Open. But whether or not the announcement comes soon, the stage is set. IPL 2026 could be the season of closure, the final chapter of a story that began in 2008 when Srinivasan bet on a young captain from Ranchi, and won.

title: Ruturaj Gaikwad Hits Century in Deodhar Trophy Semi-Final
content:
CSK captain Ruturaj Gaikwad is having a great start to the domestic season. The Indian batter smashed a fiery century in the Deodhar Trophy semi-final against Central Zone at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.

Gaikwad scored a total of 184 runs from just 206 balls at a strike rate of 89, while facing the likes of Khaleel Ahmed, Deepak Chahar, Yash Thakur, and even Harsh Dubey.

What’s really interesting is the scenario in which he walked in to bat was anything but batter-friendly. It was the fourth over of the game, and his former CSK teammate Deepak Chahar had just reduced West Zone to 10 for 2.

From there, Jaiswal added 82 runs for the third wicket while batting with the young Arya Desai. Later, he also had a massive 148-run partnership with Tanush Kotian of Mumbai for the sixth wicket.

In his free-flowing inning, Gaikwad scored 25 fours and 1 six. With this, he registered his 8th first-class century. Surprisingly, this was his first competitive appearance since his injury in IPL 2025.

Gaikwad on his Deodhar Trophy Century

“I had good time to prepare, especially after not being part of the India A series. And then after that coming back, I decided to work on my red ball game, give it some amount of time and obviously still working on it, still long way to go,” said Gaikwad, in a conversation with News 18.

Ruturaj Gaikwad emphasized that his recent performances were the result of following the right process rather than chasing outcomes. He highlighted how red-ball cricket demands patience and rhythm, something he worked on consistently for over a month, including during the Buchi Babu tournament.

The injury layoff, though unfortunate, turned into a mental reset for him, giving him valuable family time. He used the break to focus on small routines, gradually returning to his game rhythm, and described the journey back as something he thoroughly enjoyed.

Lean patch of form

Ruturaj Gaikwad was going through a lean patch following his elbow injury, which ruled him out for the season. Following that, he was sent to England as a part of the India A team, but failed to perform to his fullest.

Later, he had signed up for a County stint, but couldn’t compete in the tournament because of some personal reasons, which forced him to return home before the season even began.

Even the invitational Buchi Babu saw some low scores from the batter until he scored a double century in the final game, which brought him back to form.

Gaikwad’s route to Indian team

What’s really interesting about this inning was the position in which Gaikwad came on to bat. It was not as an opener, but rather at the 4th number. This shows the transition that he’s going through.

Everyone is well aware that the Indian test team has a stable opening pair in the form of KL Rahul and Jaiswal. Hence, if Ruturaj Gaikwad wants to make a mark, he will have to bat down the order, and maybe the batter is prepping for the same.

This century, and the manner in which it was played out, couldn’t have come at a better time for Gaikwad. Everyone is aware of the lack of reliable middle-order batters that the Indian team is suffering with, and this century might just place Gaikwad at the top of the selectors’ list.

However, with the series against West Indies almost a month away, it will be interesting to see if Gaikwad can keep up his batting performance and deliver consistent results.

title: N Srinivasan Returns as CSK Chairman
content:
Chennai Super Kings’ administration is all set for a major overhaul, as they are likely to re-appoint N Srinivasan, the former BCCI president, as the chairman.

According to ESPNcrinfo, Srinivasan will take up the chair, while his daughter Rupa Gurunath will be taking up the role of the director. Although the franchise has put out an official statement, the move will be finalised following the AGM on September 27.

Kashi Vishwanathan, who is the current CEO of the franchise, confirmed the development. In a conversation with PTI, he said, “See, it’s a great boon for CSK. He’s been the best administrator for us, and I’m very happy that he’s come back into CSK. He’ll be in an advisory role only because he doesn’t travel much, but we’ll be in contact with him.”

With this move, Srinivasan will not just have control over the CSK franchise but also play an integral part in overseeing the international ventures. This includes the two international franchises, JSK and TSK, which the Super Kings own in SA20 and MLC, respectively.

Why was N Srinivasan removed from CSK?

N Srinivasan was removed from active roles with the Chennai Super Kings (CSK) primarily due to allegations of conflict of interest and his association with the IPL 2013 spot-fixing and betting scandal.

This scandal involves his son-in-law, Gurunath Meiyappan, who was a senior CSK official. Although Srinivasan was not directly accused of betting, his dual position as BCCI President and CSK owner led to intense scrutiny and criticism from the Supreme Court of India.

This ultimately forced him to step down from his leadership roles to uphold transparency and integrity within cricket administration.

N. Srinivasan as a cricket administrator

N. Srinivasan rose as one of Indian cricket’s most influential administrators. As BCCI president from 2011 to 2013, he oversaw record broadcasting deals, expanded the IPL’s reach, and strengthened the board’s global dominance.

In 2014, he became the first chairman of the ICC, marking India’s growing control in world cricket. Under his leadership, the Tamil Nadu Cricket Association modernised its infrastructure, hosting key international matches.

He backed domestic cricket, women’s cricket, and facilities development. Beyond administration, his role with Chennai Super Kings brought unmatched IPL success, cementing his status as a powerful figure who shaped cricket’s commercial and organisational growth.

Srinivasan’s Return: Stability and Strategy for the Super Kings’ Future

The return of N. Srinivasan signals stability and strength for the Super Kings setup. His track record as an administrator and his deep understanding of the franchise’s culture bring both credibility and experience back to the table.

With him as chairman, CSK gain not only sharper governance but also a stronger influence in the wider cricketing ecosystem. His presence will ensure that the franchise’s expansion into SA20 and MLC stays strategically aligned, while also safeguarding CSK’s dominance in the IPL.

For fans, this move feels like the old guard returning—one that could anchor the Super Kings’ future both on and off the field.

title: MS Dhoni Mentor Role in T20 World Cup 2026? Rumors, Reports, and Reality
content:
Are you ready to see Thala in a new role? According to internet reports, it is a possibility, as MS Dhoni has been offered the role of captain of the Indian T20I squad ahead of the T20 World Cup 2026.

CricBlogger, in one of their reports, has claimed that the BCCI is exploring options for mentorship roles, and the name of MS Dhoni is among them.

“Dhoni is once more offered to guide Indian Cricketers,” the source claimed. However, there has been no official confirmation regarding this from either the BCCI or MS Dhoni’s representatives.

The reasons behind his appointment are speculated to be the young squad. Everyone knows that MS Dhoni is great with young players. In fact, he even won his first ICC trophy with a relatively younger squad in 2007.

Will MS Dhoni become the mentor of the Indian team?

While the rumours are running rampant, experts are speculating on the former captain turning down the role, this time around. And the reasons they give are bizarre.

The most notable aspect is the presence of Gautam Gambhir as the team’s head coach. Well, it’s no secret that MS Dhoni and Gambhir don’t approach the game in the same manner.

Over the years, on several occasions, Gambhir has criticised MS Dhoni’s ideology. Hence, people believe that MS Dhoni won’t be up to work with him.

But the reason behind his turning down the role might have more to do with his previous stint with the team.

When did MS Dhoni mentor India?

MS Dhoni was part of the Indian team’s coaching setup during the 2021 T20 World Cup. Back then, the team was led by Virat Kohli and coached by Ravi Shastri, two individuals with whom he had worked extensively during his playing days.

However, the results of his stint were disastrous. Not only did India lose a game against Pakistan by a margin of 10 wickets, but they also failed to make it out of the group stages.

Should Dhoni take up the role?

Considering that the Indian T20I side has a younger squad, the presence of MS Dhoni as a mentor will be a huge boost. In the absence of Virat, Rohit, and Jadeja, the team will need a guiding figure.

Although Gambhir is doing his best as the coach, it would not hurt to have someone who actually understands youngsters and has a proven track record of bringing out the best in them, from time to time.

If we go by the current Asia Cup side,, which was selected last month, Suryakumar Yadav will be the captain, with Subhman Gill as his deputy.

In the name of experienced players, only Hardik Pandya tops the chart, along with Bumrah. But none of them have proven their mettle in the leadership roles. Hence, bringing someone like MS Dhoni for a Mentorship role won’t be a bad idea either.

With that being said, the decision of appointing him as a mentor hangs in the balance. There are very few chances that MS Dhoni will accept the role. However, if he does, it will be an interesting decision and might pave the way for him into the coaching setup, given that a retirement from the IPL might be around the corner.

title: Ravichandran Ashwin announce IPL reitrement
content:
CSK stalwart and veteran of the game Ravichandran Ashwin has announced his retirement from IPL. This news comes a month after he announced his retirement from the international stage.

Ashwin shared the news on his social media account to update his fan base. However, he also clarified that he is not stepping down from the game altogether and will be venturing into other leagues.

Ashwin announce IPL retirement

“Special day and hence a special beginning. They say every ending will have a new start. My time as an IPL cricketer comes to a close today, but my time as an explorer of the game around various leagues begins today.

“I would like to thank all the franchisees for all the wonderful memories and relationships over the years, and most importantly, the IPL and the BCCI for what they have given me until now. Look forward to enjoying and making the most of what’s ahead of me🙏,” Ashwin wrote on his X account.

This doesn’t come as a shock to anyone. From his performance in the last season, it appeared to be obvious that the player was struggling to keep up with the competition.

Ashwin himself addressed the same issue when he mentioned how he didn’t feature in all league games for the team. Following this, he had also sought clarity on the role from the franchise.

Only days after the incident, the player announced his retirement from the league, leaving fans and pundits wondering what the conversation would have been like.

Ravichandran Ashwin CSK stats

The stalwart of Chennai had his first breakthrough in IPL and later in international cricket, while representing Chennai Super Kings.

He joined the team in 2009 and captivated the fans and selectors in 2010 with his unique action and cricketing wit, which was second to none.

What really stood out for everyone was his performance under pressure. He clinched the wicket of Chris Gayle in an IPL final. Bowling against a batter who considers spinners as an easy target, that too with a new ball, is never easy. Ashwin not only took up the responsibility but also removed Gayle to prove his arrival on the biggest stage.

Ashwin IPL stats

In the next few years, Ashwin represented various IPL teams, including PBKS, where he also served as captain, as well as Delhi Capitals and Rajasthan Royals. He had a great outing with all of them before returning to CSK in 2025 and eventually retiring.

The stalwart has featured in 221 IPL games, during which he has scored 833 runs, with a highest score of 50. However, with the ball in hand, it’s a different story.

Ashwin has claimed 187 wickets in the tournament history, making him the fourth-highest wicket-taker. He picked up those wickets while bowling with an economy of 7.2 and a strike rate of 25.

For us in yellow, Ashwin will never just be another IPL player—he’s a piece of CSK’s soul. From that unforgettable Gayle wicket in the 2011 final to the crafty spells that set him apart, he carried the Super Kings spirit wherever he went. His return in 2025 felt like a homecoming, a full circle moment for a man who first made his name in Chennai.

Yes, his IPL chapter is over, but for CSK fans, Ashwin’s story will always glow in gold. The numbers will fade in time, but the pride he gave us never will. Once a Super King, always a Super King.

title: Ayush Mhatre Player Profile: Scorecard, Stats & Journey So Far
content:
When cricket fans talk about emerging talents who could redefine the future of Indian cricket, one name echoes louder than most: Ayush Mhatre. Every innings he plays is followed closely, every performance dissected, and every Ayush Mhatre score adds to the growing excitement around this prodigious teenager.

Still only 18, his journey from the crowded gullies of Mumbai to the bright lights of the Indian Premier League (IPL) and India U-19 leadership has been nothing short of inspiring. This is not just a profile of numbers and statistics; this is the unfolding Ayush Mhatre biography, one of resilience, brilliance, and the making of a star.

Early Life and Background: Humble Beginnings of a Rising Star

Born on July 16, 2007, in Walunje, Maharashtra, and raised in Nallasopara, Virar, Ayush Mhatre’s cricketing story started like that of countless young boys in Mumbai. But unlike many, his determination, discipline, and relentless pursuit of the game set him apart. Hailing from a Samvedi Brahmin family, Ayush was introduced to cricket at the age of six.

His father, Yogesh Mhatre, made a bold sacrifice by stepping away from a banking career to support his son’s cricketing dreams. The family’s support system extended beyond parents; his nana and chacha often accompanied him on the gruelling 80-kilometre daily journey from Virar to Churchgate, where he trained at Mumbai’s iconic maidans. These formative years defined the rising star Ayush, someone willing to outwork everyone else to create his place in cricket.

Ayush Mhatre Cricket Journey: Coaching, Grit, and Breakthroughs

Guided by renowned coaches Dinesh Lad (who also mentored Rohit Sharma) and Prashant Shetty, Ayush Mhatre honed his technique and temperament. It wasn’t always smooth sailing; depression and fitness struggles tested him. But perseverance paid off when he broke into competitive circuits like the Kalpesh Koli U-16 tournament and quickly progressed to represent Mumbai in U-19 and U-23 cricket.

His performances in the KSCA Thimmappiah Tournament were standout, where he smashed 173 against Gujarat and followed it with a gritty 52 against Andhra. These knocks fast-tracked him to Mumbai’s Ranji squad, where he announced his arrival with a maiden first-class century in only his third game.

Ayush Mhatre Age across different competitions

Ayush Mhatre age 17, has had a cricketing journey that already looks like a prodigy’s script. Picking up the game at six in Virar, he broke into senior club cricket by 13.

At 17, Ayush ticked off milestones most players dream of—ACC U19 Asia Cup debut, Irani Cup first-class debut, Ranji Trophy century, and a record-breaking 181 in Vijay Hazare, the youngest to cross 150+ in List-A.

By Ayush Mhatre age 17 years, 278 days, he was wearing yellow for Chennai Super Kings in the IPL. His career so far proves age is just a number when talent speaks.

Domestic Records and Stats: Ayush Mhatre Score Across Formats

By mid-2025, Ayush’s domestic performances had already begun shaping his reputation as one of the brightest young batters in the country. The Ayush Mhatre score sheets looked more like those of a seasoned professional than a teenager still learning his trade.

The standout moment came in the Vijay Hazare Trophy 2024-25, where Ayush Mhatre scored 181 off 117 balls against Nagaland, becoming the youngest player to score 150+ in List A cricket, overtaking the record set by Yashasvi Jaiswal. That single Ayush Mhatre score not only highlighted his shot-making ability but also his temperament to convert starts into big knocks.

Ayush Mhatre The IPL Story

Ayush Mhatre CSK journey is a story in its own. Despite these numbers, Ayush Mhatre went unsold in the IPL 2025 auction — a snub that many experts called a blind spot. But destiny had other plans. Hence, when Ruturaj Gaikwad fractured his hand during IPL 2026, Chennai Super Kings (CSK) turned to their promising trial player, Ayush Mhatre.

It wasn’t just a debut; it was a spectacle.

Mhatre score in IPL 2025

Ayush Mhatre carved his name with some unforgettable knocks in the IPL. On debut against Mumbai Indians, Ayush Mhatre score of 32 off 15 balls at No. 3 set the tone, fearlessly attacking Jasprit Bumrah and company.

He followed it up with another mature innings—30 off 19 balls versus Sunrisers Hyderabad, proving he wasn’t just about power but also composure. But the real highlight came against Royal Challengers Bangalore, where an astonishing Ayush Mhatre score of 94 off 48 balls in a tense 215-run chase stunned fans and stamped him as CSK’s next-gen superstar.

For a then-17-year-old, these numbers were not just impressive, they were transformative for CSK’s season. He turned from an injury replacement into a cult hero overnight, showcasing that fearless brand of cricket the franchise desperately needed in a transition year.

Ayush Mhatre in U-19 Cricket: Captain and Red-Ball Giant

Ayush Mhatre’s rapid rise earned him the captaincy of the India U-19 team against England U-19 in a two-Test and five-ODI series. While his ODI performance was disappointing, 28 runs across five games, his Test batting was extraordinary.

That’s 340 runs at an average of 85.00, underlining his ability to excel in the red-ball format. While the white-ball struggles showed areas for growth, these Test innings demonstrated why coaches and selectors regard him as a future all-format star.

Other Records and Achievements by Mhatre

Some key highlights from his young career so far:

  • Youngest player to score 150+ in List A men’s cricket (181 vs Nagaland).
  • Two centuries in his first nine first-class matches.
  • Fastest fifty in ACC U-19 Asia Cup history (20 balls).
  • Most wickets by a spinner in a single U-19 season, showcasing his all-round potential.

These feats make the Ayush Mhatre biography not just about runs but also about versatility and impact in pressure situations.

Impact on CSK and Future Predictions

Chennai Super Kings are known for backing young talent who embody maturity and composure. In Ayush Mhatre, they seem to have unearthed a gem who could define their next generation. With veterans like Jadeja and Gaikwad providing the experience, Mhatre represents the future core of CSK’s squad.

Insiders suggest he’s already being earmarked for long-term retention. Some even believe that, with leadership grooming, he could one day wear the CSK captain’s armband. For fans, every Ayush Mhatre score in yellow feels like the beginning of a new era.

As IPL 2026 predictions swirl, many pundits tip him as the breakout star of the tournament if given a longer run.

The Road Ahead for Ayush Mhatre

To sum it up, the Ayush Mhatre cricket journey is a blend of grind, glory, and growth. From his father’s sacrifices and long train journeys to scoring centuries in domestic cricket and Tests, and now smashing IPL bowlers with audacity, he has checked every box a prodigy must.

The numbers, especially the recent U-19 red-ball performances and IPL cameos, show that he’s not only ready for the big stage, but he thrives on it. His white-ball struggles remind us he’s still a work in progress, but that’s the beauty of an 18-year-old story. The canvas is wide open.

For fans, every Ayush Mhatre score isn’t just a number on the scoreboard; it’s a glimpse into the future of Indian cricket. If his biography so far is any indication, the next chapters promise to be nothing short of extraordinary.

title: CSK Head Coach 2027
content:
Zaheer Khan is the new head coach of Chennai Super Kings for IPL 2027. CSK announced his appointment on September 21, 2026, as he replaced Stephen Fleming, who had served as the franchise’s head coach since 2009. This marks the first change in the CSK head coach position since Fleming took charge ahead of IPL 2009. 

The appointment makes Zaheer the new CSK head coach 2027, bringing his international playing career and IPL management experience to the role. 

This article covers the Chennai Super Kings head coach history, Zaheer Khan’s experience, his expected role, and what the change means for IPL 2027.

CSK Head Coach 2027: Quick Facts

Who Is the Current Head Coach of CSK?

Zaheer Khan is the current CSK head coach, having been appointed by Chennai Super Kings on September 21, 2026, ahead of the IPL 2027 season. He replaces Stephen Fleming, who stepped down after serving as CSK’s head coach from 2009 to 2015 and again from 2018 to 2026.

The appointment marks Zaheer’s first full-time head-coaching role in the IPL. Before joining CSK, he gained franchise management experience with Mumbai Indians, where he served as Director of Cricket Operations and later Head of Global Development. 

He also worked as a mentor with Lucknow Super Giants. These roles gave him experience in player development, franchise operations and team support structures. Zaheer will now take charge as the new coach of the CSK setup from IPL 2027, with his responsibilities extending beyond the bowling group to the team’s overall coaching and development structure.

What Coaching Experience Does Zaheer Khan Have?

Zaheer Khan’s coaching experience comes mainly from franchise management, player development, and mentoring rather than a previous head-coaching role. His first major post-playing IPL role came with Mumbai Indians, where he was appointed Director of Cricket Operations in December 2018. 

In September 2022, he moved into the role of Global Head of Cricket Development, focusing on talent development across the Mumbai Indians network.

In August 2024, Lucknow Super Giants appointed Zaheer as their mentor for IPL 2025. His role involved guiding the squad and working with the coaching setup, but he was not the team’s head coach.

A director operates at the broader franchise-management level, a mentor provides guidance and support to players and the coaching group, while a head coach carries primary responsibility for the team’s coaching structure, preparation and on-field strategy. CSK therefore represents Zaheer’s first full-time head coach appointment in the IPL.

What Can Zaheer Khan Bring to CSK?

Zaheer Khan brings nearly two decades of IPL experience across playing, captaincy, management and mentoring. His understanding of Indian cricket and franchise systems could help CSK develop its next squad while building a strong team environment. Here’s what he brings as a head coach: 

Bowling Knowledge

Zaheer Khan has been part of the IPL since 2008, across playing, captaincy, management and mentoring roles. His 610 international wickets and 102 IPL wickets underline the experience he can bring to CSK’s bowling group. His understanding of Indian conditions could also help bowlers adapt their lengths, variations and plans to different pitches and conditions.

IPL Management Experience

Zaheer has worked with Mumbai Indians in senior management and with Lucknow Super Giants as a mentor, while also captaining Delhi Daredevils. His first full-time head-coaching role means he now moves from a supporting position to overseeing the wider coaching setup and squad. He has reportedly signed a one-year contract, open to extension.

Understanding Indian Players

His long involvement in Indian cricket and the IPL could help CSK identify domestic talent and develop its next squad. His experience across different IPL environments may also help create a team environment where players can communicate openly and develop together.

The Main Concern

This is Zaheer’s first full-time head-coach role. Managing an entire coaching staff and building team processes is different from mentoring players or contributing to recruitment. His effectiveness in the role can only be assessed once CSK begin playing under him in IPL 2027.

Why Did Zaheer Khan Replace Stephen Fleming?

Stephen Fleming’s departure ended an 18-year association with Chennai Super Kings. After missing the playoffs for three consecutive seasons and finishing 10th in 2025 and eighth in 2026, CSK opted for a change in coaching direction. Fleming’s exit closed one of the longest chapters in IPL coaching, with the franchise now looking to reshape its setup ahead of IPL 2027.

The search for his successor became something of a game of musical chairs, with several names entering the conversation before the position eventually landed with Zaheer Khan. Hemang Badani was among those in contention, while overseas options were also discussed. CSK ultimately settled on Zaheer, whose IPL experience with Mumbai Indians and LSG suited the franchise’s preference for an Indian-led setup. 

His appointment as CSK’s new head coach makes him the third head coach in the franchise’s history and marks his replacement of Stephen Fleming ahead of the 2027 season.

What Is Zaheer Khan’s Salary as CSK Head Coach?

CSK have not officially disclosed Zaheer Khan’s salary as head coach at the time of writing. Reports have discussed possible figures and comparisons with previous CSK coaching packages, but these remain unconfirmed and should not be presented as Zaheer’s actual salary. The franchise has confirmed his appointment on a one-year contract, open to extension, but has not publicly disclosed the financial terms.

Complete List of CSK Head Coaches

Kepler Wessels was the first coach of CSK, taking charge in the inaugural 2008 season when the franchise reached the final. Stephen Fleming then took over in 2009 and became the franchise’s longest-serving head coach. Under Fleming, CSK won five IPL titles and reached nine IPL finals, along with two Champions League T20 titles.

CSK did not compete in the 2016 and 2017 IPL seasons because the franchise was suspended for those two editions. Fleming therefore had two separate spells as head coach, returning when CSK re-entered the competition in 2018.

With Zaheer taking charge in 2027, the CSK head coach list now contains three names. He becomes the third head coach in franchise history and the CSK coach before Zaheer Khan, Fleming, leaves after an 18-year association with the franchise.

Keppler Wessels: CSK’s First Head Coach

Keppler Wessels was the first head coach of Chennai Super Kings, leading the team during the inaugural IPL season in 2008. The former South Africa captain, who had also represented Australia, was appointed on a one-year contract before the tournament.

Under Wessels, CSK won nine of their 16 matches and reached the first IPL final. They finished third in the league stage before defeating Kings XI Punjab in the semi-final. Their campaign ended with a three-wicket defeat to Rajasthan Royals in the final.

Wessels left CSK after that season, with Stephen Fleming taking over as head coach in 2009. Although his tenure lasted only one campaign, Wessels guided CSK to their first final and helped establish the team as an immediate IPL contender.

Stephen Fleming’s Record as CSK Head Coach

Stephen Fleming became the CSK head coach ahead of IPL 2009 and remained in charge through the 2026 season, excluding the two years when CSK were suspended. Across 16 IPL seasons under Fleming, Chennai played 252 matches, winning 139 and losing 110, while three produced no result.

Under his leadership, CSK qualified for the playoffs 11 times and reached nine IPL finals. They won five titles in 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023, while finishing runners-up four times. Fleming also guided CSK to two Champions League T20 titles in 2010 and 2014, taking his overall trophy count with the franchise to seven.

Note: These match figures cover only IPL games played under Fleming. They exclude CSK’s 2008 season under Kepler Wessels and all Champions League T20 matches.

FAQs About the CSK Head Coach

Who is the CSK head coach for IPL 2027?

Zaheer Khan is the CSK head coach for IPL 2027. Chennai Super Kings appointed the former India fast bowler on 21 September 2026, replacing Stephen Fleming. The role marks Zaheer’s first full-time head-coaching position in the IPL after management and mentoring assignments.

When was Zaheer Khan appointed CSK head coach?

Chennai Super Kings appointed Zaheer Khan as their new head coach on 21 September 2026. He will take charge of the team from IPL 2027, following the end of Stephen Fleming’s long tenure with the franchise.

Who did Zaheer Khan replace as CSK coach?

Zaheer Khan replaced Stephen Fleming as CSK head coach. Fleming led Chennai from 2009 to 2015 and again from 2018 to 2026, winning five IPL titles and two Champions League T20 trophies during his time in charge.

Has Zaheer Khan previously worked as a head coach?

No, Zaheer Khan had not previously worked as a full-time head coach in the IPL. Before joining CSK, he held senior management and player-development roles with Mumbai Indians and later served as mentor of Lucknow Super Giants. CSK is his first full-time head-coaching assignment.

Who was the CSK head coach in 2026?

Stephen Fleming was the CSK head coach during IPL 2026. It was his final season in charge before he and the franchise mutually ended their long association. Zaheer Khan was later appointed as his replacement for IPL 2027.

Who was the first head coach of CSK?

Kepler Wessels was the first head coach of Chennai Super Kings. He led the franchise during the inaugural IPL season in 2008, when CSK reached the final before losing to Rajasthan Royals. Stephen Fleming replaced him ahead of IPL 2009.

How many head coaches have CSK had?

CSK have had three head coaches since their first IPL season: Kepler Wessels in 2008, Stephen Fleming from 2009 to 2015 and 2018 to 2026, and Zaheer Khan from IPL 2027. CSK did not compete in 2016 and 2017.

How many trophies did CSK win under Stephen Fleming?

CSK won seven major trophies under Stephen Fleming. These included five IPL titles in 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023, along with two Champions League T20 titles in 2010 and 2014. They also finished as IPL runners-up four times during his tenure.

title: JSK Matches 2025: Full SA20 Schedule, Fixtures, Dates & Venues
content:
The wait is over. The SA20 JSK schedule for Season 4 is finally out, and so is the Joburg Super Kings’ retention list. Fans can now start marking their JSK timings on the SA20 calendar for all JSK Matches 2025, where the team will look to go one step further after three consecutive playoff appearances.

Under Faf du Plessis’ captaincy, JSK leadership has built a strong core with match-winners across departments, aiming to challenge defending champions MI Cape Town for the ultimate prize.

With a balanced squad and a well-planned list of match fixtures, every clash will test their mettle as genuine title contenders.

Match 1: Pretoria Capitals v Joburg Super Kings, Centurion – 27th December 2025

JSK’s campaign begins away from home against Pretoria Capitals at Centurion, a venue known for pace and bounce. Early-season conditions could suit Richard Gleeson, while Akeal Hosein’s variations may be vital in the middle overs.

Faf and James Vince will aim to set the tone with a solid start against a Capitals attack that likes to use the new ball aggressively. It is a tricky opener, but a win here would give JSK confidence heading into a demanding festive period.

Match 2: Durban Super Giants v Joburg Super Kings, Durban – 30th December 2025

For the second game, the JSK will witness a coastal shift to Kingsmead bringing them to conditions favouring spin and slower bowlers. Hosein’s left-arm spin will be central, as will Donovan Ferreira’s ability to counterattack in the middle order.

Durban Super Giants have historically been strong at home, and this clash will test JSK’s adaptability early in the SA20 calendar. Expect Faf to use his experience to rotate the strike and build partnerships, targeting a competitive total on a ground where 160 is often defendable.

Match 3: Joburg Super Kings v Durban Super Giants, Joburg – 1st January 2026

The new year, according to the SA20 JSK schedule, begins at the Bullring. Playing their first game at home JSK will look to repay the fans with fireworks in their second match fixture against Durban Super Giants.

Gleeson and Ferreira, both key members of the Texas Super Kings core, will relish home conditions. Hosein could also be used in the power play to unsettle Durban’s top order. The pace-friendly pitch might bring the quicks into play as well, making this a match for bowlers who can hit hard lengths.

Match 4: Joburg Super Kings v Sunrisers Eastern Cape, Joburg – 3rd January 2026

This is a fixture circled on every JSK fan’s SA20 calendar. Sunrisers Eastern Cape have been JSK’s playoff nemesis for three years running, ending their campaigns in 2023, 2024, and 2025. Breaking that pattern is key to the season’s momentum.

Expect a charged atmosphere and a fiercely contested battle between bat and ball. Faf’s leadership will be crucial here, especially in marshalling his bowlers to contain the SEC’s explosive middle order.

Match 5: MI Cape Town v Joburg Super Kings, Cape Town – 6th January 2026

Facing the defending champions, MI Cape Town at Newlands will be one of JSK’s toughest away match fixtures. Cape Town’s balanced side has the experience and depth to exploit any weakness. The key for JSK will be to neutralise Cape Town’s top order early. Hosein’s spin and Gleeson’s swing could be the weapons of choice. With Faf’s calm approach, JSK will look to post or chase a target with calculated aggression.

Match 6: Joburg Super Kings v Paarl Royals, Joburg – 8th January 2026

Back home at the Wanderers, SA20 JSK schedule calls for a game against Paarl Royals in what could be a high-scoring affair. Vince’s role as a steadying opener will be vital, allowing big hitters like Ferreira to finish the innings with a flourish.

Paarl’s spin-heavy approach might tempt JSK to promote hitters up the order. Expect JSK to leverage home conditions and the altitude advantage to put pressure on Paarl’s bowlers.

Match 7: Joburg Super Kings v MI Cape Town, Joburg – 10th January 2026

A quick turnaround sees JSK host the defending champions just four days after facing them away. This is a prime chance to settle scores and make a statement in front of home fans.

Faf du Plessis, the captain, will look to lead from the front, anchoring the chase or setting up a big total. MI Cape Town’s bowling will test JSK’s depth, but the home advantage and crowd energy could tip the balance.

Match 8: Sunrisers Eastern Cape v Joburg Super Kings, Gqeberha – 14th January 2026

A return fixture against the SEC, this time in Gqeberha, offers another opportunity to turn the tide in this rivalry. SEC’s familiarity with home conditions will be an advantage, but JSK’s revamped core is designed for exactly these high-pressure match fixtures. Expect Faf to use Hosein early to disrupt the SEC’s rhythm and rely on pace to handle the death overs.

Match 9: Joburg Super Kings v Pretoria Capitals, Joburg – 17th January 2026

Heading towards the end of SA20 JSK schedule, we come to the penultimate home match, that sees JSK welcome Pretoria Capitals. This could be a must-win game depending on the points table and other JSK timings on the SA20 calendar.

Vince and Faf’s partnership will be key in setting the platform, while the bowlers will need to execute plans against a Capitals side that likes to play aggressively at altitude. With playoffs looming, JSK leadership will be focused on peaking at the right time.

Match 10: Paarl Royals v Joburg Super Kings, Paarl – 19th January 2026

JSK Matches 2025 conclude with the final league fixture takes them to Paarl, where conditions could slow down and favour spin. Hosein and Ferreira’s spin options will be critical here, while the batters will need to adjust to a less pace-friendly surface. A win here could be the difference between just qualifying and entering the playoffs with momentum.

Playoffs Outlook

  • Qualifier 1 – 21st January 2026
  • Eliminator – 22nd January 2026
  • Qualifier 2 – 23rd January 2026
  • Final – 25th January 2026

If JSK maintain form through the league stage, the playoffs will be their real test. With MI Cape Town holding the title and Sunrisers Eastern Cape having been their stumbling block, the road to the final will not be easy. But with a stronger batting core, a more settled bowling unit, and experienced SA20 team captain leadership from Faf, their chances have never looked better.

JSK Matches 2025

Why This Schedule Works for JSK

The SA20 JSK schedule is spaced well enough to allow recovery and tactical preparation. Home advantage at the Bullring in five matches gives JSK the chance to turn the Wanderers into a fortress. Crucially, back-to-back matches against key rivals like the SEC and MI Cape Town in January will prepare them mentally for playoff intensity.

With the retention of Vince, Hosein, Gleeson, and Ferreira alongside Faf du Plessis, the captain, this team finally has the stability and firepower to challenge the league’s best. The JSK leadership group has been deliberate in building a squad that can handle diverse conditions and high-pressure games.

The JSK Matches 2025 lineup offers both challenges and opportunities. Every fixture on the SA20 calendar is a chance to prove that this is the year they break the playoff curse and lift the SA20 trophy. With strong leadership, a reinforced squad, and the motivation of past near-misses, JSK head into Season 4 not just as participants but as genuine title contenders.

title: Cheteshwar Pujara Retires from Cricket: India’s ‘Wall’ Bids Farewell to an Iconic Career
content:
Team India’s legendry batter and format Chennai Super Kings’ player Cheteshwar Pujara has announced his retirement from all formats of the game.

The news came early on Sunday, when the player took to social media to share a heartfelt note in which he announced his retirement from the game as well.

Pujara was a part of the Indian test setup for over a decade, in which he played 103 games for his side, scoring 7195 runs in them at an average of 43.61. In his illustrious career, he also scored 35 fifties and 19 hundreds.

His highest score of 206* came against England in a home test at Ahmedabad. It was following this knock that he got the title of the next wall of India, a title which was previously credited to Rahul Dravid.

Pujara: defiance personified

However, when we think of Pujara, we just don’t talk about runs. We talk about the serenity with which he operated in the middle. It didn’t matter if he walked in when his team was struggling with quick wickets or after a long partnership. He worked the game on his own pace, which made him a difficult batter to bowl at.

This side of his batting characteristic is highlighted by a stat that it took bowlers 99.4 balls on average to dismiss him in the longest format of the game.

Many of today’s fans remember him from his heroics down under in 2021. But many of us forget that he was the hero even in 2018. One of his famous knocks came in Adelaide, when he walked in to bat and India were already 86/5.

Pujara toiled hard for the next 376 minutes (6+ hours) for his 123 runs, for which he took 246 deliveries. Not only did his innings help his team set a total of 250 runs in the first inning, but also set up a victory which turned out to be crucial in the long run, to help them script history by winning their first ever series win on Australian soil.

Pujara the IPL winner

It will come as a surprise to many, but Pujara has an IPL trophy to his name as well. He was a part of the CSK 2021 team that went on to lift their fourth IPL trophy. Although he didn’t get a chance to feature in that tournament, he was an integral part of the leadership role.

Overall, the Indian stalwart has featured in the IPL with three other teams. He made his IPL debut with KKR in 2009 and then went on to represent RCB between 2011 and 2013. Then he was picked by Punjab in 2014, before CSK gave him another chance in 2021.

All in all, Pujara has featured in 30 IPL games in which he scored 390 runs at an average of 20, with 51 being his highest score. In fact, he also smashed 50 fours and 4 sixes in the course of his IPL career.

title: Super Kings Star Donovan Ferreira Earns South Africa Recall for England Tour
content:
JSK and TSK’s star batter Donovan Ferreira has received an international call-up from the South African cricket team. The player is all set to feature in the away series against England.

Ferreira’s last featured T20I game was way back in December 2024. It came against Pakistan at SuperSport Park, Centurion.

The all-rounder didn’t have the best of series, both with the bat and ball in hand. However, after being dropped from the squad, he had performed amazingly across different leagues.

One of the best examples of his power hitting came in a recently concluded game of The Hundred, where he scored 41 runs off just 15 balls. In that particular inning, he scored 3 fours and 4 sixes, batting at a strike rate of 273.

Apart from that, he has been in phenomenal form in other leagues as well. Following the series against Pakistan, Ferreira showcased his style at home in the SA20 league.

Playing for our beloved Joburg Super Kings, he scored 63 runs at a strike rate of 155.24, with a highest score of 51. Furthermore, picking up 8 wickets in 10 games at an outstanding average of 16 and economy of 5.82, he provided balance in the side as a genuine all-rounder. His best of 3/23 highlighted his knack for breaking partnerships in crucial phases.

This dual skill set, both finishing games with the bat and offering economical overs, has made him a standout in the Super Kings ecosystem. It’s this versatility that ultimately pushed selectors to view him as an international-ready talent.

Later this year, playing for the Texas Super Kings, he established himself as a key middle-order batter. In just nine matches, he piled up 248 runs at a superb average of 41.33, ranking among the top scorers of the season.

What stood out was his ability to consistently provide stability while still accelerating when needed, an asset in the shorter American pitches and pressure-filled chases. His reliability in the middle order was crucial to TSK’s playoff run and showcased his temperament for international-level cricket.

Performances like these, in a league filled with global stars, demonstrated that Ferreira could handle high-pressure environments, making his South Africa call-up a natural progression.

He is not alone, though. Apart from Ferreira, the Protean team has also decided to strengthen their middle order with experience in the form of David Miller.

Along with that, Marco Jansen and Lizard Williams have also recovered from their respective injuries and will be a part of the squad. Keshav Maharaj, who shone in the recently concluded ODI series against Australia, is another name, making his return to the T20I side.

title: Chepauk Revamp: MA Chidambaram Stadium Gears Up for T20 World Cup 2026
content:
MA Chidambaram Stadium, popularly known as Chepauk, is undergoing massive renovation ahead of the hectic Chennai Super Kings Match schedule in 2026. Despite the start of the domestic season being weeks away, the ground is going to get a new outfield and drainage system.

This Chepauk revamp started after the ground was slated to host the bulk of international action next year. According to a report by CricTracker, the ground is likely to host games in the upcoming T20 World Cup in 2026. Hence, the home venue of the Chennai Super Kings is all set for a makeover.

Chepauk renovation plan

The Tamil Nadu Cricket Association released a video showing that everything around the field, except the middle part, is being dug up. Apparently, they are putting in a brand new drainage system and a new field. The improved drainage should get games going sooner after it rains.

These changes to the field and drainage should make for better cricket at one of India’s oldest stadiums. It has been a witness to many historic matches, which include both IPL and international games; however, as it is going for a complete revamp, it hopes to add many more chapters to the glorious history of IPL and Indian cricket.

The Chepauk revamp will be a time taking process, and with India’s domestic season just around the corner, it will be interesting to see how things take place from here on.

History of Chepauk

Chepauk, officially the M. A. Chidambaram Stadium, has been the heartbeat of Chennai cricket since 1916. As India’s second-oldest international ground, it has witnessed history unfold for over a century. In 1934, Chepauk hosted its first Test match, and in the same year, India’s first Ranji Trophy game was played here. It later became the stage for India’s first-ever Test victory in 1952, a moment that cemented its place in cricketing folklore.

Over the decades, Chepauk has seen unforgettable contests—from the dramatic tied Test against Australia in 1986 to high-voltage IPL finals that electrified fans. Renamed in 1986 after M. A. Chidambaram, a visionary administrator, the ground has retained its charm through eras of cricketing change.

What makes Chepauk truly iconic isn’t just the matches, but its atmosphere. The roar of the Chennai crowd, the weight of its history, and its emotional connection with fans make it a fortress of Indian cricket.

A fortress for the Lions

Chepauk is also the home ground of Chennai Super Kings, who have won the IPL 5 times. 2025 was not a good season for them, in fact, it was their worst as they finished last with just 4 wins out of 14 matches.

Generally, the ground is considered a fortress, but not last season. Chennai was only able to win 1 out of their seven home games, which was one of the biggest reasons behind their poor outing as well.

Even Tamil Nadu, which uses the ground as its home venue, didn’t play a single game here last season. Coimbatore acted as their home ground for the last season, and most likely it will remain to be the case for this season as well.

title: Shivam Dube picked for India’s Asia Cup 2025 Squad
content:
Chennai Super Kings’ powerhitter and highest runs scorer of the 2025 IPL season, Shivam Dube, has been named in India’s squad for the Asia Cup 2025.

The player has been a regular part of the Indian for over a year now. He was a part of the 2024 World Cup Squad that lifted the title in West Indies. Even in the final, he played a handy knock of 27 runs from 16 deliveries that helped his team post a competitive total.

Dube’s Role in Indian Team

Dube is no longer seen as the hitter of the hard ball. He has grown into a middle-order batsman for the Indian team. He brings stability and can adapt to any situation, which is something the team values a lot.

Now, as the 2025 Asia Cup approaches, everyone is looking at Dube, who is 31. He can hit big shots, he knows the game well and can bowl useful medium pace.

This combination makes him someone who can turn the game around for India. He gives the team flexibility and depth, and his presence in the team makes the opposition think twice.

 T20I Stats of Shivam Dube

Perfect for Asian Conditions

Dube is good against spin, which is a big plus for the Asia Cup, which will be played in Sri Lanka, where spin is a key factor. In the IPL, he has regularly attacked spinners and changed the game in a few overs.

Also, he’s a left-handed batsman. With many right-handers in India’s middle order, Dube offers variety, disrupting the opposition, especially against left-arm spinners or leg-spinners.

While Dube’s sixes are attention-grabbing, his medium pace bowling gives India another option, which is always useful in white-ball cricket. In close games, even a couple of good overs can be game-changing.

Asia Cup matches are tough with low scores and battles in the middle overs. This is where Dube does well, gets the team out of tough situations, handles pressure and finishes strong. He’s done this with Chennai Super Kings and has shown glimpses of it playing for India.
