title: Faf du Plessis Leads from the Front: Texas Super Kings’ Captain in MLC 2025
content:
The Faf du Plessis Texas Super Kings 2025 campaign is a story of unmatched consistency and leadership that spans continents. From Chennai to Joburg and now Texas, Faf du Plessis has not just represented but personified the Super Kings brand.

In MLC 2025, he reinforced his status as the franchise’s golden child, combining tactical sharpness with fearless batting to guide the Texas Super Kings (TSK) deep into the playoffs yet again.

Across leagues, Faf’s legacy has been built on standout performances, like his impressive Faf du Plessis MLC stats and game-changing captaincy that make him the heartbeat of every team he leads. Whether it’s the IPL, SA20, or the USA’s Major League Cricket, his calm leadership and match-winning contributions shine through.

Faf’s MLC Captaincy Journey: Consistency Across Seasons

Since the launch of Major League Cricket (MLC) in 2023, Faf has been at the helm for Texas Super Kings. His leadership ensured TSK consistently stayed among the league’s top contenders:

  • 2023 Season: Qualified for playoffs, finished in the top 2.
  • 2024 Season: Playoff qualification secured, finished 3rd.
  • 2025 Season: Another top 2 finish, making it three in a row under Texas Super Kings captain Faf du Plessis.

Under his watch, TSK have reached the Qualifier 2 in each of the three seasons, making them one of the MLC’s most consistent sides. While the title remains elusive, Faf’s leadership has crafted a strong, competitive outfit in the league.

MLC 2025: Faf’s Finest Hour with Texas Super Kings

The MLC 2025 season showcased everything that makes Faf du Plessis Texas Super Kings 2025 a headline act. With a squad frequently bolstered by local talents and often missing overseas stars, Faf stepped up both with the bat and as a tactician.

Despite missing just one game due to a precautionary injury rest, he was instrumental in TSK’s campaign.

Batting Brilliance:

  • Matches Played: 10
  • Runs Scored: 468
  • Hundreds: 2
  • Fifties: 3
  • Average: 50+
  • Strike Rate: 170+

When you look at the Faf du Plessis MLC stats, his contribution in MLC 2025 alone sums up his impact, leading by example and consistently delivering under pressure. His performances earned him a place among the tournament’s top scorers and highlighted his ability to produce TSK match-winning knocks at crucial junctures.

Faf the dependable batter

In one memorable game during the qualification round, with key players missing, TSK posted a modest 166, with Faf’s half-century single-handedly holding the innings together.

And in the highly anticipated TSK vs SFU 2025 clash, Faf unleashed a breathtaking century, scoring a brilliant hundred as TSK piled up 198 batting first, only to suffer a heartbreaking loss despite his heroics.

Yet, fate had other plans. After finishing in the top 2, TSK’s Qualifier 1 was abandoned due to rain, handing Washington Freedom a direct passage to the finals.

And in Qualifier 2, despite dominating for large parts of the game, Kieron Pollard, a nemesis for Super Kings fans, turned the match on its head as MI New York knocked TSK out before going on to win the finals.

When it comes to MLC 2025 captain stats, Faf’s leadership numbers remain among the league’s best with a playoff qualification percentage of 100 percent and a win rate that speaks volumes about his tactical acumen. 

Faf’s ability to empower his players became a standout feature of the 2025 season. He gave Donovan Ferreira the freedom to express himself as a finisher, a move that paid off with crucial cameos under pressure.

Equally important was how he brought the best out of young Afghan spinner Noor Ahmad, who finished with an impressive 15 wickets in 12 matches.

Even with a depleted squad missing key overseas players like Nandre Burger and Daryl Mitchell, Faf led TSK with relentless intent. His ability to inspire belief and fight tooth and nail despite the odds was a testament to his remarkable leadership.

The Super Kings DNA: Faf’s Bond with CSK and SA20

Faf du Plessis is no stranger to playoff heartbreaks, but also to unforgettable match-winning moments with the Super Kings family.

  • CSK 2018 Qualifier 1: The iconic knock against Sunrisers Hyderabad where Faf’s unbeaten 67 dragged CSK from the jaws of defeat into the finals, a win that eventually set up their title run.
  • CSK 2021 Final: A defining 86-run masterclass against Kolkata Knight Riders that helped CSK lift their fourth IPL title, underlining his big-match prowess.

The bond extended into SA20, where with Joburg Super Kings, Faf ensured playoff qualification in all three seasons. His best finish in the SA20 came in the 2024 edition, guiding JSK to a third-place finish. Once again, his consistency and leadership played pivotal roles in shaping their campaign.

Captain Across Continents: The Super Kings’ Golden Child

Be it in India, South Africa, or the USA, Faf’s Super Kings journey has been nothing short of remarkable. Few players have carried the franchise’s flag across leagues with such commitment and success.

What sets him apart?

  • Leadership Stability: Calm, composed, and an exceptional reader of the game.
  • Batting Under Pressure: Whether chasing or setting totals, Faf’s hunger to deliver at crunch moments is second to none.

title: “Am I Really Jealous of You?": Harbhajan’s Honest Take on Ashwin’s Direct Question
content:
The debate around Harbhajan Ashwin jealousy has simmered quietly for years, fueled more by perception than proof, and often shaped by the shifting tides of Indian cricket. While not a typical on-field rivalry, it’s a story born out of transitions, comparisons, and legacy.

Harbhajan Singh and Ravichandran Ashwin, two of India’s most prolific off-spinners, have long been central to fan discussions and debates, with speculation often outweighing facts. Recently, a candid on-camera conversation between the two brought much-needed clarity.

On a recent episode of Ravichandran Ashwin’s YouTube podcast, a viewer’s comment triggered a raw and revealing moment. The viewer implied that Harbhajan harboured jealousy towards Ashwin, a remark that set the stage for a conversation far deeper than cricket.

Ashwin and Harbhajan: A Candid Conversation on Jealousy

When the interview was announced, everyone was aware that there was going to be some conversation around the topic of Harbhajan Ashwin jealousy. And that is what happened as well. Ashwin, never one to shy away from directness, brought up the fan’s accusation with nuance.

  • “Before I allow you to answer that, let me clarify something. People look at everything from their perspective… This comment that you are jealous of this person who is interviewing you today, what would that be about?”

Harbhajan, taken slightly aback, responded with a calm but pointed question of his own:

  • “Do you think I am jealous of you? You are sitting here with me today. We have spoken at length. Do you think I am that kind of person?”

Many expected a light-hearted or diplomatic response from Ashwin. What followed, however, was an unusually grounded reply that won over both critics and fans:

  • “Even if you were jealous at one point, it is justified. That is my point. I would never take it the wrong way because we are all human. Naturally, it is bound to be like that.”

Ashwin’s answer highlighted the human side of elite sports, a space where competition, insecurity, and transition often walk hand in hand. Harbhajan, in turn, opened up about the inevitable thoughts that arise when a younger, potentially long-term replacement enters the picture.

  • “When you came into the side… you know that this could be the guy who could be playing for a longer period of time… it’s competition. At that time, somewhere in my mind, even if just a small thought must have come, like ‘I have to step up my game.’”

It was a moment of vulnerability that peeled back the media-filtered layer of player dynamics. Harbhajan’s maturity and Ashwin’s acceptance of emotional complexity gave the internet a rare insight into how legends handle legacy.

No Jealousy between Harbhajan and Ashwin: Just Misconceptions

Interestingly, this isn’t the first time Harbhajan addressed public speculation about his equation with Ashwin. Back in 2024, the Turbanator released a video on his YouTube channel where he categorically denied any ill will:

  • “If there is a standoff between me and Ashwin or if there was ever any fight, quarrel or disagreement, I would be the first person to go up to him and ask what the issue is. But it was never like this and it will never be like this… He has been a phenomenal bowler for India. I am very happy for his achievement.”

The former Indian spinner, addressing the Harbhajan Ashwin jealousy saga, further pointed out that the narrative around their relationship has been exaggerated by social media and public perception:

  • “If people twist things on Twitter and make it seem as if I have a problem with Ashwin, then it’s their point of view. I am a little vocal about the fact that the pitches on which India play cricket are not good cricket, there is a lot of spin on these tracks and matches get over within two and a half days.”

His critique of Indian pitches, a topic Ashwin has also weighed in on, was misinterpreted by some as a jab at the newer generation of spinners. The clarification puts to rest a lingering misunderstanding.

Two Careers, Two Journeys, One Shared Legacy

While the talk of Harbhajan Ashwin jealousy makes for clickable headlines, a deeper look into their careers reflects more collaboration than conflict.

  • Harbhajan Singh made his Test debut in 1998 and went on to become one of India’s most successful off-spinners. His record includes 417 Test wickets in 103 matches, 269 ODI wickets in 236 matches, and several match-winning spells that shaped Indian cricket in the 2000s. He was instrumental in India’s victories at home and abroad and played a crucial role in the 2001 series against Australia, still regarded as one of the greatest performances by an Indian bowler.
  • Ravichandran Ashwin, who recently retired from Test cricket, took over the baton and elevated the role of a modern-day spinner. He finished his career with 537 Test wickets in 106 matches, 156 ODI wickets in 116 games, and 72 T20I wickets in 65 matches. More than just a bowler, Ashwin evolved into a thinking cricketer, engineering dismissals, decoding batters, and mastering formats from Chennai to Sydney.

While Harbhajan was raw aggression mixed with classical off-spin, Ashwin became the tactician who constantly adapted. Each spinner dominated their era, and India was richer for it.

In the end, what the world saw as rivalry, was just evolution. And through honesty, both players may have finally buried one of Indian cricket’s most persistent myths: that one man’s rise means another’s bitterness. 

Let the numbers speak. Let the legacy remain.

title: Dewald Brevis vs AB de Villiers: Is 'Baby AB' Ready to Carry the Legacy?
content:
Dewald Brevis as Baby AB; the tag has followed him since his U-19 days, and in 2025, it feels more real than ever. With his explosive performances for the Chennai Super Kings, the South Africa team player is now making headlines not for what he could become, but for what he’s already doing.

The Dewald Brevis stats from IPL 2025; 225 runs in six matches at a staggering strike rate of 180, peppered with 17 sixes; reflect a player stepping out of the shadow of comparison and into the spotlight of legacy.

Dewald Brevis CSK debut

CSK’s 2025 campaign wasn’t one for the ages, but it would’ve been far worse without Dewald Brevis. Coming in as a replacement for the injured Gurpajneet Singh, Brevis didn’t just fill a spot; he ignited a spark. Despite joining a struggling setup, he delivered two match-winning knocks, playing with an audacity that’s been sorely missing in CSK’s middle order.

Dewald Brevis arrived at Chennai Super Kings like a late‑season cyclone and left bowlers picking debris out of the boundary cushions. Signed as a mid‑season injury patch, “Baby AB” stitched together 225 runs in just six innings, rattling them off at a blistering strike‑rate of 180.

His blitzkrieg 57 from 23 against Gujarat Titans set the tone, followed by rapid‑fire fifties versus KKR and a pair of 42‑run cameos that turned stalemates into thrillers. Apart from one RCB duck, Brevis treated every delivery like it owed him runs—averaging 37.50 while redefining CSK’s middle‑order tempo.

In a season of mixed fortunes for the Super Kings, his fearless stroke‑play offered a glimpse of a yellow future built on audacious power and youthful swagger.

His fearless intent and attacking game turned around stagnant chases and brought life to a batting lineup that often looked devoid of answers. The CSK star batsman showed that his potential wasn’t just a label; it was action, aggression, and impact in the IPL’s toughest moments.

Why is Brevis compared to AB de Villiers?

Dewald Brevis is fast becoming the face of the CSK franchise, a rare distinction for a young overseas talent. There is a lot of AB de Villiers comparison for Brevis, because he brings a fearless, unorthodox flair that captures fans’ imagination.

AB wasn’t just a player; he was a spectacle, a match-winner, and a crowd-puller who symbolised loyalty and consistency. Brevis, still early in his journey, echoes that same energy with his ability to shift momentum in a few deliveries and his comfort against both pace and spin.

CSK’s faith in him, coupled with his natural aggression and maturity beyond his years, has placed him in a league of his own. He’s not just another recruit; he represents the next-gen CSK, one that blends youth with legacy. If nurtured right, Brevis could become to CSK what AB once was to RCB: irreplaceable.

At just 22, Dewald Brevis isn’t merely aiming for records. He’s carrying a culture. A franchise known for its undying belief in its players has now found in Brevis a new torchbearer. The Super Kings have always backed players who show fight and heart. Brevis fits that mould perfectly.

In a squad marred with injuries, a disjointed bowling attack, and a half-performing batting unit, Brevis became a bright spot. More importantly, he became an embodiment of what the Super Kings stand for: loyalty, grit, and growth.

Is Brevis the next AB de Villiers?

AB de Villiers, through his years at RCB, became the heartbeat of the franchise. Alongside Virat Kohli and Chris Gayle, he formed a batting trio that lit up the IPL for a decade. Yet, despite all the runs and memories, the silverware eluded them. The individual brilliance of AB was unquestionable, but the team dynamic often fell short.

Brevis finds himself at a unique crossroads. He has the blueprint of AB’s genius to emulate, the 360-degree play, the fearless shot-making, and the calm in chaos. But what sets him apart is the system around him. The Super Kings franchise isn’t just a team; it’s a family that rallies together, both in glory and grind.

Brevis is ready to shine

Brevis’s rise with CSK opened doors beyond franchise cricket. His IPL exploits earned him a Test debut against Zimbabwe, marking his official transition into South Africa’s full-time setup.

Currently part of the Tri-Series involving Zimbabwe, New Zealand, and South Africa, Brevis is no longer just a prodigy; he’s a name on the team sheet that matters.

Much like AB, who transitioned seamlessly between formats, Brevis has shown he’s ready to shoulder South Africa’s batting responsibilities. From the bright lights of IPL to the tough grind of international cricket, he’s walking a path trodden by legends.

How can Super Kings culture help Brevis?

The difference between Dewald Brevis and many other young talents is clear: environment. The Super Kings franchise, unlike many others, thrives on long-term vision and player-centric leadership.

Players aren’t judged on a bad season or a rough patch. Instead, they’re nurtured, given time, and made to feel part of a larger mission.For Brevis, this culture has been transformative. He has found a cricketing home that allows him to blossom.

AB de Villiers did it all on his own for RCB. Brevis, with the Super Kings backing, has a chance to become a legend with a team that believes in collective legacy.

Carving a Legacy of His Own

At 22, it’s tempting to drown Brevis in comparisons. But the truth is, while the ‘Baby AB’ tag opened doors, his performances have kicked them down. If AB de Villiers became the heart of RCB, Dewald Brevis is shaping up to be the soul of the Super Kings franchise.

He’s shown he can lift a sinking team, adapt across leagues, and thrive in formats as varied as T20 and Test cricket. The blend of audacity and composure he brings is rare, and it’s why fans and pundits alike believe he’s ready to carry forward not just AB’s legacy, but forge one that belongs entirely to him.

A Chance to Rewrite and Replicate Greatness

Dewald Brevis as Baby AB wasn’t a moniker handed out lightly; his fearless mindset, dynamic range of shots, and uncanny resemblance in technique make every AB de Villiers comparison feel valid.

But now, beyond emulating AB’s style, Brevis is poised to craft something even more special. AB, a once-in-a-generation talent, dazzled the IPL with his 360-degree game and unmatched genius, yet a title remained elusive despite his brilliance. 

That gap in IPL history presents a rare opportunity for Brevis. With his seamless integration into the Super Kings setup, a franchise that thrives on unity, belief, and long-term vision, he stands at the brink of forging a legacy built not just on personal milestones but on iconic team triumphs.

The values and culture that surround him now offer the perfect backdrop for him to chase what AB couldn’t. For CSK, the global Super Kings family, and South African cricket, Brevis is the face of a future where talent meets legacy, setting the stage for unforgettable success stories.

The Next Icon of the IPL?

If the IPL is a stage for stars, then Dewald Brevis is on his way to becoming its next icon. The Super Kings have given him a canvas, and Brevis is painting innings after innings with strokes of genius.

He’s more than a baby AB; he’s the future of a franchise, a beacon for South African cricket, and a player who, backed by the right system, could become one of the most iconic batters the league has ever seen.

AB de Villiers showed the world what’s possible when talent meets determination. Dewald Brevis is showing what happens when talent, determination, and a rock-solid team culture come together. And for CSK, the Super Kings family, and South Africa, that’s a legacy worth carrying forward.

James Vince’s retention has added a huge layer of finesse to JSK’s top order. The elegant right-hander from England is a veteran of T20 leagues worldwide; be it the Big Bash, T20 Blast, or The Hundred, Vince has always delivered with grace and consistency.

The southpaw has featured in 443 T20 games and scored a gigantic amount of 12461 runs with an average of 32 and a strike rate of 136. His ability to find gaps, rotate strike, and suddenly accelerate with well-timed strokes makes him a complete package in the power play.

Paired with Faf at the top, Vince forms a formidable opening duo. His presence allows Faf to pace his innings while Vince goes for early boundaries.

JSK saw glimpses of his brilliance last season, and in 2026, they showed complete faith in him by putting him on the SA20 retention 2026 list. Expect Vince to be the stabilising force in those crucial high-pressure chases and powerplay assaults that define a title run.

Akeal Hosein: Spin Control & Mid-Overs Weapon

Akeal Hosein is a strategic retention and a valuable asset in JSK’s bowling blueprint. A seasoned left-arm spinner from the West Indies, Hosein is known for his economical spells and ability to pick up key wickets in the middle overs. He brings something every T20 team craves control and calmness under pressure.

Having already been part of the Texas Super Kings setup, Hosein now strengthens the Super Kings’ family further by becoming a key cog in the Joburg unit.

His SA20 numbers are impressive, with tight spells that often turn the tide of matches. Not only does he slow down the opposition, but he also forces batters to take risks, resulting in wickets at crucial junctures.

In the slower surfaces of Johannesburg and Durban, Hosein’s role becomes even more critical. He’s not just a bowler; he’s JSK’s insurance policy during the mid-innings grind.

Richard Gleeson: Firepower with the New and Old Ball

Fast, fierce, and reliable, Richard Gleeson has been retained to give JSK bite in their pace attack. The English speedster has made a name for himself in T20 leagues as a dependable death-over specialist and an effective new-ball bowler. He generates a sharp bounce and hits the deck hard, troubling batters who fancy swing and spin.

Gleeson adds a different flavor to the bowling unit. With Nandre Burger or Gerald Coetzee expected to return in the auctions or drafts, Gleeson complements the local pace battery with his experience. He’s particularly lethal at the backend of innings, where his slower balls and yorkers have closed games in JSK’s favour before. By securing him early in the JSK retention strategy, Joburg have made sure their fast-bowling stocks are in safe hands, especially in a format where death bowling often decides the fate of matches.

Donovan Ferreira: Homegrown Match-Winner

Donovan Ferreira’s retention by JSK doesn’t come as a huge surprise. In the recent years, his rise is one of the brightest stories in the SA20 league. Picked by JSK in the very first season, Ferreira has been a loyal soldier of the franchise and is now rewarded with a place in the JSK retained players 2026 list.

Over the last three seasons, he has emerged as the perfect middle-order weapon, someone who can shift gears effortlessly and win matches single-handedly.

Ferreira’s finishing skills have drawn comparisons to the likes of David Miller. His ability to clear boundaries with ease and bowl part-time spin gives the team flexibility. More importantly, his calmness in tense situations has made him one of Faf’s go-to players.

With home support and franchise continuity, Ferreira is poised to take the next leap, from promising youngster to team backbone. If JSK are to break their title jinx, Ferreira’s contributions will be crucial.

A Look Back at Former Seasons

Looking back at JSK’s journey over the past three seasons, one thing is clear: they’ve been a consistent force, always in the playoff mix but narrowly missing out on the final push.

In the inaugural 2023 season, under the steady leadership of Faf du Plessis, JSK made it to the semi-finals but fell just 14 runs short in a high-octane chase of 215 against eventual champions Sunrisers Eastern Cape (SEC). 

The following year, in 2024, they reached Qualifier 2, only to crumble under scoreboard pressure; they were bowled out for 142 in pursuit of yet another 215. The pattern repeated in 2025, with a loss in the Eliminator once again to SEC, this time falling 32 runs short in a chase of 185.

While the results were heartbreaking, Faf’s calm captaincy, strategic game awareness, and ability to extract the best out of his players have kept JSK consistently within reach of glory; a sign of a strong foundation.

With Faf du Plessis’s leadership, the composure of James Vince, the control of Akeal Hosein, the speed of Gleeson, and the x-factor of Ferreira, Joburg have retained a team with both experience and flair.

Add in potential auction picks like Leus du Plooy and others, and this side becomes an even more dangerous outfit. Last season’s heartbreak in the Eliminator was tough, but it lit a fire within the franchise. This year, with a stable core and smart additions, JSK look ready to go all the way.

The fans are dreaming. The management is plotting. The players are preparing. Will 2026 finally be the year the Joburg Super Kings go from contenders to champions?

title: CSK's Anshul Kamboj Strikes on Test Debut, Removes Ben Duckett to Open Account
content:
Anshul Kamboj will never forget July 23, 2025.Playing his debut Test match for India at Old Trafford, the young right-arm seamer from Haryana claimed his maiden international wicket by dismissing England’s Ben Duckett for 94.

The wicket turned out to be more than just a personal milestone. It was a crucial breakthrough in the game, halting England’s strong start and breaking a threatening partnership.

But things didn’t start off smoothly for Kamboj. He looked a bit off-rhythm early in the innings, conceding runs at a brisk rate. In his first spell, the player only bowled a spell of 4 overs. There were a few nervy overs, and the English batters, especially Duckett, were quick to capitalise.

However, what separates a promising cricketer from the rest is the ability to bounce back. And bounce back Kamboj did. He came back to bowl in the 39th over and got his breakthrough.

Duckett was dismissed caught behind to Dhruv Jurel. Although the ball was not very extraordinary, what really caught the batter by surprise was the extra bounce generated by Kamboj. This reminded us of something that Dhoni had said earlier in IPL 2025.

Dhoni Praises Kamboj

MS Dhoni had earlier praised the youngster’s unique bowling traits. “Kamboj is someone who doesn’t get swing, but he gets some seam movement. The ball hits you harder than the speed gun suggests,” he said. “He has taken the responsibility and he is someone who can bowl good yorkers.”

And that is exactly what he did in Manchester—stayed patient, stuck to his plans, and eventually earned a breakthrough that could very well mark the beginning of a long international journey.

Kamboj’s rise to the Indian team was fast-tracked after an impressive IPL 2025 season with Chennai Super Kings. In his debut IPL season, the pacer played 8 matches, picked up 8 wickets, and delivered a match-winning spell of 3/13 against Gujarat Titans. His average of 21.50 and strike rate of 16.13 spoke volumes about his control, while an economy of 8.00 under pressure situations made him a trusted asset for CSK in crunch games.

More Than Just a Debut for Kamboj

What makes Kamboj’s debut even more memorable is the historic parallel he now shares with Anil Kumble. He became the first Indian Test debutant at Old Trafford in 35 years, and interestingly, both Kamboj and Kumble have taken all 10 wickets in a first-class innings earlier in their careers.

From domestic cricket to IPL and now a dream debut at Old Trafford, Anshul Kamboj’s story is just getting started.

title: Texas Super Kings’ MLC 2025 Journey Ends: Season Recap and Key Performances
content:
The Texas Super Kings 2025 season recap is a tale of dominance, heartbreak, and individual brilliance. Despite finishing in the top two and delivering consistent performances, TSK fell short in the playoff stages yet again. With standout player stats, including impactful knocks and bowling spells, the season was packed with highlights.

From thrilling wins to narrow losses, and high-profile battles against teams like MI New York and MI Cape Town, this MLC season summary captures the roller-coaster journey of the Texas Super Kings and their top players.

1st Match: Texas Super Kings vs MI Cape Town, Oakland Coliseum

The season opener had TSK facing MI Cape Town in a high-octane clash. Batting first, Devon Conway anchored the innings with a solid 65 while Calvin Savage provided late fireworks with a 34-ball 50, taking TSK to 185.

MI Cape Town stumbled early but found resistance through Monank Patel’s 44-ball 62. Despite a late surge from their middle order, MI fell short by three runs. TSK kicked off their MLC 2025 campaign with a thrilling win, showcasing early form and intent.

2nd Match: Texas Super Kings vs Los Angeles Knight Riders, Oakland Coliseum

TSK continued their strong start by posting 181 in the second game, courtesy of Daryll Mitchell’s gritty 33-ball 36 and useful cameos from the middle order. LAKR’s chase unravelled quickly as Noor Ahmad weaved his magic with a mesmerising 4-wicket haul.

Bowling them out for just 121, TSK stamped their authority with a convincing 60-run victory. The bowling unit, led by Noor, proved their worth early in the season, giving Texas Super Kings a dominant 2-0 start.

3rd Match: Texas Super Kings vs Seattle Orcas, Oakland Coliseum

Batting first, TSK struggled to get going, but Saiteja Mukkamala’s 30 off 23 helped them post a modest 153. However, the bowlers turned the game on its head. Seattle Orcas crumbled under relentless pressure, bundled out for just 60 runs.

Nandre Burger, Noor Ahmad, and Zia-ul-Haq Muhammad picked up three wickets apiece, scripting one of the most lopsided wins of the MLC 2025 season. TSK’s bowling attack firmly established itself as the tournament’s most lethal unit.

4th Match: Texas Super Kings vs San Francisco Unicorns, Grand Prairie Stadium

Faf du Plessis lit up the stage with a blazing 100, powering TSK to 198. However, the San Francisco Unicorns returned the favour with an annihilating chase.

Finn Allen’s explosive 78 off 35 and Matt Short’s brutal 61 off 29 saw them chase down the target with 23 balls to spare. It was a wake-up call for TSK as their bowling unit, so dominant earlier, faced its first real test against the power-packed Unicorns lineup.

5th Match: Texas Super Kings vs Washington Freedom, Grand Prairie Stadium

TSK’s batsmen fired again, posting a massive 220/6, spearheaded by Faf’s quickfire 69 off 31. However, Washington Freedom staged a remarkable chase. Mitchell Owen’s blistering 89 off 52 and Andries Gous’ unbeaten 80 off 45 stunned the Super Kings.

Adam Milne took three wickets, but the bowlers couldn’t stem the flow of runs as Washington Freedom sealed the win with two balls to spare. The loss exposed TSK’s vulnerability in defending big totals against fearless batting lineups.

6th Match: Texas Super Kings vs Los Angeles Knight Riders, Grand Prairie Stadium

TSK bounced back strongly against LAKR, piling up 196/8. Shubham Ranjane top-scored with a 45-ball 70, while Donnovan Ferreira provided a quickfire 43 off 21. Akheil Hossein and Noor Ahmad shared two wickets apiece, choking LAKR’s chase and restricting them to 144/7.

It was a much-needed win for the Super Kings, restoring confidence in both their batting depth and bowling prowess after two consecutive losses.

7th Match: Texas Super Kings vs MI New York, Central Broward Regional Park

Faf du Plessis struck a magnificent unbeaten 103 off 53 balls, ably supported by Donnovan Ferreira’s explosive 53 off just 20 deliveries, taking TSK to a commanding 223. MI New York fought valiantly, with Kieron Pollard hammering a 39-ball 70, but fell short at 184/9.

Akeal Hossein was the standout with his sensational figures of 4-1-15-3. This match solidified TSK’s reputation as a powerhouse team with match-winners across departments, especially against top-tier opposition.

8th Match: Texas Super Kings vs Washington Freedom, Central Broward Regional Park

In a rain-shortened 5-over contest, TSK scored an imposing 87/2, thanks to Shubham Ranjane’s rapid 39 off 14 and Donnovan’s brutal 37 off 9. Washington Freedom struggled to 44/4 in their chase, giving TSK a commanding victory despite missing skipper Faf.

The win underscored TSK’s depth and adaptability in tricky conditions, proving they could perform even without their talismanic captain in the mix.

9th Match: Texas Super Kings vs San Francisco Unicorns, Central Broward Regional Park

San Francisco Unicorns set a target of 149, anchored by Matt Short’s unbeaten 80 off 63. TSK’s chase wobbled early at 43/3, but a middle-order fightback brought them close. A rapid 39 off 20 set them up for a tight finish.

Needing 13 off the final over and three off the last ball, TSK fell agonizingly short by a single run. This heartbreaking loss was a reminder of how fine margins defined their MLC 2025 journey.

10th Match: Texas Super Kings vs Seattle Orcas, Central Broward Regional Park

TSK’s top order fired once again, with Faf scoring a brilliant 91 and Shubham Ranjane contributing an unbeaten 65. They set a challenging 188. Seattle Orcas crumbled in response, dismissed for 137, as Adam Milne ripped through with a sensational five-wicket haul.

This dominant display sealed TSK’s top-two finish in the league stage, capping off a season where they showcased depth, resilience, and star power across all departments.

Qualifier 1: Texas Super Kings vs Washington Freedom, Grand Prairie Stadium

Fate intervened cruelly as the crucial Qualifier 1 against Washington Freedom was washed out without a ball being bowled.

With Washington Freedom finishing higher on the table, they advanced directly to the finals, forcing TSK into a do-or-die Qualifier 2.

The washout denied TSK a direct shot at the title and added extra pressure heading into the knockout clash with MI Cape Town.

Qualifier 2: Texas Super Kings vs MI Cape Town, Grand Prairie Stadium

TSK posted 166/5, with Faf leading the charge with a steady 59 and Akheil Hossain’s surprising 55 off 32 providing a crucial lower-order boost. MI Cape Town faltered early but regrouped with Kieron Pollard’s blistering 47 off 22 and Nicholas Pooran’s unbeaten 52 off 32.

Chasing 69 off the last five overs, MI’s power-hitting proved decisive. This painful loss ended TSK’s 2025 campaign, echoing the same playoff heartbreak from the previous season.

TSK Player Stats 2025: Key Performers

Top Batters:

  • Faf du Plessis: 468 runs in 10 matches, including two centuries and three fifties at a strike rate of 170.
  • Shubham Ranjane: 268 runs in eight innings, two fifties, striking at 160.
  • Donnovan Ferreira: 248 runs in 10 matches, a staggering strike rate of 213.

Top Bowlers:

  • Noor Ahmad: 15 wickets in 12 matches, TSK’s spin spearhead.
  • Adam Milne: 14 wickets in seven matches, including a five-wicket haul.
  • Akheil Hossain: 10 wickets in seven matches and vital contributions with the bat.

Season Summary

The Texas Super Kings’ 2025 season was a gripping saga of explosive batting, lethal bowling, and moments of high drama. Finishing in the top two with seven wins in ten matches, they displayed depth in both batting and bowling departments. However, rain-affected playoffs and heartbreak in crucial moments derailed their championship aspirations.

Texas Super Kings top players like Faf du Plessis, Shubham Ranjane, Donnovan Ferreira, Noor Ahmad, Adam Milne, and Akheil Hossain became cornerstones of the campaign. TSK’s ability to bounce back after defeats, their high-scoring games, and dominance over powerhouses like MI New York made them one of the standout teams of the MLC 2025 season. Yet, the elusive title remains a goal for the coming years.

title: Sanju Samson CSK News: Is RR Captain Replacing MS Dhoni at CSK?
content:
The latest Sanju Samson CSK news has sent shockwaves across the IPL fanbase. The buzz about Sanju Samson to CSK is no longer just a passing rumour; insiders suggest there might be some real substance to this speculation.

As the cricketing world looks forward to IPL 2026, talks about MS Dhoni’s replacement, the CSK 2026 squad, and CSK’s latest transfer news have intensified. And right in the middle of it all is Sanju Samson, a dynamic batter, a wicketkeeper, and a seasoned IPL captain.

Sanju Samson to CSK: More Than Just a Rumour?

For weeks now, social media platforms have been abuzz with IPL 2026 rumours, particularly linking Sanju Samson with the Chennai Super Kings (CSK). However, this time, the chatter isn’t baseless.

According to Cricbuzz, CSK’s top brass have confirmed their interest in bringing the Kerala batter into the yellow brigade. A senior CSK official, who is closely involved in the franchise’s decision-making, admitted to the possibility of a Sanju Samson move to CSK. He said:

“We are definitely looking at Sanju. He is an Indian batter who is a keeper and an opener. So if he is available, we will certainly have a look at the option of having him in our fold. Who we will trade him with, we have not taken that call because the matter has not gone that far. But yes, in principle, we are interested.”

This confirmation places Sanju among the top targets for the CSK 2026 squad, potentially filling the void once Dhoni finally steps away from the playing field.

Why Sanju Samson Makes Sense for CSK

If Thala does retire, now or shortly, CSK will need an Indian wicketkeeper-batter who can anchor the innings and keep up with the demanding nature of IPL leadership. Sanju checks all those boxes and presents himself as the perfect MS Dhoni Replacement. Samson has:

  • Proven IPL experience as captain
  • Explosive batting abilities at the top of the order
  • Wicketkeeping skills
  • Marketable personality; fits into the CSK brand appeal

With the CSK 2026 squad in mind, adding Sanju would be a calculated masterstroke, potentially giving them the edge in the post-Dhoni era.

The Dhoni Factor: Will MS Continue in IPL 2026?

MS Dhoni has remained a central figure in CSK’s success story for over a decade. The question on every fan’s mind is whether MS Dhoni’s replacement will be unveiled in IPL 2026.

Dhoni himself has said he’ll take about 6-7 months to decide on his future, but it’s already known that Ruturaj Gaikwad will continue as captain. However, Samson’s move adds flair to the MS Dhoni replacement and retirement talks.

The Chennai management sees Sanju Samson as a natural fit; a wicketkeeper who can bat up the order and, if needed, lead the team. Even if Dhoni stays, having a backup keeper-batter like Samson seems a strategic move.

CSK latest transfer news: Who’s on the Table?

The biggest question surrounding the Sanju Samson to CSK move is: Who will CSK offer in return? Samson, retained by RR at ₹18 crore, commands a hefty price tag.

Theoretically, CSK’s captain Ruturaj Gaikwad, also retained at ₹18 crore, could be a like-for-like swap. But with head coach Stephen Fleming reiterating Gaikwad’s long-term captaincy role, this seems unlikely.

A more realistic trade scenario floated by insiders involves a package deal; CSK could offer Cash along with seasoned spinner Ravichandran Ashwin (the latter returning to RR). This move could benefit both franchises:

  • CSK gets: Sanju Samson (keeper-batter, potential leader)
  • RR gets: Ravichandran Ashwin (senior bowler) & Cash.

Notably, CSK’s history with player trades is limited. One such precedent was the cash trade of Robin Uthappa from RR in 2021; a move that worked well for CSK. Hence, it remains to be seen what developments take place in CSK’s latest transfer news over the coming weeks.

Can Sanju Samson really leave Rajasthan?

The Sanju Samson CSK news has also been fueled by growing unrest within the Rajasthan Royals (RR) camp. The tipping point? His recent injuries and rise of other superstars among the ranks.

IPL 2025 saw Samson missing three games due to a finger injury, and surprisingly, Riyan Parag, not senior names like Nitish Rana or Yashasvi Jaiswal, was named stand-in captain. This unexpected move sparked rumours of internal politics in the RR dressing room.

To make matters more intriguing, reports suggest that Yashasvi Jaiswal, who’s been RR’s batting mainstay, has been eyeing the captaincy role himself. KKR is reportedly interested in bringing him on board after their unsuccessful 2025 campaign under Ajinkya Rahane.

As if all of this was not enough, the batter who replaced Samson in the top order, went on to create history. Yes, the player we are talking about is Vaibhav Suryavanshi, who made a solid impact in his debut season.

The Royals have also leveraged Samson’s brand value massively; reportedly earning ₹35-40 crore per season via endorsements linked to his ₹18 crore retention. Now, with Samson seemingly unhappy and seeking a new challenge, CSK sees a golden opportunity.

Samson’s Social Media Hints: Adding Fuel to the Fire

Another factor that contributed to the latest CSK transfer news frenzy was Sanju Samson’s cryptic social media activity. They have played a crucial role in adding fuel to the fire of these IPL 2026 rumours.

The Indian opener posted a photo featuring him and his wife, captioned “Time to MOVE..!!” with a prominent yellow line in the background. This had fans speculating if this was a nod towards Chennai Super Kings.

Adding to the intrigue, Samson’s agent, Prashobh Sudevan, liked a post suggesting a potential move to CSK, making fans believe there’s no smoke without fire.

Royals’ Changing Guard: Is Samson Still Needed at RR?

With the emergence of young talents like 14-year-old Vaibhav Suryavanshi and the ever-consistent Yashasvi Jaiswal, many believe RR’s future leadership lies elsewhere. Injuries and inconsistent form marred Samson’s IPL 2025 season.

While he’s been a vital part of the Royals’ setup, the franchise may see this as an opportunity to rebuild with younger leaders. It’s a narrative that further boosts the possibility of the Sanju Samson to CSK switch becoming a reality.

How Does IPL 2026 Look for CSK?

The IPL 2026 rumours promise to be an exciting chapter for CSK. With a blend of proven stars and emerging talent, the team looks well-equipped for a fresh era. Youngsters like Ayush Mhatre, Dewald Brevis, Urvil Patel, and Anshul Kamboj have shown immense potential in domestic circuits and franchise leagues.

Mhatre’s aggressive batting, Brevis’ all-round prowess, Urvil’s dynamic keeping abilities, and Kambhoj’s fast bowling make them future stars in the making.

If CSK can integrate these names alongside their seasoned campaigners, including Ruturaj Gaikwad and possibly Sanju Samson, the franchise could well be on track for another golden period in their IPL journey. The mix of youth and experience could see CSK remain a formidable force even in the post-Dhoni era.

What’s Next?

While nothing is official yet, all signs indicate that this saga will intensify in the coming months. The IPL trade window and auction will provide more clarity on whether Sanju Samson will replace MS Dhoni at CSK or if this remains another IPL 2026 rumour that fizzles out.

For now, CSK fans can dream, and RR fans can speculate. But one thing’s certain: the IPL 2026 build-up has started with a bang, and Sanju Samson CSK news will continue to dominate headlines.

title: CSK New Comer Anshul Kamboj Joins India Squad Ahead of 4th Test vs England
content:
Fast bowler Anshul Kamboj, a rising star from Chennai Super Kings (CSK), has been added to the India Test squad as a cover for Arshdeep Singh, who is currently nursing a minor injury. The upcoming 4th Test match between India and England is scheduled to begin on July 23 at Old Trafford, Manchester.

Arshdeep, who was expected to play a key role, suffered a cut on his bowling arm during a practice session. As a precaution, the selectors have brought in Anshul Kamboj, who has been making headlines with his performances both in domestic cricket and the IPL.

Anshul recently impressed in the India A tour of England, picking up five wickets and scoring a solid half-century in the unofficial Tests against England Lions. His all-round show caught the attention of selectors, and with Arshdeep unavailable, Kamboj was the natural choice for a backup.

A Year of Ultimate Hardwork and Performances Secure Anshul Kamboj a place in the India Squad

The 24-year-old seamer from Haryana had a memorable IPL 2025 season with CSK, where he took eight wickets in eight matches at an average of 21.50 and an economy of 8. Bought for INR 3.40 crore, Kamboj showed great promise with the ball and proved to be a valuable addition to the CSK squad.

Earlier this year, he made history in the Ranji Trophy, becoming just the third bowler ever to take all 10 wickets in a single innings. Playing for Haryana, he registered jaw-dropping figures of 10/49 against Kerala, placing him in an elite list alongside Premangshu Chatterjee and Pradeep Sunderam.

Born on December 6, 2000, in Karna, Haryana, Kamboj is a seam-bowling all-rounder. In his first-class career, he has taken 79 wickets at an average of 22.88, along with two five-wicket hauls and one ten-wicket haul. He also has 74 wickets across List A and T20 cricket.

With his ability to bowl consistently and bat lower down the order, Anshul brings balance and energy to any squad. His selection is a proud moment not only for him but also for CSK and domestic cricket fans in India. Now, all eyes will be on whether he gets a chance to make his India Test debut at Old Trafford.

The Chennai Super Kings batter has not played a professional match in over three months, ever since he sustained an elbow injury during the IPL. His absence as Ruturaj Gaikwad CSK captain was deeply felt by fans and the franchise alike, as he was expected to lead from the front.

Though he later recovered and was selected in the India A squad for their tour of England, he did not feature in any of the four-day games. title: Ravindra Jadeja's Lone Battle in Lord's Test Goes in Vain; England Defeat India by 23 Runs
content:
India’s hopes of a historic win at Lord’s were dashed on Day 5 of the third Test, as England edged out a thrilling 22-run victory to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series. Despite the defeat, the match will be remembered for Ravindra Jadeja’s heroic innings, where he scored his maiden fourth-innings Test fifty, a knock filled with grit, patience, and character.

Chasing 193 for victory, India were rocked early on the final day. Starting at 40/3, they slipped further to 71/5, losing key batters including KL Rahul and Washington Sundar. The pressure was immense, but Jadeja walked in and took control when his team needed him most. At 82/7, the match seemed all but over, but the left-hander had other ideas.

World No.1 Test Allrounder Ravindra Jadeja’s Grit Almost Shook Stokes-led England at the Lord’s Test

The No. 1-ranked Test All-rounder for a record time, Jadeja built a fighting partnership with Nitish Kumar Reddy and then with Jasprit Bumrah, who held firm for 54 balls in a vital lower-order stand. Together, they pushed India past the 100-run mark and kept hopes alive. Jadeja’s 50 came off 150 balls, a display of resilience in challenging conditions. As wickets kept falling around him, he remained calm and determined.

Mohammed Siraj joined Jadeja as the last man in, and the pair gave England a real scare. The duo added crucial runs, taking India to 170. Just 23 runs away from victory, a loose shot from Siraj saw him dismissed in the 75th over, leaving Jadeja stranded at the other end, unbeaten and heartbroken.

Earlier in the match, Jadeja had also contributed a solid 72 in the first innings, helping India post 353. England replied with 298, and India then bowled them out for 192 in their second innings, with Washington Sundar leading the attack with a 4-fer. But the final chase proved just out of reach.

This match also marked Jadeja’s fourth consecutive 50+ score in the series, joining elite company alongside Rishabh Pant and Sourav Ganguly. It was his 26th Test fifty overall, and his seventh in England.

While the result didn’t go India’s way, Jadeja’s performance was a standout, a true lone warrior’s effort that nearly turned the match. Sadly, he was left stranded as his brilliant knock went in vain.

title: Ayush Mhatre Slams Maiden Youth Test Century Against England, Silences Critics
content:
India Under-19 captain Ayush Mhatre made headlines with a stunning century on Day 1 of the first Youth Test against England at the Kent County Cricket Ground in Beckenham. The 17-year-old opener from Mumbai displayed maturity and flair well beyond his age, scoring a brilliant 102 off just 115 balls—his maiden hundred in Youth Test cricket.

After a quiet run in the recent Youth ODI series, where he managed only 27 runs in four matches, Mhatre answered critics in emphatic fashion. From the first over, he was in complete control, showcasing his wide range of strokes and exceptional timing. His innings featured 14 classy boundaries and two towering sixes, with one maximum coming during a dominant spell where he took apart the English bowling attack.

Mhatre reached his century in style, punching Archie Vaughan, son of former England captain Michael Vaughan, for a boundary off the first ball of the 36th over. It was a poetic moment, symbolic of the young Indian’s rising stature on the international youth stage.

CSK’s Young Star Ayush Mhatre Leads from the Front with Sublime Century to Provide a Solid Foundation

The innings began with a short-lived 17-run stand with fellow opener Vaibhav Suryavanshi (14 off 13), but Mhatre soon found solid support from Vihaan Malhotra, with whom he built a commanding 173-run second-wicket partnership. Malhotra contributed a composed 67 from 99 deliveries, allowing Mhatre to play freely.

Mhatre eventually fell for 102 in the 38th over, when Archie Vaughan finally got his revenge, but not before the Indian skipper had laid a rock-solid foundation for his team.

This century adds to a growing list of achievements for Ayush Mhatre, who is rapidly emerging as one of India’s most promising young batters. Earlier this year, he made his first-class debut for Mumbai in the Irani Cup final. His talent further shone in the IPL 2025, where he was signed by Chennai Super Kings as an injury replacement for Ruturaj Gaikwad. In a standout performance, he hammered a stunning 94 off 48 balls against Royal Challengers Bengaluru, hitting nine fours and five sixes.

title: CSK’s Road to IPL 2026: Lessons from 2025 & Future Game Plan
content:
As the dust settles on IPL 2025, Chennai Super Kings find themselves at a defining crossroads. A team that has dominated the IPL narrative for over a decade now faces the task of rebuilding, recalibrating, and reigniting its winning fire. The 2025 season offered a reality check; CSK can no longer afford to live in the shadows of past glories.

With Ruturaj Gaikwad now leading the franchise and with MS Dhoni likely entering his final IPL season, the franchise must strike a balance between sentiment and strategic direction.

In many ways, IPL 2026 presents CSK with an opportunity to evolve into a modern, data-driven, youth-fueled unit while retaining the cultural ethos that has made them five-time champions.

This is the CSK IPL 2026 game plan, one that takes stock of past mistakes and maps out a bold and visionary path forward.

IPL 2025 Review: Brutal Truths CSK Must Acknowledge

CSK’s 2025 season was underwhelming by all metrics. Injuries, inconsistency, and outdated approaches resulted in a 10th-place finish, with only four wins in 14 matches. But deeper than the numbers, it was the decision-making and strategy flaws that hurt the most.

1. Break Free from Outdated Strategies

CSK has long been admired for its loyalty and experience-first model. However, in a rapidly evolving T20 ecosystem, adhering to past formulas can be fatal. IPL 2025 proved this.

The management banked heavily on experienced Indian batters like Rahul Tripathi, Deepak Hooda, and Vijay Shankar. All three, unfortunately, failed to deliver. Their strike rates were poor, their intent was outdated, and their inability to anchor or accelerate in crunch games cost CSK big.

Similarly, overseas acquisitions like Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra, once pivotal, looked completely off-colour in the 2025 campaign. Conway struggled with strike rotation and fluency. Rachin was either underutilised or miscast in the playing XI.

2. Let Go of Emotions

CSK has always been about sentiment, but the game now demands clarity over nostalgia. Devon Conway, Ravichandran Ashwin, and even Rachin, former CSK favourites, failed to adapt. The franchise has to now move away from emotional investments and make decisions purely based on performance and team balance.

That means tough calls must be taken, even if it means parting ways with former title-winning players. The future belongs to those willing to embrace change.

3. Look Beyond MSD

There’s no denying MS Dhoni’s stature and aura. But CSK cannot afford to build its entire strategy around a 44-year-old icon, no matter how great he is.

While Dhoni’s experience and tactical acumen remain invaluable, his on-field impact is diminishing, and 2025 saw signs of fatigue, with dropped catches, slower movements, and increased reliance on “Impact Player” status.

The franchise must look to create a team that wins games independently of Dhoni’s presence, allowing him to play the mentor role rather than the match-winner. That will be Dhoni’s greatest legacy: to leave behind a team that can succeed without him.

CSK Team Building: The Core is Established

If 2025 brought pain to CSK, it also brought promise. Amidst the gloom, a new core emerged, one that looks ready to take the baton forward.

Ruturaj Gaikwad (Captain)

Classy, composed, and now a county cricketer for Yorkshire, Gaikwad’s evolution from opener to leader has been seamless. Despite an injury-hit 2025, he is CSK’s long-term captain and spiritual successor to Dhoni.

Ayush Mhatre (Opener)

The 17-year-old sensation lit up the 2025 season with 240 runs at a strike rate close to 190. He is fearless, adaptable, and the future of CSK’s top order.

Shivam Dube (Middle-Order Muscle)

A consistent performer, Dube offers a mix of power-hitting and part-time bowling. He will be crucial to CSK’s middle-overs punch.

Dewald Brevis (Overseas Finisher)

The South African prodigy scored 225 runs in six matches and was CSK’s most explosive middle-order presence. He’s un-droppable now.

Ravindra Jadeja (Vice-Captain & All-Rounder)

Jadeja remains the glue that holds the team together. His experience, fitness, and dual skills make him the X-factor, especially in Chepauk conditions.

Noor Ahmad & Matheesha Pathirana (Bowling Spine)

The Afghan left-arm mystery spinner and the Sri Lankan slinger are CSK’s bowling future. Their wicket-taking ability in the middle and death overs is a foundation to build upon.

Khaleel Ahmed (Left-Arm Pace)

A valuable Indian pacer who offers variety and powerplay penetration.

This core ensures that CSK doesn’t need to scramble at the 2026 auction. What they now need are complementary players to plug the gaps and ensure they have flexibility across conditions.

Dhoni’s Legacy Plan: A Final Push for Glory

With all signs pointing to IPL 2026 being Dhoni’s final season, CSK’s motivation will be sky-high. The management, players, and fans will want to give their Thala a fitting farewell, but not through just sentiment.

If Dhoni is to walk away with a sixth title, the franchise must ensure:

  • He isn’t overburdened physically or mentally
  • He plays as a finisher or Impact substitute, not as a full-time keeper
  • Leadership is fully in Gaikwad’s hands, allowing Dhoni to mentor from the background.

The best way to honour Dhoni is not by overplaying him, but by allowing the franchise he built to now stand on its own feet. That would be the ideal culmination of the Dhoni legacy plan.

IPL 2026 Roadmap: Smart Investments, Ruthless Decisions

Going into the IPL 2026 auction, CSK must follow a clear and bold roadmap:

1. Invest in Multi-Dimensional Players

Players like Mitchell Owen, Dasun Shanaka, Michael Bracewell, or even an experienced Rashid Khan-type all-rounder would bring balance and flexibility. Target players who can contribute to two departments.

2. Offload Spent Forces

It’s time to move on from players who peaked years ago. Whether it’s Tripathi, Hooda, Shankar, or underwhelming overseas picks like Conway or Rachin, there must be no room for sentiment.

3. Retain and Back Youth

CSK’s young brigade has arrived, and they must be given backing. Mhatre, Brevis, Noor, and even lesser-used talents like Urvil Patel or Anshul Kambhoj can play key roles with proper grooming.

4. Prioritise Death Bowling Depth

Pathirana and Khaleel are solid, but another reliable Indian or overseas death bowler must be added. This is one area where CSK struggled immensely in 2025. Expect them to retain Nathan Ellis.

5. Build a Strong Bench

A strong bench ensures injuries don’t derail the campaign like in 2025. CSK should look at wild card players, under-22 Indian talents, and associate nation stars who bring spark.

CSK’s future strategy isn’t about reinvention, it’s about evolution. The franchise has the building blocks of a championship-winning team. What it now needs is clarity, ruthlessness, and forward-thinking.

The CSK IPL 2026 game plan isn’t just about winning another trophy. It’s about creating a system where the team can win with or without Dhoni, where strategy replaces sentiment, and where the next generation takes centre stage.

IPL 2026 isn’t just another season. It’s the beginning of CSK 2.0. And if they play their cards right, it might just end with one last trophy lift, and the perfect sunset for a certain #7.

title: Ravindra Jadeja Stats: All-rounder Becomes First Player with this WTC Double Record
content:
Indian cricket star Ravindra Jadeja has made history! He’s now the first-ever cricketer to score over 2,000 runs and take over 100 wickets in the important ICC World Test Championship (WTC). This is a truly special achievement for an all-rounder.

Jadeja reached this big milestone during the ongoing second Test match against England at Edgbaston. He played a fantastic innings, scoring 89 runs. He only needed 79 runs to reach 2,000 runs in the WTC, and he did it beautifully, especially when India was in a tricky spot at 211 runs for 5 wickets.

Ravindra Jadeja World Test Championship (WTC) Numbers Shine Bright

Looking closely at his performance in the WTC, Jadeja has played 41 matches. In these games, he has scored a total of 2,010 runs. His batting average is a very respectable 37.92. What’s more, he has hit three centuries (scores of 100 or more) and thirteen half-centuries (scores of 50 or more).

But Jadeja isn’t just a great batsman. With the ball, he has taken an impressive 132 wickets! His bowling average is also very good, at just over 25 runs per wicket. This includes six times where he took five wickets in an innings, and six times where he took four wickets in an innings. These numbers truly show how valuable he is as an all-rounder in Test cricket.

A Strong Partnership and a Special Connection with Edgbaston

In the current match, Jadeja formed a vital 203-run partnership with captain Shubman Gill, who scored a massive 269. This stand was instrumental in helping India post a commanding total of 587/10. Though Jadeja missed out on a well-deserved fifth Test century, falling for 89, his contribution was pivotal.

Interestingly, this is Jadeja’s second double-century partnership at Edgbaston. In 2022, he shared a 222-run stand with Rishabh Pant, where both batsmen hit centuries. No other Indian pair has recorded two 200-plus partnerships at this venue in Tests.

Ravindra Jadeja Stats: Jadeja’s Overall Test Career and His Success Against England

Playing his 82nd Test, Jadeja’s knock of 89 runs pushed his overall Test run tally to 3,495 at an average of 35.30, with four centuries. With his left-arm spin, he has also claimed 324 Test wickets at an average of just over 24, including 15 five-wicket hauls.

Against England specifically, Jadeja boasts an excellent record. This innings took his Test runs against England to 1,156, including two centuries. Notably, England is the only country against which he has scored over 1,000 Test runs. He also has 71 wickets against England. His ability to perform strongly with both bat and ball against a top Test nation further solidifies his status.

This achievement underlines Ravindra Jadeja’s consistent impact and his unique place in Test cricket history.

title: Top 5 Wild Card Picks CSK Could Target for IPL 2026 Auction
content:
As the 2026 IPL season draws closer, there’s an undeniable buzz around one team, Chennai Super Kings. With Ruturaj Gaikwad at the helm, a reinvigorated mix of youthful exuberance and experienced heads, and the legacy of MS Dhoni guiding them from the shadows, CSK is gearing up to be the most exciting side in IPL 2026.

The Super Kings may have had a forgettable 2025 campaign, but it gave birth to CSK young talent like Ayush Mhatre, Dewald Brevis, Noor Ahmad, and Matheesha Pathirana stepping into core roles.

With Shivam Dube, Khaleel Ahmed, and the ever-reliable Ravindra Jadeja forming the crux, the team is almost locked in, with eight starters already identified. And if Dhoni chooses to play as an impact player, the team’s leadership and lower-order firepower only get stronger.

There are, however, a few open positions that CSK needs to address smartly ahead of the CSK auction 2026. Assuming Sanju Samson doesn’t join, despite swirling rumours, the management will look to fill five critical roles using their purse wisely and strategically.

And this is where the CSK wild card players IPL 2026 discussion comes into focus.

CSK’s Available Slots and Needs

With Noor Ahmad and Pathirana as guaranteed overseas starters, CSK will be looking to fill the remaining roles with either impactful overseas players or underrated Indian talents. Here’s what they need:

  1. Foreign Opener: An alternative or complement to Ayush, given Devon Conway’s uncertain form.
  2. Foreign All-Rounder: To offer balance in the middle order.
  3. Fast Bowler or Third Bowling Option: To rotate with Khaleel and Pathirana.
  4. Experienced Finisher Who Can Bowl: Someone who can close innings and offer a couple of overs.
  5. Experienced Spinner: To share duties with Noor and Jadeja.

Let’s now dive into the top 5 wild card picks CSK could target for IPL 2026, based on form, versatility, and tactical need.

1. Mitchell Owen – Explosive Opener and Bowling Option

Mitchell Owen is Australia’s biggest T20 wild card right now and fits the IPL wild card rules perfectly: young, explosive, and under the radar when it comes to IPL auctions.

  • BBL 2025/26 Performance: 452 runs in 11 innings with two centuries at a strike rate of over 200, playing a crucial role in Hobart Hurricanes’ maiden title win.
  • MLC 2025 Impact: Already lighting up the Major League Cricket with 288 runs and 14 wickets in 7 matches.

What makes Owen irresistible for CSK is his dual skill set. A top-order batter who can hit from ball one and medium-pace bowling that brings balance, he can open with Ayush Mhatre, offering explosive starts and occasionally replacing Pathirana or Dube as an Impact Player.

He represents everything CSK needs in an underdog player with high upside, and with most teams overlooking him for bigger Aussie names, CSK can snag him for a steal.

2. Sikandar Raza – The Experienced Finisher Who Ages in Reverse

Raza might be 38, but his game seems to be age-proof. Having featured in leagues across the globe, Sikandar Raza is the definition of a T20 mercenary who wins you matches.

  • T20 Career: 298 matches, 6080 runs, 183 wickets
  • Batting Strike Rate: 139.5
  • Bowling: Off-spin with the ability to take wickets in the middle overs

CSK’s lineup is packed with power hitters like Dube, Brevis, and Ruturaj, but they lack a versatile finisher who can adapt and bowl 2-3 overs. Raza fills that void. His global experience, tactical acumen, and cricketing intelligence would make him the perfect stabiliser if CSK is 90/4 in the 13th over or 170/3 in the 16th.

While other teams chase big names, CSK can quietly slip Raza into their plans and turn him into a match-winning asset, a move reminiscent of how they used Shane Watson or Moeen Ali in the past.

3. Quinton de Kock – The Redemption Pick

Once a force to reckon with, Quinton de Kock has seen his stocks fall in the IPL after a poor 2024 season with LSG, scoring just 250 runs in 11 games. With rumours suggesting he may go unsold in the 2026 IPL auction, CSK could pounce and breathe new life into the South African southpaw’s career.

  • IPL Career: 3309 runs in 115 matches
  • T20 Career: Nearly 10,000 runs, including his international career.

Quinton can be CSK’s backup or rotation opener for Ayush or Owen. With his ability to accelerate in the powerplay and keep wickets if needed, he could be a low-risk, high-reward buy, especially if CSK opt to give Dhoni more flexibility.

He might not be CSK’s first-choice overseas pick, but as a backup or floater who has a big-game temperament, he’d be one of the smartest CSK wild card players IPL 2026.

4. Michael Bracewell: All-Round Utility and Tactical Depth

New Zealand’s Michael Bracewell is a genuine floater, a multi-skilled player who fits the CSK mould to perfection. Whether it’s batting at 4, bowling off-spin in the powerplay, or being the sixth bowling option, he’s tailor-made for Dhoni-Ruturaj style gameplay.

  • T20 Career Stats: 3234 runs, 83 wickets, strike rate 140+
  • Role: Middle-order aggressor and off-spinner

Bracewell could be used as a matchup-based player against left-heavy teams or slower tracks, such as Chepauk. He would allow Jadeja to play a more specialised role while providing batting depth and finishing strength in the bottom half of the innings.

If CSK is looking for a budget-friendly tactical overseas pick, Bracewell is their man. He brings calmness, utility, and most importantly, consistency.

5. Rashid Khan – The Dream Spinner Acquisition

This may be wishful thinking, but recent rumours suggest Gujarat Titans could release Rashid Khan following a poor IPL 2025 season by his standards. If that happens, CSK should go all-in.

  • T20 Stats: 643 wickets in 477 matches
  • Batting: 2589 runs as a lower-order dasher

Despite the presence of Noor Ahmad and Jadeja, having Rashid and Noor bowling in tandem would make CSK virtually unplayable in the middle overs. Rashid also adds value as a deadly finisher with the bat, capable of scoring 30 off 10 in crucial moments.

Imagine a CSK bowling unit featuring Rashid, Noor, Pathirana, Khaleel, and Jadeja – that’s five potential wicket-takers. Add Ruturaj and Brevis in the field, and you’ve got a championship-calibre unit.

If Rashid is released, expect a bidding war to ensue. But if CSK wins, they instantly become title favourites.

CSK’s Auction Game Plan Must Be Smart and Strategic

Heading into the 2026 CSK auction, the franchise already has a powerful core in place. With Ruturaj Gaikwad leading a youthful side backed by Dhoni’s mentorship, the Super Kings just need a few strategic wild card entries to complete the puzzle.

Here’s a quick recap of the Top 5 CSK wild card players IPL 2026:

  1. Mitchell Owen: Explosive opener with bowling ability
  2. Sikandar Raza: Veteran finisher and utility bowler
  3. Quinton de Kock: Experienced opener and backup keeper
  4. Michael Bracewell: Tactical middle-order all-rounder
  5. Rashid Khan: Spin king and lower-order gamechanger

In a tournament where success hinges on balance, adaptability, and bench strength, these wild-card picks could be the difference between a playoff spot and a trophy.

The IPL 2026 underdog players could very well become the headline makers, and knowing CSK’s history with turning low-key names into superstars, this year’s wild card strategy might just be their winning mantra.

title: Will Ruturaj Gaikwad Return as Captain in IPL 2026? What We Know So Far
content:
Ruturaj Gaikwad IPL 2026 captaincy buzz has already started swirling in the cricketing world, and rightfully so. Ever since MS Dhoni stepped down as captain of Chennai Super Kings (CSK), handing over the baton to his trusted opener, Ruturaj, has been seen as the chosen one, the Dhoni successor CSK fans have been waiting for.

But two seasons later, uncertainty looms. From a successful personal campaign in IPL 2024 to a heartbreaking injury in 2025, Gaikwad’s leadership journey has been nothing short of a rollercoaster.

With the 2026 edition of the IPL approaching fast, fans and analysts alike are wondering: Will Ruturaj Gaikwad return as captain in IPL 2026?

Let’s break down the past two seasons, Ruturaj’s captaincy record, the emerging young stars of CSK, trade rumours, and what Dhoni’s own words suggest for the future of Ruturaj leadership at CSK.

Ruturaj Gaikwad’s Initial Stint as Captain

Ruturaj Gaikwad joined the elite list of CSK new captainin 2024, just days before the IPL kicked off. The announcement marked a significant moment in CSK’s history, as it finally transitioned from the Dhoni era.

And Gaikwad didn’t disappoint. He scored 583 runs in 14 matches, including a scintillating century and four fifties, asserting his prowess not just as a batter but also as a composed leader.

Despite his personal brilliance, CSK narrowly missed the playoffs, losing out to RCB on Net Run Rate (NRR). The 2024 season, however, gave fans and the franchise a glimpse of what Ruturaj Gaikwad’s IPL captain potential could truly look like in 2026.

Ruturaj Gaikwad: The Stats Behind the Leader

As the new CSK captain, let’s break down Ruturaj’s leadership records to understand the full picture:

As Captain (2024–2025):

  • Matches: 19
  • Wins: 8
  • Losses: 11

Overall for CSK:

  • Matches: 71
  • Innings: 70
  • Runs: 2502
  • Average: 40
  • Strike Rate: 137
  • 50s: 20
  • 100s: 2

In just 70 innings, Ruturaj has already amassed over 2500 runs, a testament to his class and consistency. Currently signed with Yorkshire in English county cricket, he’s sharpening his game further in overseas conditions.

With Jadeja continuing as the bowling spearhead and Ruturaj taking over long-term batting duties, CSK’s leadership group for 2026 looks both stable and dynamic.

IPL 2025: The Injury That Changed Everything

Heading into IPL 2025, the expectations were high. Gaikwad retained his place as captain of the Chennai Super Kings, and the team looked to build on their 2024 progress. Unfortunately, fate had other plans.

Ruturaj sustained a fracture just five games into the tournament, ruling him out for the remainder of the season.

By that time, CSK had won just one of their first five matches, a mix of injuries and out-of-form senior players hampering any momentum. Gaikwad had already scored two fifties in that short span, showing signs of good form, but his injury turned out to be a massive blow to the team’s morale and planning.

With Gaikwad sidelined, none other than MS Dhoni, listed as an “uncapped player” to save team balance, stepped up to lead the side. However, the campaign spiralled, and CSK finished as the wooden spooners, winning just 4 out of 14 matches, their worst season in IPL history.

Dhoni’s Assurance: A Team for Gaikwad

After their final match of IPL 2025, where CSK salvaged a win, Dhoni made a statement that resonated with every CSK supporter:

“When Ritu comes back next year… he doesn’t have to worry about too many things.”

This clear endorsement not only reassured fans about Ruturaj’s return as captain but also underlined that the franchise was building a future-ready team, the perfect environment for Ruturaj Gaikwad’s IPL 2026 captain ambitions to flourish. It was vintage Dhoni: selfless, forward-thinking, and loyal to the core.

The Rise of the Young Brigade

While 2025 was forgettable for CSK in terms of results, it gave birth to a promising young core that could complement Ruturaj Gaikwad’s leadership in the future.

1. Ayush Mhatre – The Firestarter

At just 17, Ayush Mhatre stepped up in Ruturaj’s absence and announced his arrival in style. Coming in as a replacement, he scored 240 runs in 7 innings at a jaw-dropping strike rate of 188.

His 94 off 48 against RCB was arguably CSK’s most exciting innings of the season. His impact at No. 3 allows Ruturaj to slide into a flexible anchor or finisher role in IPL 2026.

2. Urvil Patel – The Power Opener

Given a three-match window, Urvil made every ball count with a strike rate of 213. He provided blistering starts and showcased a fearless brand of cricket. Although his role was limited in 2025, his retention for IPL 2026 suggests that he will be part of the larger leadership puzzle.

3. Dewald Brevis – The Middle-Order Messiah

The South African prodigy delivered on the hype. Brevis racked up 225 runs in 6 games at a strike rate of 180, hitting 17 sixes. His ability to shift momentum and bat with intent revolutionised CSK’s middle order in Ruturaj’s absence. The “Baby AB” effect is real, and his presence will take the load off Ruturaj’s shoulders.

4. Noor Ahmad – The Silent Assassin

While the batters were making noise, Noor Ahmad quietly became CSK’s most lethal weapon with the ball. The Afghan spinner picked up 24 wickets in 14 matches, emerging as the leading wicket-taker for CSK in IPL 2025. His control in the middle overs and ability to take crucial wickets made him indispensable and a frontrunner to lead CSK’s spin attack in IPL 2026.

5. Anshul Kamboj – The Emerging All-Round Asset

Not far behind was Anshul Kamboj, who made his presence felt with 8 wickets in 8 matches. While his figures might seem modest, his knack for breaking partnerships and bowling tough overs earned praise from both management and fans. As an all-around option, Kamboj could play a bigger role in CSK’s balance in the upcoming season.

Rumours: Sanju Samson to CSK?

Adding spice to the IPL captain news for 2026, there are whispers of Sanju Samson joining CSK in a money-plus-player trade deal. If it goes through, the former RR captain could take over wicket-keeping duties and open the batting, similar to his role in India’s T20I team.

However, according to team insiders and Dhoni’s public statements, Ruturaj remains CSK’s first-choice leader. With Gaikwad being part of the franchise since 2020 and commanding immense respect within the group, Sanju’s arrival is unlikely to dethrone him, though it would boost CSK’s depth and experience.

The Verdict: Will Ruturaj Gaikwad Be CSK’s Captain in IPL 2026?

Yes. All signs point to Ruturaj Gaikwad returning as CSK captain in IPL 2026.

From Dhoni’s emotional backing to the emergence of a support system around him, Gaikwad’s leadership tenure is far from over. His calm demeanour, tactical nous, and ever-improving batting credentials make him the ideal candidate to lead CSK into a new era.

While challenges await, especially managing young talent and integrating stars like Samson, Gaikwad’s patient yet attacking leadership style suits CSK’s DNA. The 2026 season could be his true test: fit, experienced, and with a rejuvenated squad at his disposal.

The Ruturaj Gaikwad IPL 2026 captain saga is one of promise, trust, and unfinished business. If 2024 was his arrival and 2025 a setback, then 2026 is set to be his redemption arc. With CSK’s core of young guns, overseas firepower, and the legacy of MSD watching over, Ruturaj Gaikwad is not just leading a team; he’s continuing a legacy.

Whether you’re following CSK’s new captain 2026 debates or searching for the next big thing in IPL captain news 2026, one name remains front and centre: Ruturaj Gaikwad.

title: MS Dhoni Files Trademark for 'Captain Cool’: What It Means for His Brand Legacy
content:
Cricket legend MS Dhoni has reportedly filed a trademark for his famous nickname, ‘Captain Cool’. This news has sparked considerable interest, highlighting a smart move in Dhoni’s already impressive branding strategy. But what exactly does this Dhoni nickname trademark mean for one of India’s most beloved sports figures?

For a long time, ‘Captain Cool’ has been the perfect way to describe Dhoni. It brings to mind his calm nature and clever decisions, especially when things were tough on the field. This nickname really captures his way of leading and has become a big part of who people know him to be. By making this nickname a trademark, Dhoni is taking an important step to protect something very valuable to him.

MS Dhoni Trademarks ‘Captain Cool’: A Smart Move for His Brand

In the world of sports and business, a nickname like ‘Captain Cool’ is worth a lot of money. It’s not just a casual word; it makes people think of trust, being dependable, and winning. Imagine how many companies want to work with people who show these good qualities. When Dhoni trademarks this phrase, he gets the legal right to own it. This means no one else can use ‘Captain Cool’ to sell things or for business without his permission. This stops anyone from using his famous name unfairly and makes sure that any product or ad connected to ‘Captain Cool’ will directly help Dhoni’s brand.

This action by Dhoni shows he’s planning ahead, looking past his days of playing cricket. Many sports stars build strong public images while they are playing, but not as many take steps to protect them for many years later. By securing ‘Captain Cool’, Dhoni is building a stronger base for any future business ideas, advertising deals, or anything else where his unique personality can be useful. It’s a smart step he’s taking now to make sure his legacy is not just remembered for his amazing games, but also protected legally in the business world.

This smart decision makes MS Dhoni’s brand even stronger. It ensures that ‘Captain Cool’ stays only with his image and the good things he stands for. It really shows that he understands how important his own name and image are, and he has a clear plan for his life after cricket. For both fans and people who work in marketing, this news reminds us how powerful a strong personal brand can be, especially when it belongs to someone as iconic as MS Dhoni Captain Cool.
