title: "CSK Might Think to Leave MS Dhoni Out for a Match": Ricky Ponting
content:
Ricky Ponting, former Australian captain, recently shared his views on Chennai Super Kings (CSK) retaining MS Dhoni for the IPL 2025 season. At 42 and in the final stages of his cricket career, Dhoni has been playing only in the IPL since retiring from international cricket in 2020. Under his leadership, CSK has won five IPL titles, solidifying Dhoni’s legacy as one of the league’s greatest captains.

Ponting believes that CSK might consider resting Dhoni for occasional games to keep him fresh and maximize his impact. Reflecting on Dhoni’s recent performances, Ponting noted that two seasons ago, Dhoni had a challenging year but made a remarkable comeback last season, delivering match-winning performances much like his prime years. On a recent episode of The ICC Review, Ponting stated, “Two seasons ago, he probably had his worst season, but then last year, he bounced back, impacting games like the MS Dhoni of old.”

“CSK Might Think to Leave MS Dhoni Out for a Match”: Ricky Ponting

Ponting thinks this approach could work well for Dhoni this season too. Given Dhoni’s age, CSK might need to manage his workload by resting him accordingly to ensure he remains at his best throughout the tournament. Ponting suggested, “They might not get him through the whole season. They might think about leaving him out for a game and resting him here and there to get the best out of him.”

Besides his batting and wicket-keeping skills, Dhoni’s presence brings invaluable experience and leadership to CSK. Even when he isn’t captaining, Dhoni remains a mentor and a guiding force for the team. Ponting emphasized Dhoni’s influence, saying, “Any team he’s in, whether he’s captain or not, he’s always going to be a mentor and a leader, whether he’s playing or on the sidelines. He’s crucial to Chennai, for that leadership he brings on and off the field.”

Ponting also admired Dhoni’s ability to adapt over the years, allowing him to maintain his effectiveness despite the demands of T20 cricket. Dhoni’s current strategy of batting late in the innings highlights his selflessness, flexibility and ability to maximize his role. Ponting added, “He’s batting the last 20 balls of an innings now but still showing that you can make a big impact by doing that.”

Praising Dhoni’s longevity, Ponting highlighted how only the best players can stay at such a high level for over a decade, adapting their game as they go. Moving on, all eyes will be on the IPL 2025 Mega Auction which is to be held in Riyadh on 24 and 25 November. IPL fans will be eager to see how their favourite franchises strategize to complete their squads.

title: Jadeja Surpasses Zaheer Khan to Become Fourth-highest Wicket-Taker in Test Cricket for India
content:
India’s star all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja achieved major milestones one after the other during the third and final Test against New Zealand at Mumbai’s Wankhede Stadium. Jadeja took a ten-wicket haul on Day 3, dismantling the visitors for 174 in their second innings. With this, Jadeja surpassed former fast-bowler Zaheer Khan to become India’s fourth-highest wicket-taker in Test cricket. Taking 314 Test wickets, Jadeja now sits behind Anil Kumble, Ravichandran Ashwin, and Harbhajan Singh in India’s all-time list of wicket-takers.

This performance also pushed Jadeja’s wicket tally for the current World Test Championship (WTC) cycle to 50, making him only the second Indian, after Ashwin, to achieve this feat in a single WTC cycle. Jadeja had taken 47 wickets in the previous WTC cycle (2021–2023) and has improved on that tally this time around. Currently, he is the third-highest wicket-taker in the WTC, with Ashwin leading the way at 62 wickets, followed by Australia’s Josh Hazlewood with 51 wickets.

Ravindra Jadeja moves to fourth place in List of most 10-wicket hauls for India in Test cricket

Jadeja picked up five wickets for 55 runs in New Zealand’s second innings, adding to his earlier five wickets for 65 runs in the first innings. Apart from surpassing Zaheer Khan in list of most Test wickets for India, Jadeja marked another milestone.

The achievement marked Jadeja’s third career 10-wicket haul in Test cricket, putting him among India’s top bowlers in terms of 10-wicket hauls. He now surpasses legendary Indian bowlers like Erapalli Prasanna, Kapil Dev, and Irfan Pathan. The record for the most 10-wicket hauls by an Indian bowler is held jointly by Anil Kumble and R. Ashwin, who each have eight. Following them, Harbhajan Singh has five, while Jadeja’s three 10-wicket hauls place him next in line.

Most 10-wicket hauls for India in Tests:

  1. Anil Kumble – 8
  2. R. Ashwin – 8*
  3. Harbhajan Singh – 5
  4. Ravindra Jadeja – 3*
  5. Kapil Dev – 2
  6. Irfan Pathan – 2

Jadeja’s performance has been a beacon of hope for India, who are aiming to produce a win in this final Test after losing the first two games and facing their first series defeat at home in over a decade. On top of that, his wicket-taking ability adds depth to India’s bowling attack, which will be especially valuable in future matches, including the much-awaited Border-Gavaskar Trophy series against Australia. This form could play a crucial role as India aims to defend the title on Australian soil.

With New Zealand managing a lead of just 143 runs by the end of the second day, India is hopeful of chasing down the target. However, as the pitch continues to wear, India’s batting lineup may have to contend with tricky spin bowling, especially after recent struggles against spin.

title: Ravindra Jadeja Surpasses Ishant Sharma to Become India's Fifth-Highest Wicket-Taker in Test
content:
India’s star all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja surpasses Ishant Sharma to become India’s fifth-highest wicket-taker in Test cricket. Jadeja achieved this milestone on Day 1 of the Test match against New Zealand played in Mumbai. He not only went past Ishant but also surpassed former pacer Zaheer Khan, who had taken 311 wickets. Jadeja’s 312th wicket was New Zealand’s Glenn Phillips, and he further showcased his skill by dismissing Tom Blundell and Will Young.

Jadeja’s bowling was on full display shortly after the tea break, where he managed to bag a five-wicket haul. His fifer marked another impressive achievement in a career that has made him one of the most valuable players in India’s Test squad. The 35-year-old has become a crucial part of India’s spin setup, sharing the load with fellow spinner Ravichandran Ashwin over the years. Jadeja’s efforts have often been very important in India’s home successes, especially on spin-friendly pitches.

Ravindra Jadeja Creates History Becomes One of Only Three Indian players with 3,000 runs and 300 wickets in Test cricket

In addition to being India’s fifth-highest wicket-taker, Jadeja is also one of only three Indian players to have scored 3,000 runs and taken 300 wickets in Test cricket—a feat he shares with Kapil Dev and Ashwin. His ability to contribute with both bat and ball makes him a vital player for the Indian team, adding balance to the side. Since his Test debut in 2012, he has taken 231 of his wickets at an impressive bowling average of 21.78 and has scored four centuries with a batting average of 35.72.

Ravindra Jadeja bowled 22 consecutive overs in Mumbai’s heat and humidity, taking his 14th five-wicket haul to help India bowl out New Zealand for 235. Jadeja’s persistence paid off as he dismissed key players like Glenn Phillips, Ish Sodhi, and Matt Henry, showing both patience and skill on a pitch that began to show signs of wear.

However, India’s response faltered late in the day. They lost three wickets in the last two overs, including Yashasvi Jaiswal, who fell to a reverse sweep, and Virat Kohli, run out in a mix-up. India ended the day at 86/4, giving up the advantage they had worked hard to secure. India will be looking to recover on Day 2.

title: CSK Retention List IPL 2025: 'Uncapped' MS Dhoni Retained with 8 Crore-Pay Cut
content:
After much anticipation regarding his IPL retention, Chennai Super Kings (CSK) wicketkeeper-batter MS Dhoni will officially return to play his 18th season in the cash-rich tournament, as CSK confirmed on October 31. Since the 2024 season ended, fans have been eagerly waiting for news about Dhoni’s return, hoping to see their beloved “Thala” back on the field at Chennai’s MA Chidambaram Stadium.

Dhoni’s return is only possible due to the re-introduction of the “uncapped player” rule by the BCCI, which had been previously scrapped in 2021. This rule now states that an Indian player with previous international experience can be classified as uncapped if they haven’t played international cricket in the last five years and don’t hold a BCCI Central Contract. As Dhoni last played internationally in 2019 and does not have a current BCCI contract, he qualifies as an uncapped player for the 2025 season.

Thanks to this rule, CSK was able to retain Dhoni at the price of an uncapped player—INR 4 Crore—allowing them to preserve their auction purse. Dhoni, who has been with CSK since the start of the IPL in 2008, has led the team to five IPL titles (2010, 2011, 2018, 2021, and 2023), making him one of the league’s most celebrated captains.

CSK Retention List Consists Ruturaj Gaikwad, Matheesha Pathirana, Shivam Dube, Ravindra Jadeja Alongwith Dhoni

Along with Dhoni, CSK also retained several other key players. Star opener Ruturaj Gaikwad will stay with CSK at INR 18 Crore, while talented fast bowler Matheesha Pathirana was retained at INR 13 Crore. All-rounder Shivam Dube and seasoned player Ravindra Jadeja were also retained at INR 12 Crore and INR 18 Crore, respectively. After retaining these five players, CSK has spent INR 65 Crore out of their total purse of INR 120 Crore, leaving them with INR 55 Crore to further strengthen their squad in the mega auction.

CSK fans are thrilled to have Dhoni and the core team members back as they prepare for another promising season. With the retention list finalized, CSK can focus on building a balanced team for IPL 2025. This announcement has added excitement to the upcoming mega auction, where CSK will look to finalize their team and create a competitive squad to support captain Ruturaj Gaikwad to give Dhoni a dreamy farewell before he announces his IPL retirement.

The much-awaited IPL retention process is here, as all 10 teams get ready to announce their retained players ahead of the mega auction for IPL 2025 on October 31. MSD’s Presence Amongst CSK Potential Retentions Assures Another Year of Thala in the IPL

With the support of CSK’s CEO, Kasi Viswanathan, Dhoni aims to enjoy the final phase of his cricketing journey. Now, his focus is on playing with more freedom and finding joy in the game, particularly through the IPL. Dhoni shared that he plans to balance his love for the sport with quality time with his family, dedicating around two and a half months each year to IPL and spending the rest of his time relaxing.

Dhoni also explained the importance of staying fit year-round to be ready for the IPL season. “I need to stay fit for nine months to play those two and a half months of IPL, so I have to plan and still chill a bit,” he concluded.

Fans are eagerly awaiting the full list of retentions to see if their guesses are correct. As CSK hints at keeping its core players, it looks like Dhoni and other key names will continue to bring excitement to the field for the “Men in Yellow” in IPL 2025.

title: MS Dhoni Reveals He Batted at 8 in IPL 2024 to Give Shivam Dube, Jadeja More Chance Ahead of  T20 WC
content:
MS Dhoni recently opened up about why he chose to bat lower in the order for Chennai Super Kings (CSK) during the IPL 2024 season. This move puzzled many fans who expected him to promote himself higher up. The former CSK captain shared that his decision was because of a selfless reason: he wanted to give other CSK players, who were potential candidates for India’s T20 World Cup squad, a chance to prove themselves. Dhoni explained that he didn’t feel the need to take up valuable opportunities when he believed his teammates could benefit more.

“My thinking was simple, if others are doing their job well, why do I need to come up the order?” Dhoni explained during an event. He noted that since the T20 World Cup squad announcement was approaching, it was essential to give players fighting for a spot in the national team an opportunity to shine. “In our team, we had players like (Ravindra) Jadeja and Shivam Dube, who were in the running for the Indian team. So, giving them a chance to prove their abilities was the right thing to do,” Dhoni added.

“There was nothing in it for me, no selection or other things”: ‘Selfless’ MS Dhoni on IPL 2024 Batting Position

Emphasizing his selfless approach, Dhoni stated there was no personal gain in it for him since he wasn’t focused on selection or personal milestones. “There was nothing in it for me, no selection or other things. I was comfortable batting down the order, and my teammates were happy with what I was doing,” he shared. His decision reflects his commitment to supporting his teammates and helping them prepare for bigger opportunities, and it was appreciated by the entire team.

Despite batting lower, Dhoni managed to deliver thrilling cameos in high-pressure games. Across 14 matches, he scored 161 runs at an impressive average of 53.67 and a remarkable strike rate of 220.55, continuing to entertain fans with his finishing prowess.

Fans are now eagerly awaiting Dhoni’s decision on his future in the IPL. Although he hinted at possibly playing in IPL 2025, Dhoni said he wants to enjoy “whatever last few years of cricket” he has left, leaving fans hopeful about his continued presence in the CSK lineup.

title: MS Dhoni Appreciates Aggressive, Result-Oriented Approach Of Modern day Test Cricket
content:
Legendary cricketer and former World Cup-winning captain MS Dhoni recently shared his appreciation for the more aggressive and result-oriented approach in Test cricket. Speaking at an event in Goa, Dhoni noted how the game has evolved over the years, especially with teams now actively seeking to avoid draws.

Reflecting on this evolution, Dhoni remarked, “You can give cricket any term, but the way people play has changed. There was a time in ODIs when certain scores were safe, but now even higher scores don’t feel safe in T20s.” He believes naming playing styles—like England’s “Bazball” approach—adds excitement, but ultimately, each team’s approach depends on its strengths. “Some teams play aggressive cricket, while others stick to a more traditional style. It all depends on your team’s strengths, and you need time to adapt. You can’t change the way players play overnight, especially if they’ve been playing a certain way for over a decade,” Dhoni added.

Dhoni also spoke about the challenge of drawn matches in his career, especially on the fifth day of Tests, where results often seemed unlikely. He explained, “For me, the most challenging part was on Day 5, when it was almost certain the match would end in a draw. Keeping for nearly three sessions with no result in sight was exhausting. Bowlers would still go for wickets, and batters would try for runs, but it felt like going through the motions. Sometimes, you just want the match to end.”

Now, he enjoys seeing more games ending with results and fewer drawn matches. “Imagine explaining cricket to someone unfamiliar with the game—that you play for five days, starting in the morning, ending in the evening, and sometimes still have no result. It’s not ideal for the game,” Dhoni shared. He appreciates the current trend of result-oriented play, where even if one day is washed out, there’s still a strong push to secure a result within five days. “That’s the beauty of Test cricket—you want a result at the end, and it’s great to see that happening more often.”

Dhoni’s admiration for this shift in Test cricket highlights the ongoing transformation in the sport. During his Test career from 2005 to 2014, MS Dhoni played 90 matches, scoring 4,876 runs with six centuries and a high score of 224. With the upcoming IPL retention period, fans are eagerly waiting to see if Dhoni will play another season with Chennai Super Kings (CSK).

title: Mitchell Santner With 7-Wicket-Haul Traps Indian Batters in his Spin Web in Pune Test
content:
New Zealand took a commanding lead over India at the Maharashtra Cricket Association Stadium in Pune, ending Day 2 with a 301-run lead. The Indian batting lineup crumbled under the pressure of the spinweb laid by Mitchell Santner, which played a pivotal role in dismissing India for just 156 runs.

India began the day at 16/1, having lost skipper Rohit Sharma on the first day. Young batter Shubman Gill, who replaced Rohit, added 30 runs in a promising 49-run partnership with Yashasvi Jaiswal. However, Santner soon had his first breakthrough by trapping Gill in front of the stumps. Virat Kohli also fell cheaply, bowled out for just a single run by Santner’s tight left-arm spin.

Mitchell Santner Sets the Right Web to Trap Indian Team Cheaply

Jaiswal, who had managed to reach 30 runs and crossed the 1,000-run mark for the calendar year, was dismissed by Glenn Phillips, who followed it up by taking Rishabh Pant’s wicket for 18. Santner then returned to pick up several middle-order wickets, removing Sarfaraz Khan for 11, Ravichandran Ashwin for 4, and finally, top-scorer Ravindra Jadeja, who made 38. Santner claimed an impressive seven-wicket haul, wrapping up India’s innings by dismissing tailenders Akash Deep for 6 and Jasprit Bumrah for a duck.

Mitchell Santner had a fantastic day with the ball. He bowled really well and took career-best figures of 7 for 53. He tricked the Indian batsmen with his spin and made it very difficult for them to score runs. His bowling performance was a big reason why New Zealand was able to take a big lead in the match. Santner showed that he is a very good bowler and can be a match-winner for his team.

New Zealand, now with a substantial lead, began their second innings confidently. Openers Tom Latham and Devon Conway provided a steady start until Conway was dismissed by Washington Sundar for 17 runs. Ravichandran Ashwin provided support from the other end, ending Will Young’s innings at 23, while Sundar continued his form, removing Rachin Ravindra for 9. Sundar also claimed Daryl Mitchell, sending him back for 18 runs.

Following these setbacks, Latham played an outstanding knock of 86, further extending New Zealand’s lead before Sundar finally dismissed him. By stumps, New Zealand had reached 198/5 with Tom Blundell and Glenn Phillips unbeaten on 30 and 9 runs, respectively. Their growing lead of over 300 runs has left India facing an uphill task as they prepare for Day 3.

title: Ruturaj Gaikwad Continues to Shine Again in Ranji Trophy 2024 with Scintillating 145 Against Mumbai
content:
Ranji Trophy 2024: Ruturaj Gaikwad continues his scintillating form in domestic cricket proving his mettle time and again. The Maharashtra captain reached an important milestone by scoring his seventh century in First-Class cricket during their match against Mumbai. The match took place at the Sharad Pawar Cricket Academy in BKC, Mumbai, and Gaikwad’s century came on Day 3, after his team suffered an early loss in their second innings.

Maharashtra had a tough start in the match, getting bowled out for just 126 runs in their first innings. Mumbai capitalized on this, scoring an imposing 441 runs, thanks to standout performances from Ayush Mhatre and Shreyas Iyer, who scored 176 and 142 runs respectively. This left Maharashtra in a difficult position, facing a huge trail to follow.

Ruturaj Gaikwad Completes 7th First-Class Century with 145-run Innings in Ranji Trophy 2024

In their second innings, Maharashtra lost opener Siddhesh Veer early, adding pressure on the team. However, Gaikwad, leading as the captain, rose to the occasion scoring 145 runs in 171 balls. He started his innings with intent, hitting a six off the very first ball he faced from Shardul Thakur. His aggressive approach paid off as he steadily built his innings, reaching a century and helping stabilize Maharashtra’s position.

At 27 years old, Ruturaj Gaikwad has already built an impressive record in First-Class cricket. He has played 35 First-Class matches, scoring over 2,400 runs at an average of 43. His seven centuries and 14 half-centuries highlight his consistency as a top-order batsman. Despite having played six ODIs and 23 T20Is for India, Gaikwad is yet to make his debut in Test cricket.

After dominating the Duleep Trophy, this strong performance in the Ranji Trophy keeps Gaikwad in the spotlight as a potential candidate for the Indian Test team, particularly with the upcoming Border-Gavaskar Trophy in November. With reports suggesting that Indian captain Rohit Sharma might miss the first Test in Perth, starting on November 22, Gaikwad could be considered as a backup opener. His solid form in domestic cricket strengthens his chances of being included in the playing XI for this high-profile series against Australia.

Gaikwad’s ability to lead his team under pressure and his consistent batting performances make him a promising candidate for India’s Test squad in the near future.

title: Devon Conway Puts New Zealand in Strong Position but Equals an Unwanted Record
content:
India’s batting performance was a major disappointment in the first Test against New Zealand in Bengaluru. They were bowled out for a paltry 46 runs in their first innings, their lowest-ever Test score at home. This was a significant blow to their hopes of winning the match. New Zealand, on the other hand, batted solidly and built a strong lead. Devon Conway, the Black Caps’ opener, played a crucial knock of 91 runs, which helped his team reach a total of 180/3 at the end of the day.

India’s batting collapse started early, with captain Rohit Sharma being dismissed for just two runs. Virat Kohli and other Indian batsmen also failed to make a significant contribution, and the team was all out for 46 runs in just over 31 overs.

New Zealand’s bowlers, Tim Southee, Matt Henry, and Will O’Rourke, were in excellent form and exploited the Indian batting weaknesses to great effect. Their disciplined bowling and accurate line and length made it difficult for the Indian batsmen to score runs.

Despite India’s poor batting performance, New Zealand’s openers, Devon Conway and Tom Latham, started strongly and laid a solid foundation for their team’s innings. Conway’s 91 runs was a valuable contribution, and his innings helped New Zealand gain a significant lead over India.

Devon Conway equals McCullum in unwanted club with 91 in Bengaluru Test

CSK batter Devon Conway’s unlucky streak in the 90s continued as the batter fell just short of a century in the first Test against India at Bengaluru’s M Chinnaswamy Stadium. Conway scored 91 off 105 balls, hitting 11 fours and three sixes, before being dismissed.

This marks his third Test score in the 90s, placing him alongside Tom Blundell, Jeremy Coney, Brendon McCullum, John Reid, Mark Richardson, and Ross Taylor. New Zealand’s record for the most scores in the 90s is held by Stephen Fleming, with six. Conway’s previous 90s came against South Africa and Pakistan in 2022.

Moreover, India’s bowlers, Kuldeep Yadav and Ravindra Jadeja, managed to take a few wickets, but the damage had already been done. New Zealand’s batsmen, Rachin Ravindra and Daryl Mitchell, will start at the crease on day two and will be looking to press home their advantage.

Overall, it was a disappointing day for India, and they will need to improve their batting significantly in the second innings if they want to have any chance of winning the match. New Zealand, on the other hand, are in a strong position and will be confident of securing a victory.

title: JSK Auction Buys 2027: Full List of Players Bought by Joburg Super Kings
content:
It’s here, Super Kings fans! Ahead of SA20 2027, the auction delivered surprises, fixed a few gaps, and left us wondering about a few others. But the biggest twist? The one man who has given Super Kings fans plenty of sleepless nights over the years is now on our side. 

Kieron Pollard, once a formidable rival and a nightmare to bowl to, could now be the man deciding whether we sleep happily after match day. With the drama already set, let’s dive into the JSK auction Buys 2027 and see what the Super Kings have brought in.

JSK Auction Buys 2027 – Complete Players List With Prices 

Joburg Super Kings bought six players at the SA20 2027 auction, spending R8.975 million. Jason Rowles was their most expensive signing at R2.9 million, followed by returning star Faf du Plessis at R2.7 million. 

Players Bought by Joburg Super Kings in SA20 2027 Auction 

While the list of JSK players bought is very small, but they have bought some impact players who can make the difference in the next season.

Jason Rowles – R2.9 Million

At just 18, Jason Rowles became JSK’s biggest auction buy at R2.9 million and a clear investment in the future. The slow left-arm orthodox bowler has shown serious batting potential, scoring 201, 85, 66 and 52 in his recent U-19 outings. In his only T20, he made an unbeaten 45 and took a wicket. He could become JSK’s trump card once he settles into the squad.

Faf du Plessis – R2.7 Million

Death, taxes and Faf in yellow. We simply never have a season without him. Across 36 innings, Faf has scored 1,029 runs, including seven fifties and a hundred, at a strike rate of 144 and average of 32.5. His return is about far more than numbers. He brings leadership, experience and the familiarity of someone who knows this Super Kings set-up inside out. Expect Faf to once again set the tone at the top and give JSK a reliable foundation.

Kieron Pollard – R1.5 Million

The biggest plot twist of 2026! After years of praying for Pollard to get out against us, we are now counting on him. At 39, the veteran brings an astonishing 14,999 T20 runs, alongside elite power-hitting, experience and leadership. His arrival significantly strengthens the middle order alongside Donovan and JSK’s new all-rounders. Pollard can absorb pressure, then completely destroy an attack in the final overs. This is precisely the kind of player who could turn competitive totals into massive ones.

Andries Gous – R1 Million

One of the auction’s underrated buys, Gous adds a proven wicketkeeper-opener with 4,036 T20 runs, 27 fifties and three centuries. He can bat long and gives JSK another reliable option at the top.

Blessing Muzarabani – R500,000

The 6’8″ Zimbabwean adds serious pace and bounce, joining Holder and Overton to form an intimidating trio of towering fast bowlers. He has 170 wickets in T20s in just 149 matches.

Dayyaan Galiem – R375,000

Galiem adds valuable lower-order depth, with 66 wickets and 898 runs from 82 T20s. A useful No.10 option who strengthens JSK’s all-round flexibility.

Jamie Overton JSK Wildcard Signing

Jamie Overton joins JSK as their wildcard signing, bringing his CSK experience to Johannesburg. The English all-rounder offers serious pace, bounce and lower-order hitting. Alongside Holder and Pollard, he strengthens JSK’s batting depth while adding another valuable bowling option.

How the Auction Buys Strengthen Joburg Super Kings

The Super Kings banked on experience, conditions, depth and versatility. The result is a bowling unit packed with height and pace, while the batting order now stretches much deeper. With Gous keeping wickets, Donovan Ferreira offering another bowling option and the batting potentially running until No.10, JSK could have seven to eight genuine bowling options. Faf and Pollard bring enormous T20 experience, while Rowles and Galiem add future potential.

What These Signings Mean for SA20 2026

Three towering fast bowlers, a marquee middle-order batter capable of clearing the ropes at will, and a proper wicketkeeper-opener, JSK have addressed some major gaps. Gous’ arrival gives Donovan Ferreira the freedom to focus more on his all-round role, while Galiem provides valuable depth. And then there is Faf, back in yellow, a top-order banker who brings consistency and experience. On paper, JSK look significantly stronger than last season. If injuries stay away, this could be a season to remember.

FAQs

Which players did JSK buy in the SA20 2027 auction?

Joburg Super Kings bought six players: Jason Rowles, Faf du Plessis, Kieron Pollard, Andries Gous, Blessing Muzarabani and Dayyaan Galiem.

Who was JSK’s most expensive buy in 2027?

Jason Rowles was JSK’s most expensive purchase at R2.9 million. The 18-year-old all-rounder was also the most expensive player across the SA20 2027 auction.

How much did JSK spend at the SA20 2027 auction?

Joburg Super Kings spent R8.975 million on six players at the auction held on 7 October 2026.

Did JSK buy Kieron Pollard in the 2027 auction?

Yes. Joburg Super Kings signed former Mumbai Indians all-rounder Kieron Pollard for R1.5 million ahead of SA20 2027.

Did Faf du Plessis return to JSK for SA20 2027?

Yes. JSK bought back Faf du Plessis for R2.7 million after a bidding battle with MI Cape Town.

Was Jamie Overton bought at the SA20 2027 auction?

No. Jamie Overton joined Joburg Super Kings as their wildcard signing. He was not one of the six players JSK bought at the auction.

title: MS Dhoni Flaunts New Hairstyle Amid IPL Retirement Rumours
content:
Former CSK and India captain MS Dhoni, known for his trend-setting looks over the years, recently made headlines with a fresh new hairstyle, debuting the style with the help of celebrity hairstylist, Aalim Hakim.

Dhoni’s new appearance quickly captured the attention of fans, who took to social media to express their admiration and excitement over his latest transformation. Although Dhoni’s social media presence is minimal, his evolving style keeps him in the spotlight.

This hairstyle update comes after Dhoni brought back his signature long hair during the 2024 IPL season, reminding of his look from the 2007 T20 World Cup. That nostalgic choice thrilled fans, reminding them of the days when Dhoni first emerged as a cricketing sensation.

It’s clear that, even in retirement from international cricket, Dhoni remains a powerful presence in the sport and an influencer off the field, with each new look generating significant buzz among the “Whistle Podu” army of Chennai Super Kings (CSK) supporters.

The timing of Dhoni’s new hairstyle has also added fuel to the ongoing speculation about his future with CSK. Since stepping down from international cricket in August 2020, Dhoni has continued to participate in the IPL, captaining CSK until 2024, when he passed the leadership to Ruturaj Gaikwad.

Despite this transition, Dhoni has remained central to the CSK lineup, leading them to a record fifth IPL title in 2023. His decision to remain tight-lipped about his future after the 2024 season left fans wondering whether he’ll return for another IPL season or finally bid farewell to the game.

Will MS Dhoni Play in IPL 2025?

With new IPL auction and retention rules introduced in September 2024, discussions have intensified around the possibility of Dhoni continuing his IPL career as an uncapped player. According to the new rules, a capped Indian player who has not played international cricket for five consecutive years can be classified as uncapped for IPL purposes. This rule has led to a surge in excitement among fans, as it raises questions about Dhoni’s potential status for the upcoming season and what this means for CSK.

Despite his retirement from the international arena, Dhoni’s influence is as strong as ever. He continues to captivate his massive fanbase not only through his on-field prowess but also with his evolving style.

Whether he’s rocking a bold new hairstyle or leading his team to victory, Dhoni’s appeal remains unmatched, and his recent side-fade hairstyle is yet another reminder of his lasting impact on Indian cricket and beyond. As the countdown to the next IPL season begins, Dhoni’s fans eagerly await his next move—both on the field and in style.

title: Rinku Singh Shares MS Dhoni Advice That Helped Him Rescue India After Top-order Collapse against Bangladesh
content:
Rinku Singh holds a separate fanbase for his forgetful nature, forgetting advice given by legends of the game like MS Dhoni. However, he was in exceptional form during India’s dominant win over Bangladesh in the second T20I of their three-match series, held in New Delhi on Wednesday. The hosts secured an impressive 86-run victory to clinch the series 2-0, showcasing strong performances in both batting and bowling.

Batting first, India posted a formidable total of 221/9 in 20 overs, thanks to stellar half-centuries from Nitish Kumar Reddy and Rinku Singh. Nitish, who batted at number four, was awarded the Player of the Match for his explosive 74 off 34 balls, featuring four boundaries and seven sixes. Rinku provided solid support with his own impressive innings, scoring 53 runs from 29 deliveries, which included five fours and three sixes. Together, they forged a 108-run partnership in just 49 balls, setting up a challenging target for Bangladesh.

Chasing 222, Bangladesh was held to 135/9 in their 20 overs, with Varun Chakravarthy and Nitish Kumar Reddy each claiming two wickets. The Indian bowlers kept up the pressure, making it difficult for Bangladesh to build any momentum. This all-around performance marked India’s dominance in New Delhi.

Rinku Singh Shares MS Dhoni Advice That Helped Him Rescue India From 41/3

Following the match, Rinku Singh shared insights into his approach to the game. He credited his experience with red-ball cricket as a key factor in his recent success, explaining, “I love playing with the red ball. The way I batted today is similar to how I approach my role in domestic games, coming in at 5-6 when wickets fall. I back myself and focus on getting runs for the team, especially in tough situations.”

Rinku also praised Nitish for his intelligent batting, noting that a no-ball turned into a free hit for Nitish, who smashed it for six, significantly boosting his confidence. “He batted with great intelligence,” Rinku shared. “We enjoyed the partnership, and I told him, ‘It’s God’s plan, keep hitting.’ We just focused on staying positive and playing our game.”

Reflecting on his approach to the future, Rinku mentioned that he no longer tries to overthink his game. “Earlier, I started thinking too much, and things weren’t going well. So now, I focus on the present and try not to look too far ahead,” he said.

Rinku also spoke about his conversations with MS Dhoni, who has been a valuable mentor. “I’ve been talking to Mahi Bhai (Dhoni), and he’s been very helpful. He gave me advice on what a batter should do if the team loses early wickets. I’ve taken this advice to heart, as I’ve encountered similar situations with India, my IPL team, and my state team.”

With a strong first-class record, Rinku has scored 3,179 runs in 48 matches for Uttar Pradesh, boasting an impressive average of 53.88, along with seven centuries and 20 half-centuries.

title: The Hundred: CSK and KKR Engage in Fiery Battle to Attain Manchester Originals
content:
Two of India’s biggest franchise cricket teams, Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) and Chennai Super Kings (CSK), are looking to buy a team in The Hundred. The tournament being one of the newest cricket tournaments in England is attracting a lot of attention. This shows that IPL teams are interested in expanding their reach beyond India after Carribean Premier League, Major League Cricket, SA20 League, and what not.

The Manchester Originals, a team in The Hundred, is currently owned by Lancashire Cricket Club. KKR and CSK are competing to buy this team. Even though some people have criticized The Hundred’s auction process, the English cricket market is still very attractive to IPL teams.

KKR, owned by Bollywood stars Shah Rukh Khan and Juhi Chawla, already has teams in other countries like the Caribbean Premier League (CPL) and Major League Cricket (MLC) in the United States. Buying Manchester Originals would help KKR grow even bigger.

CSK, owned by billionaire N. Srinivasan, is one of the most successful teams in the IPL. CSK has won the IPL five times and has many loyal fans. Srinivasan wants CSK to be more popular in other countries, especially England.

Daniel Gidney, the head of Lancashire Cricket Club, is happy to work with an IPL team. He thinks it would help The Hundred become more popular. All 10 IPL teams are interested in English cricket, and several other teams besides KKR and CSK might also buy a team in The Hundred.

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) is trying to sell The Hundred to private companies, including IPL teams. This is part of a bigger trend where IPL teams are expanding their reach beyond India. KKR and CSK’s interest in Manchester Originals shows that cricket is becoming more global.

title: WATCH: Faf du Plessis Recreates Rohit Sharma's Winning Dance after clinching CPL Title
content:
Saint Lucia Kings (SLK) made history by clinching their first-ever Caribbean Premier League (CPL) title. SLK defeated Guyana Amazon Warriors (GAW) by 6 wickets in the final at Providence Stadium on October 7. But what attracted Chennai Super Kings fans’ attention was Faf du Plessis’ winning dance.

Following the win, SLK captain Plessis drew widespread attention with his celebration for someone who always looks to be in a serious mood this was something astounding. After receiving the CPL trophy, du Plessis recreated Indian captain Rohit Sharma’s iconic slow-motion walk from the 2024 T20 World Cup celebrations. The video of this moment quickly went viral, with fans sharing clips of du Plessis walking confidently to join his team in celebration, mimicking Sharma’s memorable style.

WATCH: Faf du Plessis Recreates Rohit Sharma’s Winning Dance after clinching CPL Title

SLK won the toss and elected to bowl, making early inroads into GAW’s lineup. Every bowler contributed with a wicket, with Noor Ahmad emerging as the standout performer. Ahmad’s economical spell saw him claim three wickets for just 19 runs in his four overs, effectively stifling GAW’s scoring momentum. Despite some resistance from Dwaine Pretorius, who scored 25 off 12 balls, and Shai Hope, who contributed 22 off 24 balls, GAW could only post a modest 138/8 in their allotted 20 overs.

Chasing 139, SLK faced initial setbacks, losing key players early. Faf du Plessis (21 off 21 balls) and Johnson Charles (7), who together accumulated over 850 runs in the tournament, were dismissed cheaply. With the team struggling at 51 for 4, Roston Chase and Aaron Jones took charge. Chase, with a quick-fire 39 off 22 balls, hit two fours and two sixes, while Jones scored an impressive 48 off 31 balls, including two fours and four sixes. Their counter-attacking partnership brought SLK back into the game, and they reached the target with 11 balls to spare, securing a memorable victory.

In the post-match ceremony, du Plessis expressed his pride in the team, saying, “We have been really consistent throughout the league stage, and I believe the two best teams played in the final. We always believed in the depth of the squad, and credit to Roston and Aaron for absorbing the pressure and stepping up when needed. It takes a special team performance to come here to their home ground and beat them twice. I am extremely proud of the team for showing grit throughout the tournament and getting the job done.”

This win marks a very special place in T20 franchise cricket as Punjab Super Kings’ sister franchise SLK wins the maiden title for their co-owners Preity Zinta, Mohit Burman, Ness Wadia, and Karan Paul.

title: "Absolute Rubbish" Tommy Smsek CSK's physio slams Harbhajan Singh for "Fake" claims
content:
Tommy Smsek, the physiotherapist of Chennai Super Kings has come out to slam Harbhajan Singh, former CSK player, on his comment regarding MS Dhoni’s anger.

Earlier, Harbhajan Singh was quoted revealing some details of the post-match scenes after RCB knocked Chennai Super Kings out of the IPL 2024. It was a do or die game for either team and CSK was unable to cross the line.

Following this defeat, according to Harbhajan Singh, MS Dhoni had a rare moment, where he lost his temper. In distress of getting knocked out of the tournament, he said to have punched a screen while walking back to the dressing room.

In an interaction with Sports Yaari, he said, “”RCB was celebrating and they deserved to celebrate because of the way they won. I was watching the whole scene from above because I was present there. RCB was celebrating and CSK had lined up to shake hands, RCB were a little late to reach CSK. By the time Team RCB finished their celebration, (Dhoni) went inside and he punched a screen outside the dressing room. I was watching from above but it is okay that every player has his own emotions, it happens.”

However, Tommy has criticized Harbhajan Singh for his words. He was quick to dismiss the claims, by calling them fake news and absolute rubbish.

“This is absolute Rubbish! MSD did not break anything and I have never seen him aggressive after any match. Fake news!” Simsek said while commenting on an Instagram post that had shared Harbhajan’s comment on Dhoni.

Apparently, Chennai Super Kings and Royal Challengers Bengaluru locked horn in their respective final league game with a berth in the qualifiers up for grab. The only catch in this encounter was that RCB didn’t just need to win the game to qualify. They needed to do so by a margin of 18 runs, to ensure they had superior net run rate against CSK.

Chasing a total of 27 runs, CSK didn’t even need to win the game. All they had to do was ensure that their opponent didn’t get a win by the margin of 18 or more runs.

However, the five time champions fell short of achieving that feat as well. Despite a blistering knock of 61 by Rachin Ravindra, and immense contribution of 42 off 22 by Jadeja, CSK couldn’t cross the line and were eliminated from the tournament by the barest of margins possible in the game.

title: IPL 2025 Mega Auction Rules:  Six Retention, RTM, and Impact Player
content:
IPL 2025 Mega Auction guidelines are here and the fans cannot keep calm, knowing how their teams can shape up ahead of the new season of the IPL. The Indian Premier League (IPL) has always been a breeding ground for innovative rules that create the most thrilling and unrealistic moments in matches. Every season has produced or demanded for a change which is fulfilled by innovation and the 2024 mega auction won’t be any different.

For a long time, there was a debate brooding in the background, which focused on the number of retention that will be allowed ahead of the mega auction. Or whether the RTM or Right To Match card will make a return to the auction. On top of everything, there was a huge question mark on the rule of Impact Player rule as well. To all these questions, BCCI replied with a single word answer: Yes.

To further understand the IPL 2025 Mega Auction guidelines, read along as we explain the intricacies of these new rule, and also discuss how they will affect team strategies and the overall conduct of the IPL.

The New Retention Rules: A Game-Changer for the IPL

One of the most significant guidelines for the IPL 2025 mega auction is allowing all ten teams to retain a maximum of six players from their previous squads, including the RTM Card. This is a notable increase from the previous seasons, where the franchises were permitted a maximum of five retentions. 

This six-player retention policy includes a combination of both capped (max 5) and uncapped (max 2) players, providing the teams with better flexibility to secure their core players. 

Impact on Team Strategies

The increased retention slots from 5 to 6 will allow teams to secure their star players without worrying about losing them in the mega auction. Successful teams like Chennai Super Kings (CSK) and Mumbai Indians (MI), renowned for their consistent squads, will likely benefit most from this rule. 

For instance, MI will look to keep their skipper, Hardik Pandya, ace pacer Jasprit Bumrah, and attacking batter Suryakumar Yadav, alongside emerging talents like Tilak Varma. 

Similarly, CSK can secure stalwarts like MS Dhoni, Ravindra Jadeja, and skipper Ruturaj Gaikwad with budding talents such as overseas bowler Matheesha Pathirana. 

Balancing the Squad

The six retentions provide stability and enable the teams to balance retaining star players while maintaining their purse value for the auction. Teams expected to invest heavily in marquee names could find themselves short on funds for their remaining squad. Hence, it will be crucial to strike a balance to build a strong squad in the highly competitive tournament. 

Teams like Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Delhi Capitals, which are still eyeing their maiden tournament title, will be looking to rebuild a strong squad ahead of the mega auction, giving the other teams a tough fight. The additional retention slot can encourage the teams to work on nurturing uncapped players.

Right to Match (RTM) Returns

The return of the Right to Match (RTM) card is a notable change for the IPL 2025 season. This rule will enable the teams to get back to another team, the former squad members they lost in the auction, by matching the highest bid. The Right to Match (RTM) rule adds a layer of more excitement and strategy to the mega auction.

Strategic Importance of RTM

The Right to Match (RTM) card gives the teams a second chance to welcome the player in their squad who might have played a pivotal role in previous editions but was left out due to retention or strategic restrictions. 

It’s a masterstroke for teams that have multiple star players, as they now bag an opportunity to safeguard the key members of their squad without retaining them directly.

For instance, if Chennai Super Kings feel like they cannot retain Mahesh Theekshana for a hefty price of 14 crores, they can release him ahead of the auction. Later, match his price using the RTM card to buy him once again.

Auction Dynamics with Right to Match (RTM)

The reintroduction of RTM will highly impact the IPL 2025 mega auction as teams will be forced to think twice before placing high bids on players, considering the player’s former team could easily match the offer. This could lead to more restrictive bidding, with teams opting for those players who are less likely to get matched by their original teams. 

The RTM card also introduces a smart bidding tactic element into the auction as teams might unnecessarily bid on players not necessarily because they need them, but solely to force the original team to stretch their budget knowing they will want to use their RTM. In such cases, the team using the RTM card may have to pay a higher amount than pre-determined for players they could have retained outright.

Continuation of the Impact Player Rule

As announced by the BCCI, the IPL 2023 innovation, the Impact Player rule, will continue until the IPL 2027 season. This rule permits the teams to substitute one player during the course of the match based on the situation of the game by swapping a squad member with a fresh face who could make a significant impact in the match. The rule has been highly controversial but adds a strategic twist to the in-game management. 

Tactical Flexibility with the Impact Player Rule

The continuation of the Impact Player rule indicates that the teams will continue to enjoy the tactical flexibility of swapping a player based on the pitch conditions and match situations. Whether it’s backing a bowler on a green top or introducing an extra batter while chasing a huge target, teams can alter their strategies between games. This rule also helps the captains who might misinterpret the conditions ahead of the toss, ensuring that they still have options to introduce new combinations during the match.

Impact on Team Selection

Even though the retention rules, along with the utility of RTM cards, provide certain pre-auction advantages, the Impact Player rule will determine how the teams strategize for the auction. Teams will seek versatile players who can perform multiple roles and can be deployed as impact players. 

For example, all-rounders and strong bowlers who can adapt to the role of a part-time attacking batter in the lower order will be highly valuable as they can provide depth to the squad and increase the tactical options available to the skipper.

Budget and Salary Cap Considerations

The IPL governing council has also taken steps to adjust the salary cap for franchises with the increased retention slots and RTM cards. For IPL 2025, the salary cap will be raised to INR 125 Crores from 100 Crores to accommodate the extra retention slot, ensuring teams have enough funds to assemble competitive squads.

Managing finances will be crucial in the auction, as teams will need to balance the salary of retained players with the need to acquire new players at the auction. 

What Does IPL 2025 Hold For Fans?

The guidelines for player retention, the Right to Match (RTM) card, and the continued use of the Impact Player rule suggest that the IPL 2025 mega auction and the tournament’s brand-new season will be even more strategic and competitive than ever. 

Teams will need to strategize wisely before the auction, deciding whether to keep their key players or save money for fresh talent. 

The RTM card adds more excitement and uncertainty to the auction, while the Impact Player rule keeps the game plans flexible and interesting. Teams that can quickly adjust to these changes and make smart use of their retention slots, RTM cards, and Impact Player rule will have a better chance of succeeding in the IPL 2025 season.

Pathirana’s growing fanbase will now get to see him in action during the SA20 tournament. Although his 2024 IPL season was cut short due to injury after playing only six matches, Pathirana still managed to take 13 wickets. His absence impacted CSK’s performance as they failed to make it to the playoffs. Now fully recovered, Pathirana aims to help JSK reach their first-ever SA20 final.

title: CSK Legend Dwayne Bravo Retires From All Formats of Cricket
content:
Chennai Super Kings legendary Dwayne Bravo has officially retired from all forms of cricket following an injury-shortened season in the Caribbean Premier League (CPL). The groin injury, sustained during a match for the Trinbago Knight Riders against the St Lucia Kings, marked the end of Bravo’s storied career. Attempting a catch in the seventh over, Bravo pulled up in pain and was forced to leave the field, not bowling a single over in what would be his final match.

Bravo announced his retirement with a heartfelt message reflecting on his cricketing journey. He expressed deep gratitude for the sport that had been a part of his life since he was five years old. “From the age of five, I knew this was what I wanted to do – this was the sport I was destined to play. In return, you gave me the life I dreamed of for myself and my family. For that, I can’t thank you enough,” Bravo shared.

He acknowledged the toll cricket had taken on his body, admitting that while his mind still wanted to continue, his body could no longer endure the pain and strain. “It’s time to face reality. My mind wants to keep going, but my body can no longer endure the pain, the breakdowns, and the strain.”

Dwayne Bravo Bids Farewell to Cricket as a Player to Join KKR as a Mentor

Throughout his 21-year professional career, Bravo set remarkable benchmarks in T20 cricket. He won titles in the IPL, PSL, and Big Bash, and was part of the West Indies’ victorious campaigns in the T20 World Cups in 2012 and 2016. Bravo finishes his T20 career as the second-highest wicket-taker in the format, with 631 wickets in 582 matches, second only to his compatriot Kieron Pollard.

Bravo’s international career saw him retire from Test cricket in 2015 and initially step away from all formats in 2018. However, he returned in 2019 to help prepare the West Indies for the 2020 T20 World Cup. His final international match came against Australia in November 2021, when he retired from international cricket after a distinguished career.

Looking ahead, Bravo has already secured his next role in cricket. He will take over as the mentor for Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) in the IPL from the 2025 season, filling the gap left by Gautam Gambhir, who was appointed head coach of the Indian men’s team. This new chapter follows his stint as bowling coach with Chennai Super Kings in 2022 and 2023, where he helped guide the team to success.

title: Dwayne Bravo Leaves CSK to Join KKR as Mentor ahead of IPL 2025
content:
Former West Indies allrounder Dwayne Bravo has officially ended his illustrious time with Chennai Super Kings (CSK), where he secured four IPL titles. From the 2025 season onward, Bravo will serve as the mentor for Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR). His appointment comes after a long and successful career as both player and coach, and it marks his full transition from playing to mentoring.

Bravo, 41, replaces Gautam Gambhir, who stepped down as KKR’s mentor after being appointed as India’s head coach. Bravo’s role will not only focus on KKR in the IPL, but he will also oversee all Knight Riders-owned franchises, including Trinbago Knight Riders (CPL), Los Angeles Knight Riders (MLC), and Abu Dhabi Knight Riders (ILT20). This long-term role was finalized after a meeting between Bravo and KKR CEO Venky Mysore during the CPL.

“DJ Bravo joining us is an exciting development,” Mysore said in a statement. “His relentless drive to win, along with his vast experience and deep knowledge, will greatly benefit our franchise and players.”

CSK Legend Dwayne Bravo Expresses Excitement For New Role With KKR

Bravo expressed his excitement about the new challenge, stating, “I’ve been part of the Trinbago Knight Riders for the last 10 years in the CPL. Having played for and against the Knight Riders in various leagues, I have a lot of respect for how they operate. The owners’ passion, the professionalism of the management, and the family-like environment make it a special place. This is the perfect platform for me as I transition from playing to mentoring and coaching the next generation of players.”

Bravo’s move to KKR comes after his retirement from all forms of cricket, which he announced shortly before taking on this new role. Known as one of the best death bowlers in T20 history, Bravo’s cricketing career boasts numerous achievements, including being the third-highest wicket-taker in IPL history and the only player to win two Purple Caps.

After his playing retirement from CSK in 2022, Bravo quickly transitioned to coaching, joining CSK as their bowling coach in 2023. His immediate impact was felt as CSK secured their fifth IPL title that year, adding to the three titles Bravo had already won with them as a player.

title: Ruturaj Gaikwad Named ROI Team Captain for Irani Trophy 2023-24
content:
The Rest of India (ROI) squad for the upcoming Irani Trophy 2023-24 was announced on Tuesday, with Ruturaj Gaikwad appointed as the captain. The ROI team will face Ranji Trophy champions Mumbai in the prestigious Irani Trophy, which is scheduled to take place from October 1 to October 5. The match will see some of India’s most promising cricketers competing on a major domestic stage.

Among the notable names in the squad are Dhruv Jurel and Yash Dayal, both of whom are currently part of the Indian squad for the ongoing Test series against Bangladesh. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) confirmed that both players will join the ROI squad if they are not selected for the playing XI in the second Test match, which begins on September 27 in Kanpur. “Dhruv Jurel and Yash Dayal have been selected in the Rest of India squad, and their participation is subject to them not being involved in the second Test match against Bangladesh in Kanpur,” stated the BCCI.

Other players in the squad include Sai Sudharsan, Devdutt Padikkal, wicketkeepers Ishan Kishan and Dhruv Jurel, and fast bowlers Prasidh Krishna and Mukesh Kumar.

Meanwhile, Mumbai’s squad will feature key players such as all-rounder Shardul Thakur, veteran batsman Ajinkya Rahane, and Shreyas Iyer. Thakur, who underwent foot surgery in June and has since recovered, will be playing his first domestic match following the injury, which had resurfaced during India’s tour of South Africa earlier this year. The Irani Trophy, a historic fixture in Indian domestic cricket, puts the reigning Ranji Trophy champions against the Rest of India squad. This year’s clash between Mumbai and ROI promises to be an exciting encounter, with both teams fielding strong line-ups.

title: Rishabh Pant Equals MS Dhoni For Smashing Most Test Centuries as Indian Wicket-Keeper
content:
Rishabh Pant made a sensational return to Test cricket, not only with a commanding century but by equalling MS Dhoni’s record of the most centuries by an Indian wicketkeeper in Test matches. Playing in his first Test after 637 days, Pant’s remarkable performance marked a significant comeback and added another milestone to his already impressive career. His sixth Test century, scored in the first match against Bangladesh in Chennai, came at a crucial time for India, solidifying his position as one of India’s most dynamic and reliable wicketkeeper-batters.

Pant walked in to bat on Day 2 of India’s second innings after the dismissal of Virat Kohli, with India in a tricky position. Despite holding a strong 227-run lead from the first innings, the team had lost key wickets as captain Rohit Sharma and opener Yashasvi Jaiswal both failed to convert their starts. Pant arrived when India was struggling at 86 for 3, needing to consolidate their lead and avoid a top-order collapse.

From the start, Pant showcased a more mature and composed approach, staying cautious through the final overs of Day 2. As play resumed on Day 3, Pant opted for patience, an uncharacteristic but effective choice. Known for his flamboyant and aggressive style, he instead focused on building India’s lead with a calculated and risk-free approach. His half-century came off 88 balls, slower than usual for the attacking left-hander, but his restraint was a clear indication of his evolving game and growing maturity.

With rain forecasts looming over Days 4 and 5, Pant and Shubman Gill accelerated after their respective half-centuries, shifting gears to increase the scoring rate. Pant switched effortlessly from a defensive mindset to an attacking one as batting conditions eased. Boundaries flowed, and Bangladesh’s bowlers struggled to keep up. His century, which came off 124 balls, put India in a commanding position, further demoralizing the visitors.

Rishabh Pant Equals MS Dhoni For Smashing Most Test Centuries as Indian Wicket-Keeper

Pant’s century equalled the record of MS Dhoni, India’s most celebrated wicketkeeper, who also scored six Test centuries in his illustrious career. Dhoni’s feat took 90 matches, while Pant achieved the same milestone in just 34 Test appearances, underscoring his rapid rise in the format. Pant was eventually dismissed for 109 after attempting an ambitious shot off Mehidy Hasan, but his contribution had already put India in control.

By matching Dhoni’s record, Pant cemented his place in Indian cricket history, further proving his ability to step up in crucial moments. With many more years ahead, it seems likely that Pant will not only break Dhoni’s record but set new standards for Indian wicketkeepers in Test cricket.

CSK’s most valuable player, Jadeja, meanwhile, took his time to settle in but was always ready to capitalize on any loose deliveries. title: Matthew Hayden’s Mongoose Bat: Popularity, Legality, and Controversies in Cricket
content:
If you are a cricket fan from the 90s, then you certainly must be familair with the cameo played by Matthew Hayden with his small buddy, “The Mongoose Bat.”

Although the bat existed in cricket, it was Hayden who made the mongoose bat famous.

Standing out with its short blade and long handle, this bat soon found itself in the limelight. Hayden played one of the greatest innings in IPL history, scoring 93 off just 43 balls against the Delhi Daredevils (now Delhi Capitals). 

The Mongoose bat received much attention and broke the silence in the cricket fraternity while at the same time raising issues on whether it is legal, feasible, and the future of technological advancement in Cricket. 

This article is an ode to the long lost and forgotten mongoose bat that was last seen in the hands of Matthew Hayden. Today, we will dive into the question of what happened to mongoose bats?

Watch: Matthew Hayden use Mongoose bat in IPL

During the 2010 IPL, Hayden of the Chennai Super Kings (CSK) brought the Mongoose bat into the limelight. Its most conspicuous feature was the reduced blade, which was about 33% smaller than the conventional cricket bat with a longer handle. 

This novelty was to provide the batsman with additional hitting power, particularly during forward and aggressive shots. His endorsement of the Mongoose bat brought it into the limelight, and people started learning about it all around the world. 

Hayden was one of the leading players in world cricket at the time, and therefore, using the bat in crucial matches created a lot of interest among the followers of the game and even the opponents. Some people were looking forward to using the bat and seeing if it would really provide the added power. 

Matthew Hayden smashed 93 runs using the Mongoose against Delhi Daredevil in a league game. This inning of his became one of the most memorable moments of IPL. People found it funny that Hayden, who was already a man of great muscle and might, could use the funny-looking bat to generate so much power. 

 Mr. IPL, Raina remembered this knock as one of the best he had ever witnessed. The media followed suit, and the Mongoose bat was hailed as the new weapon for power play in the T20 format of the game. Not even CSK captain MS Dhoni was immune to the appreciation of the innings, despite his initial reluctance towards the new bat. 

Is It Legal To Use A Mongoose Bat In Cricket? 

However, with the increasing buzz, several cricket fans were keen to know whether the Mongoose bat was legal according to the laws of Cricket. The MCC, which is the custodian of the laws of Cricket, has set down some parameters in relation to the cricket bat, and the most important ones are the dimensions of the blade part of the bat in terms of length, width, and profile. 

The Mongoose bat, however, had an unconventional shape, and all its dimensions were within the legal specifications, thus making it legal. The short blade and the long handle, which might have looked quite strange, adhered to the allowable standards. In short, Mongoose bat is completely legal to be used in cricket.

However, its legal aspect did not stop controversies from brewing within the cricket fraternity. Some thought that the bat provided an unfair edge to the big hitters, as they could easily launch even reasonable deliveries to the boundary. Others wondered whether the Mongoose could be incorporated into the game on a more permanent basis and what impact it would have on the game beyond the realm of big hitting. 

Cricketers Who Have Used the Mongoose Bat 

Though Matthew Hayden is the most prominent personality who has used the Mongoose bat, he was not the only one who did. Some foreign players also tried it out, here is a list:

Suresh Raina

Suresh Raina, renowned as “Mr. IPL,” played for Chennai Super Kings and India. He briefly experimented with the mongoose bat during the 2010 IPL season, following his CSK teammate Matthew Hayden’s lead. Raina used the bat in a few matches, including a game against Delhi Daredevils where he scored a quick-fire 49 off 34 balls.

Andrew Symonds

Andrew Symonds, the late Australian all-rounder, was a powerhouse in cricket’s shorter formats. Known for his hard-hitting batting, athletic fielding, and useful bowling, Symonds was a game-changer.

Following the example of his teammate Hayden, he tried the mongoose bat during the 2010 IPL while playing for the Mumbai Indians. Although he didn’t use it extensively in matches, Symonds was seen practicing with the bat, generating significant media interest due to his reputation as a big-hitter.

Stuart Law

Stuart Law, the former Australian cricketer, became involved with promoting cricket equipment. He was one of the early advocates for the mongoose bat, using it in exhibition matches and promotional events around 2009-2010. Law’s involvement lent credibility to the bat, given his reputation as a technically sound batsman.

Marcus Trescothick

Marcus Trescothick, is a former English opener who employed the mongoose bat while playing for Somerset in English domestic T20 matches during the 2010 season, including a notable innings of 78 off 32 balls against Hampshire.

title: Determined to Keep MS Dhoni CSK Awaits Release of IPL Retention Rules
content:
Chennai Super Kings (CSK) is eagerly awaiting the release of the IPL retention rules, as they are determined to keep for the upcoming season. ‘Thala’ Dhoni, who has been the face of CSK since the start of the IPL, holds immense value for the franchise both on and off the field. Despite rumors of his retirement, CSK is hopeful that Dhoni will continue playing for at least one more season, and they are prepared to make him one of their key retentions.

Recent information suggests that the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) may delay the release of the retention rules until the end of September, potentially around the time of the BCCI Annual General Meeting (AGM) on September 29. While there is no direct connection between the AGM and IPL policies, this delay has left franchise officials, including those from CSK in anticipation. CSK like other franchises is waiting for clarity on the number of retentions allowed and any new rules that might impact their decision-making.

One significant policy that is being debated is the classification of retired international players as uncapped. While this rule may not be specifically designed to favor CSK or Dhoni, it could still play a role in retention decisions. However, CSK officials have made it clear that regardless of whether Dhoni is considered uncapped or not, they will retain him if he decides to continue playing. The potential change in rules is not likely to affect CSK’s intent to keep their former captain.

CSK’s management knows that Dhoni’s leadership and experience are invaluable. Beyond his performances on the field, Dhoni brings a sense of calm and strategy that has been a key part of CSK’s success over the years. Even if BCCI allows only two retentions, CSK is committed to making Dhoni one of them.

The expected retention deadline of November 15 gives CSK some time to finalize their decisions. With the IPL auction likely to take place in December, the franchise is keen to make strategic choices that ensure a strong squad. Although the Right to Match (RTM) option is expected to be part of the auction, retaining Dhoni is CSK’s priority.

title: Purple Cap Winners for Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in IPL History
content:
Chennai Super Kings have established themselves as a powerhouse in IPL. They have been the most consistent team in the history of the tournament. A huge credit of it goes to the Purple Cap Winners for Chennai Super Kings.

From Dwayne Bravo’s death-overs bowling to Imran Tahir’s celebration, CSK has been able to get hold of the Purple Cap for four times. So, let’s recall these match-winning performances and how they affected CSK’s fortunes. 

Over the years, Chennai Super Kings Purple Cap winners have dominated IPL bowling charts with consistent wicket-taking performances. From Dwayne Bravo’s masterclass in death bowling to Imran Tahir’s magical leg-spin and Mohit Sharma’s disciplined pace attack, CSK bowlers have won the prestigious Purple Cap four times.

In this article, let’s look at every Purple Cap winner for Chennai Super Kings, their IPL records, and how they contributed to the franchise’s incredible journey.

Dwayne Bravo – Purple Cap Winner IPL 2013 & 2015

In the area of death bowling, one can safely say that Dwayne “Champion” Bravo is almost unbeatable. The West Indian all-rounder was a vital cog in the MS Dhoni wheel, especially in the crunch moments of the game. Bravo first got the Purple Cap in the year 2013, where he took 32 wickets in 18 matches, which was the highest wickets taken by a bowler in a single IPL match then.

He played a significant role in CSK reaching the final that year with his slower balls and accurate yorkers. Unfortunately, CSK could not taste the victory in the final. Even though Bravo had a great season on Bravo’s side, the Mumbai Indians emerged victorious. However, his performance was the sole bright spot for the Chennai Super Kings in the 2013 edition of IPL. 

 However, Bravo again took the Purple Cap in 2015, and with 26 wickets in 17 matches. Once again, his variation bowling, especially in the death overs, came in handy in guiding CSK to another final. However, as was the case in 2013, CSK’s season came to a halt in the final, where they were beaten by Mumbai Indians again. It was, however, impossible to ignore Bravo’s impact with the ball, which made him one of the most valuable bowlers in IPL history. 

Mohit Sharma – 2014

Mohit Sharma, the medium pacer who is as simple and humble as he is good with the ball, was the find of the IPL 2014. Mohit had a reputation for having a deceptive pace and being able to deliver crucial wickets; he won the Purple Cap with 23 wickets in 16 matches. His best was seen during the powerplay, where he used to halt the big overs and thus put CSK in the driver’s seat in the match. 

During Dhoni’s tenure, Mohit was always a reliable bowler, especially in the power play to control the flow of the game. Even though he was not the most economical, he knew how to take wickets at the right time, which made him a valuable asset. In that year, CSK stood third in the points table, but they were eliminated in the playoffs by Kings XI Punjab. Even though the team could not win the championship, Mohit’s growth as a bowler in the IPL was one of the bright spots of the team’s season. 

Imran Tahir – 2019 

With his energetic celebrations, Imran Tahir added plenty of spice to the CSK bowling attack in 2019 while churning out wickets. The South African leg spinner was the star of the tournament and bowled wonderfully well to bag 26 wickets in 17 matches and clinch the Purple Cap. Tahir was never easy to face, especially on slow wickets, thanks to his flight and turn with the googly and sharp spin. 

Tahir was CSK’s most successful bowler in this IPL once again and helped the team reach yet another IPL final by preventing the opposition batters from establishing partnerships. His best came in the playoffs when he was able to take crucial wickets that allowed CSK to proceed to the finals.

But everything was not going well for CSK as they were comprehensively beaten in the final by the Mumbai Indians, which ended what had been a sensational season for them. Despite the mismatches, Tahir was one of the best players of the IPL 2019 season, and his zeal and enthusiasm on the field were inspiring. 

The CSK’s IPL record is not just about their batters; their bowlers have also come up with some match-winning spells. From Bravo’s sensational last-over bowling, Mohit Sharma’s powerplay spell, or Tahir’s spin bowling, these Purple Cap winners have been vital to CSK’s success. 

List of Purple Cap Winners for Chennai Super Kings

CSK Purple Cap Winners: Key Records

  • Chennai Super Kings have produced 4 Purple Cap winners in IPL history.
  • Dwayne Bravo is the only CSK player to win the Purple Cap twice.
  • Bravo’s 32 wickets in IPL 2013 were a record for the highest wickets in an IPL season at that time.
  • Imran Tahir became the oldest player to win the IPL Purple Cap.
  • CSK bowlers have consistently ranked among the IPL’s top wicket-takers throughout the franchise’s history.

Conclusion

The history of Purple Cap winners for Chennai Super Kings reflects the franchise’s tradition of building world-class bowling attacks. Whether it was Dwayne Bravo’s unmatched death bowling, Mohit Sharma’s disciplined pace, or Imran Tahir’s wicket-taking leg-spin, each of these bowlers played a significant role in CSK’s success.

Although not every Purple Cap-winning season ended with an IPL trophy, these exceptional performances helped Chennai Super Kings remain one of the most consistent and feared teams in the tournament. Their contributions continue to inspire future generations of CSK bowlers and remain an important chapter in the franchise’s rich IPL history.

title: Orange Cap Winners for Chennai Super Kings (Updated)
content:
Have you ever wondered if is it more challenging to look for a parking space in Chennai during the peak hours or look to dismiss a CSK batter when he is on song? Although the verdict on that one could still be in the making, there is no denying the fact that once CSK gets into its groove, it is invincible. This is proven by the fact that the list of Orange Cap winners for Chennai Super Kings consists of 3 different batters.

CSK has been one of the most consistent and cool-headed teams in the IPL and is well-known for that. But apart from the yellow shirts and the loud whistle sound, it is the stars of the team that are most of the time the headline.

Cricket lovers always remember the performances of the players who have been honored with the Orange Cap. CSK has had some real batting titans in the form of Matthew Hayden, Michael Hussey, and the current roaring star Ruturaj Gaikwad, who have ignited the IPL.

On that note, let’s take a look at every player that won orange cap for CSK in IPL.

Matthew Hayden – 2009 (12 matches, 572 runs)

The second edition of the IPL took place in South Africa because of the Indian general elections, and Matthew Hayden, the Australian muscleman, showcased his power hitting in batting. The terrifying opener in world cricket continued the same in the IPL 2009 by scoring 572 runs in just.

His fiery starts used to provide CSK with a big edge, more so by laying the foundation for the middle order. His best knock of the season was 89, and he also made five fifties, which helped him emerge as the highest run scorer of the tournament. Eventually winning him the orange cap for Chennai Super Kings.

Despite the extraordinary individual contribution and the Orange Cap win, CSK’s journey in the IPL 2009 was not without its disappointments. The team, which finished third in the playoffs, was knocked out in the semi-finals by the Royal Challengers Bangalore.

However, his 2009 season is still considered one of the best seasons of power batting and match-winning innings by a top-order batsman in the history of IPL. This underscores the unpredictability of the game, which adds an element of excitement and thrill, and the team’s resilience in the face of such unpredictability. This resilience is a testament to the team’s ability to bounce back from setbacks.

Michael Hussey – 2013 (16 matches, 733 runs)

Michael Hussey, also globally and affectionately called ‘Mr. Cricket was at the core of what happened to the Super Kings. During the 2013 edition of IPL, he was in the form of his life, scoring 733 runs in 16 matches with an average of 52. 35, and this got him the Orange Cap.

What made him special was his flexibility in different match conditions. Whether it was while going after the opposition in the initial overs of the innings or while trying to overhaul a target, Hussey was a surety. He made six fifties that season, with his best performance being 95 runs. 

His performance as an opener and the contribution of CSK’s middle order made the team deliver great performances throughout the tournament. Nevertheless, CSK and Hussey‘s fighting spirit could not help them win the trophy that year.

Mumbai Indians defeated them in the final and thus were the first runners-up. However, his consistency and elegance with the bat in 2013 are still fresh in the memories of CSK fans. 

Ruturaj Gaikwad – 2021 (16 matches, 635 runs)

The IPL 2021 season was also very exciting as a young Indian batsman, Ruturaj Gaikwad, came forward and performed very well to bag the Orange cap. Gaikwad played 16 matches and made 635 runs with the help of one century and four half-centuries with an average of 45. 35.

He also had a great season for CSK that year, and the team managed to clinch its fourth IPL title that year. Gaikwad’s ability to stabilize the innings as an opener and his flair for scoring freely were plus points for the team. 

Ruturaj Gaikwad’s IPL 2021 season was marked by his impressive innings of 101 against the Rajasthan Royals, which helped him establish himself as one of the promising talents in Indian cricket. His cool temperament and good shot selection made him unplayable that season, and he was undeterred against both pace and spin.

His alliance with Faf du Plessis in the opening played a major role in giving CSK steady starts, and the two formed a formidable opening duo for the tournament. Their partnership is a testament to the team’s strong bond, and as fate would have it, they both ended as the top two leading run-getters of the tournament, with FAF ending his season 2 runs shy of Gaikwad’s tally. 

CSK’s performance in 2021 was exceptional. Having failed to qualify for the playoffs in the last season, they came back strongly and topped the league stage before defeating Kolkata Knight Riders in the final to clinch their fourth IPL title. Gaikwad’s contribution to CSK, was one of the reasons the team came from the dead to clinch the championship. 

Orange Cap winners for CSK

The Orange Cap is something that goes beyond mere personal glory, as it signifies the role of the player in helping the team win. Some of the players who eyed major contributions to CSK’s journey in the years 2009, 2013, and 2021 include Matthew Hayden, Michael Hussey, and Ruturaj Gaikw.

Hayden and Hussey contributed their bit to take CSK to the playoffs, and even though they couldn’t win the title, Gaikwad’s 2021 season was, therefore, special as he got to lift the IPL trophy.

These players have now become an integral part of IPL and CSK’s history, and their achievements will always motivate the young cricketers. The Whistle Podu Army will always look back at these seasons with a smile on their faces, and these memories will always be a part of CSK’s history.
